EDCS-00380205.translation: Publius Hortorius Scaurus and Caelsius(?), son of Sextus, as IIviri, had this built at public expense by decree of the decurions, and they approved it.
EDCS-00380205.summary: This inscription records a public building project commissioned by Publius Hortorius Scaurus and Caelsius(?), serving as IIviri, funded by the state and approved by the decurions.

EDCS-02900187.translation: Quintus Greius Crocus, one of the VIviri, and his freedwoman Greia Myrtale made this monument while alive for themselves and their family, and for their sister Quintia Anneia Prima, daughter of Quintus and freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-02900187.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Quintus Greius Crocus and his freedwoman Greia Myrtale for themselves and their family, as well as for Quintia Anneia Prima, likely an associate or relative, indicating a social network within Roman society.

EDCS-02900188.translation: To Laetilia, daughter of Lucius, according to her will. From the estate of Paronius Cordus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, in the amount of 6,000 sesterces.
EDCS-02900188.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 6,000 sesterces from the estate of Paronius Cordus to Laetilia, indicating a financial transaction or inheritance.

EDCS-02900189.translation: To the divine shades of Attia Rufina. Tigidius...
EDCS-02900189.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Attia Rufina, initiated by Tigidius, suggesting a relationship between the two individuals.

EDCS-02900191.translation: Publius Oppius, freedman of Caius, the banker
EDCS-02900191.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Oppius as a freedman banker belonging to Caius.

EDCS-03000250.translation: Publius, son of Titus, and Publius, son of Publius Attius, as aediles, had this built.
EDCS-03000250.summary: This inscription records Publius, son of Titus, and Publius Attius, son of Publius, as aediles who commissioned the construction of a monument.

EDCS-03300145.translation: Hortensia Secunda, daughter of Sextus, for herself and for her husband Publius Aninius Sabinus.
EDCS-03300145.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hortensia Secunda and her husband, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-03300146.translation: Hortensia Secunda, daughter of Sextus, for herself and for her husband Publius Aninius Sabinus, son of Publius, of the Maecia tribe. Frontage 14(?) feet.
EDCS-03300146.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hortensia Secunda and her husband, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire, and includes measurements of the funerary plot.

EDCS-03300147.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph possibly commemorating members of the Poppaeus and Pomponia families.

EDCS-03700148.summary: This inscription records Philogenes, son of Avillus.

EDCS-03700165.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Marcius Apollodorus.

EDCS-03700174.summary: This inscription records the name Aulus Sestius Dama.

EDCS-03700177.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Tettius Samia.

EDCS-03700180.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Umbricius.

EDCS-03700183.translation: To Nymphis. Caius Soranus Donatus erected this for Caius Insidius Rufus.
EDCS-03700183.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Caius Soranus Donatus for Caius Insidius Rufus.

EDCS-04900221.translation: On the fourth day before the Ides of April, the burial of Helvia Tertia, who lived with her husband Licinius Honoratus for 42 years, 3 months, and 16 days, and 3 hours, a wife well-deserving. Farewell, faithful ones. Tertia, a faithful maiden, rests in peace with the holy faithful.
EDCS-04900221.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Helvia Tertia, recording her lifespan and relationship with her husband Licinius Honoratus.

EDCS-04900222.translation: Secundus rests here. He lived 50 years. He lived with his wife for 23 years. Buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of Month.
EDCS-04900222.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age and lifespan of Secundus and his wife, along with burial details, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900223.translation: Here rests in peace Usvaldus the presbyter, who lived in this world more than 44 years, buried on the twelfth day before the Kalends of July, in the Valentiinian indiction, during the consulship of.
EDCS-04900223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Usvaldus the presbyter, recording his age and burial date, likely from the 4th century CE given the consular reference.

EDCS-04900227.summary: This is a record of goods, likely for sale or inventory, listing incense and cedar weighing 7 pounds.

EDCS-04900228.translation: Polla. ... weight 3 and a half pounds. 60.
EDCS-04900228.summary: This inscription appears to record the name Polla and a weight measurement of 3.5 pounds, followed by the number 60, possibly related to goods or a transaction.

EDCS-04900229.summary: This is a record of goods, likely for sale or inventory, listing Cascellia Nigra and spikenard weighing 13 pounds.

EDCS-04900230.summary: This inscription seems to record a transaction or debt involving Caius Mutius and Primia, with a monetary value of 120 sesterces.

EDCS-04900232.summary: This is a record of goods or an inventory item, possibly listing a quantity of 8 units associated with Amabilis and Quintus.

EDCS-04900233.translation: Arium, Rium, from Priamus, Demetrius, Priamus.
EDCS-04900233.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a transaction or ownership, featuring Arium, Rium, Priamus, and Demetrius.

EDCS-04900235.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark, identifying Titus Flavius Thraso as the owner or dedicator.

EDCS-05000189.translation: Lucius, son of Caius, twice duovir, had the basilica repaired, plastered, painted, and gilded at his own expense.
EDCS-05000189.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a basilica by a duovir, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200174.text_edition: \n Allidiae Luci libertae Philo Allidi Luci servus viv Princeps Allidi Luci servus et praeterea tres in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XII\n
EDCS-05200174.translation: To Philo, freedman of Lucius, slave of Lucius, and Princeps, slave of Lucius, and furthermore twelve feet in front and twelve feet in the rear.
EDCS-05200174.summary: This inscription seems to record land boundaries or dimensions related to freedmen and slaves, possibly for a burial plot, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200175.text_edition: \n Titus Peturtius Titi filius aevena |(mulieris) liberta Salvilla Titus Peturtius Titi filius Primus I[] in fronte pedes XVI\n
EDCS-05200175.translation: To Titus Peturtius, son of Titus, and Salvilla, freedwoman of a woman (possibly Titus Peturtius' mother), and Titus Peturtius, son of Titus, Primus, and I[---] sixteen feet in front.
EDCS-05200175.summary: This inscription details property dimensions and possibly identifies individuals associated with it, likely related to land ownership or burial, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200177.text_edition: \n coniugi piissimae e pudicissimae maritus Zenofilus! filius Zenofilus! tis fecerunt bixit sic annos XXXV menses VI d[ies ------\n
EDCS-05200177.translation: Her husband Zenofilus, son of Zenofilus, made this for his most pious and most modest wife; she lived for 35 years, 6 months, and [---] days.
EDCS-05200177.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a wife, recording her name, her husband as the dedicator, and her lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200179.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Variae Veritatis Marcus Gavius Firmus |(centurio) legionis I Italicae matri bene merenti\n
EDCS-05200179.translation: To the Divine Shades: Marcus Gavius Firmus, centurion of the First Italian Legion, for his well-deserving mother, Varia Verita.
EDCS-05200179.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a monument to a mother by her son, a centurion, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200180.translation: Pilonicus, the slave of Octavius Lucius, a Praenestine, made this new work, a paving around the crossroads, a covered structure, all completed. Sufrena Pola erected it from her own peculium.
EDCS-05200180.summary: This is a dedication for a public work, possibly a shrine or resting place, constructed by Pilonicus, a slave, and funded by Sufrena Pola.

EDCS-05200181.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or a funerary text, mentioning the names Annius and Iulia, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200182.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marci Pinni Faltoni Marci filii Quirina Valentis equo publico dulcissimae memoriae infanti Adiutor pater\n
EDCS-05200182.translation: To the Divine Shades: Of Marcus Pinnius Falton, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, Valentis, a child, most sweet, whose father Adiutor provided for his equestrian equipment, with the kindest memory.
EDCS-05200182.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant, dedicated by his father, mentioning his tribal affiliation and providing details about his burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200189.text_edition: \n Lucio Hostilio Luci filio Aemilia Tullo filio decurioni Urbe Salvia\n
EDCS-05200189.translation: To Lucius Hostilius, son of Lucius; Aemilia Tullo, daughter of Lucius, decurion, from Urbs Salvia.
EDCS-05200189.summary: This inscription records the names and affiliations of two individuals, possibly related to public office or citizenship, from Urbs Salvia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400260.text_edition: \n Publius Antilius |(mulieris) libertus Diaconus sibi et Laguriae |(mulieris) libertae Trophyme sic beneficio Cai Calvi in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XII\n
EDCS-07400260.translation: Publius Antilius Diaconus, freedman of a woman, for himself and for Trophyme, freedwoman of Laguria, by the gift of Gaius Calvus, twelve feet in front and twelve feet in the rear.
EDCS-07400260.summary: This inscription records land dimensions and beneficiaries of a gift from Caius Calvus, involving freedmen and freedwomen, likely for a burial plot, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300250.text_edition: \n Caio Quintio Montano VIviro Rupilia Iuliana coniugi suo et sibi et \n
EDCS-08300250.translation: Rupilia Iuliana for her husband Gaius Quintius Montanus, VIvir, and for herself.
EDCS-08300250.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a wife for her husband, a VIvir, and for herself, likely for a tomb or a public benefaction, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300252.text_edition: \n Cincia |(mulieris) liberta Hilara fecit Cornuficio Cai liberto Diogeni\n
EDCS-08300252.translation: Hilara, freedwoman of Cincius, made this for Diogenes, freedman of Caius Cornuficius, a freedman.
EDCS-08300252.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for a freedman, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08300253.text_edition: \n Publius Iulius |(mulieris) libertus VIvir et Augustalis Semproni\n
EDCS-08300253.translation: Publius Iulius, freedman of [a woman], a VIvir and Augustalis, for Sempronius.
EDCS-08300253.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sempronius, dedicated by Publius Iulius, a member of the Augustales college and a VIvir, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08300255.text_edition: \n Ossa Titi Saturi Titi filii Velina Celeris\n
EDCS-08300255.translation: The remains of Titus Saturnus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, and Celeris.
EDCS-08300255.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial place of Titus Saturnus and Celeris, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300259.text_edition: \n PO Cai filii Probi Nonia Phoebe filio\n
EDCS-08300259.translation: To Phoebe, daughter of Caius Probus, for her son.
EDCS-08300259.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording a dedication by Phoebe to her son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300262.translation: Lucius Terentius, son of Aulus, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-08300262.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Terentius, son of Aulus, of the Velina tribe, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300264.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quinto Petrusidio Quinti filio Velina Vero vixit annum I mensibus XI diebus XXI Quintus Petrusidius Quinti libertus Aristo pater collegiatus VIvirum Augustalium patronus collegi Geni municipi et Quintus Petrusidius Aristo frater et sibi et Petrusidiae Iphidi posterisque suis et eorum hoc monumentum heredem non sequetur\n
EDCS-08300264.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Petrusidius, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, Vero, lived 1 year, 11 months, and 21 days. Quintus Petrusidius Aristo, freedman of Quintus, his father, a patron of the college of Genii of the municipality and a VIvir Augustalis, and Quintus Petrusidius Aristo, his brother, set up this monument for themselves, their descendants, and their heirs, which shall not pass to their heirs.
EDCS-08300264.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, recording the death of Quintus Petrusidius Vero and establishing a family burial plot with specific inheritance provisions, set up by his father and brother.

EDCS-08300265.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Herennia Luci filia Cervilla uxor vixi annis sic XVIII et diem tricesimum liberis tribus relictis vitam finivi dolens coniux karus ut memoriae posuit hoc vivos sic mihi ut prodesset in suppremis talem titulum consequi Caius Carrenas Verecundus coniugi incomparabili bene merenti\n
EDCS-08300265.translation: To the departed spirits. Herennia Cervilla, daughter of Lucius, his wife, lived 18 years and 30 days, leaving three children, and ended her life in sorrow. Her dear husband, Gaius Carrenas Verecundus, has erected this monument while alive, so that it might benefit me in my last moments, that I might receive such a tombstone, to his incomparable and well-deserving wife.
EDCS-08300265.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, set up by a husband for his deceased wife who died young after having three children.

EDCS-08600149.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucio Petronio Luci filio Velina Sulpiciano Petronia Rufina coniux et Petronius Lanus filius patri karissimo\n
EDCS-08600149.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Petronius Sulpicianus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe. From Petronia Rufina, his wife, and Petronius Lanus, his son, to their dearest father.
EDCS-08600149.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, set up by a wife and son for their deceased husband and father.

EDCS-08900279.text_edition: \n Lucius Arrius Luci libertus Panther Pnae Luci libertae R concubinae Lucio Arrio Luci liberto Felici Lucio Arrio Luci liberto Aucto s Aucti libertus S\n
EDCS-08900279.translation: Lucius Arrius Panther, freedman of Pna, freedwoman of Lucius. For Lucius Arrius Felix, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Arrius Auctus, freedman of Lucius, freedman of Auctus.
EDCS-08900279.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, recording the patronage and familial relationships between freedmen.

EDCS-08900280.text_edition: \n Quinto Munatio Quinti liberto Diphilo patrono Quinto Munatio Quinti liberto Tertio Caeliae |(mulieris) libertae Helpidi coniu(gi) Caelio |(mulieris) liberto Potito VIviro Augustali \n
EDCS-08900280.translation: For Quintus Munatius Diphilus, freedman of Quintus, patron. For Quintus Munatius Tertius, freedman of Quintus. For Helpidia, freedwoman of [a woman], wife. For Potitus, freedman of [a woman], a VIvir Augustalis.
EDCS-08900280.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from the Roman Imperial period, commemorating Quintus Munatius Diphilus, his freedman, his wife, and another freedman who held a municipal office.

EDCS-08900281.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Philematium, a freedwoman, identifying her patroness.

EDCS-08900283.text_edition: \n Caetranius |(mulieris) libertus Dama in fronte pedes XIII in agro pedes XVI\n
EDCS-08900283.translation: Dama, freedman of Caetranius (erected this): 13 feet in front, 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-08900283.summary: This is a boundary inscription, likely for a property, specifying dimensions and belonging to Dama, a freedman.

EDCS-08900284.text_edition: \n Sexti Histimenni in fronte pedes XVI in agro pedes XXXVII\n
EDCS-08900284.translation: Of Sextus Histimenus: 16 feet in front, 37 feet in the field.
EDCS-08900284.summary: This is a boundary inscription, likely for a property, specifying dimensions and belonging to Sextus Histimenus.

EDCS-08900285.text_edition: \n Marcus Aquillius VIvir filio et coniugi libertis\n
EDCS-08900285.translation: Marcus Aquillius, VIvir, for his son and wife, and freedmen.
EDCS-08900285.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or burial arrangement made by Marcus Aquillius, a member of the VIvirate, for his family and freedmen.

EDCS-08900286.text_edition: \n Lucius Toranius Luci libertus Demostenes sibi et Aprodisiae libertae Hilarioni Demetriae libertae Eroniae libertae Liviae\n
EDCS-08900286.translation: Lucius Toranius Demostenes, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for his freedwomen: Aphrodisia, Hilarion, Demetria, and Eronia, and Livia.
EDCS-08900286.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Lucius Toranius Demostenes provides for the burial of himself and several freedwomen and Livia.

EDCS-08900287.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-08900288.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a name or names associated with a monument.

EDCS-08900289.text_edition: \n Publius Aculanus Spinter sibi et utoniae Egloge coniugi merenti\n
EDCS-08900289.translation: Publius Aculanus Spinter, for himself and for Egloge, his deserving wife.
EDCS-08900289.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Publius Aculanus Spinter dedicates a monument to himself and his wife Egloge.

EDCS-08900896.text_edition: \n ius Quinti filius Urvinius Cai filius Caccius Publi filius magistri aaram faciundam coeravere\n
EDCS-08900896.translation: The magistri, [son] of Quintus Urvinius and Caius [son] of Caccius, son of Publius, supervised the making of the altar.
EDCS-08900896.summary: This inscription records the supervision of the construction of an altar by two magistri, identified by their patronymics.

EDCS-09001271.text_edition: \n Titus Sillius Karus vivos sic posuit sibi et Vetiliae Priscae contubernali carissimae et Ianuariae filiae in fronte pedes XX in agro pedes XX qui hoc violarit dabit aerario Faleriensi HS MM\n
EDCS-09001271.translation: Titus Sillius Karus placed this while alive for himself and for his dearest comrade-in-arms Vetilia Prisca, and for his daughter Ianuaria; 20 feet in front, 20 feet in the field; whoever violates this shall pay 2,000 sesterces to the public treasury of Falerii.
EDCS-09001271.summary: This is a funerary inscription and boundary marker, set up by Titus Sillius Karus for himself, his partner Vetilia Prisca, and daughter Ianuaria, with a penalty for desecration, likely from Falerii.

EDCS-09001274.translation: To our Lords, our Emperors Flavius Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, the Pious, Fortunate, and ever-triumphant Augusti, born for the good of the Republic.
EDCS-09001274.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, dating to their joint rule.

EDCS-09001276.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Verecundo Eutichia sic coniugi dulcissimo et fili qui vixit nnos IXX menses V dies IIII bene merenti\n
EDCS-09001276.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Eutichia [sets this up] for Verecundus, her most loving husband, and for her son, who lived 19 years, 5 months, and 4 days, who deserved well.
EDCS-09001276.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife and son for their deceased husband and father, respectively.

EDCS-09001278.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Terentiae Valentillae coniugi sanctissimae et inconparabili sic cum qua vixi nnos XV a virginitate sua sine ulla vile sic Pulfennius Corinthus maritus et fili matri pientissimae posuerunt\n
EDCS-09001278.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pulfennius Corinthus, husband, and [his] son set this up for Terentia Valentilla, [his] most holy and incomparable wife, with whom I lived 15 years from her virginity without any shame, and for [his] mother, most devoted.
EDCS-09001278.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband and son for a wife and mother, emphasizing her purity and the length of their marriage.

EDCS-09300199.text_edition: \n Publio Flavio Publi liberto Rufioni ex testamento et Publio Flavio Publi filio Rufo filio arbitratu Publi Flavi Publi liberti Sodalis\n
EDCS-09300199.translation: For Publius Flavius Rufio, freedman of Publius, by his will, and for Publius Flavius Rufus, son of Publius, by the arbitration of Publius Flavius, freedman of Publius, his associate.
EDCS-09300199.summary: A dedication or funerary arrangement for two individuals named Publius Flavius, related through patronage and sonship.

EDCS-09300887.text_edition: \n Publi Marci Titi filii Fabia XXX Titi Oesieci Luci filii Velina\n
EDCS-09300887.translation: Of Publius, son of Titus, of the Fabian tribe, 30 years old. Of Titus, son of Oesiecus, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-09300887.summary: A fragment of a list of names, possibly from a census record or a dedication with tribal affiliations and ages.

EDCS-09400302.text_edition: \n Coniugis Firminae bono reddito deae Salutis Frontinius Auli libertus Acer haec tibi dona dedit\n
EDCS-09400302.translation: To Firmina, the good wife returned to the goddess Salus, Frontinius Acer, freedman of Aulus, gave these gifts.
EDCS-09400302.summary: A dedication to the goddess Salus and her consort Firmina, by a freedman named Frontinius Acer.

EDCS-09400303.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-09400303.text_edition: \n ni sacerdotis dei Solis patronus collegii fecerunt nam hic filius noster Felix os decessit praedicimus ergo ut si alistris hanc domum nostram aperire\n
EDCS-09400303.translation: [...] of the priest of the god Sol, the patron of the college made [this], for our son Felix died here; we warn, therefore, that if anyone else [...] open our house [...]
EDCS-09400303.summary: A partial inscription concerning a priest of Sol, a college, and a deceased son, possibly with a warning about the property.

EDCS-09400304.text_edition: \n Ossa Cai Isidi Cai liberti Philerotis et Cossutiae Quinti libertae Lepidae\n
EDCS-09400304.translation: The bones of Caius, freedman of Caius, of Isidis Phileros, and of Cossutia Lepida, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-09400304.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial place of two freed individuals, Phileros and Lepida.

EDCS-09400305.text_edition: \n Caio Nonio Cai filio Velina Flacco flamini divi Augusti et divi Iuli et divi Claudi tribuno militum bis legionis V Macedonicae et legionis VII Claudiae piae fidelis praefecto equitum alae I nnum IIviro quinquennali III praefecto Imperatoris Augusti Vespasiani patrono coloniae testamento fieri iussit arbitratu Noni Auli filii He loco dato decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-09400305.translation: For Gaius Nonius Flaccus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, flamen of the divine Augustus, the divine Julius, and the divine Claudius, tribune of the soldiers of the V Macedonica legion and the VII Claudia pia fidelis legion, prefect of the I ala nnum cavalry twice, quinquennial duovir, prefect of the Emperor Augustus Vespasian, patron of the colony, he ordered this to be made in his will, by the arbitration of Nonius Aulus, son of [...], in this place, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09400305.summary: An extensive funerary dedication for Gaius Nonius Flaccus, detailing his numerous prestigious civic and military offices, and establishing his burial place by senatorial decree.

EDCS-09400306.text_edition: \n Quinto Terentio Cai filio Velina Senecioni Fanniano IIviro quinquennali pontifici Augusteo dedicato et epulo dato coloni et incolae\n
EDCS-09400306.translation: For Quintus Terentius Senecio Fannianus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, quinquennial duovir, Augustan pontiff, dedicated and a feast given by the colonists and inhabitants.
EDCS-09400306.summary: A dedication for Quintus Terentius Senecio Fannianus, a local official and priest, by the colonists and inhabitants of the town.

EDCS-09400307.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flaviae Philumene quae vixit nnis XVIII mensibus II diebus XXIII Titus Calestrius Ampliatus et Ulpia Plotina piissimae bene merenti posuerunt\n
EDCS-09400307.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Flavia Philumene, who lived 18 years, 2 months, and 23 days. Titus Calestrius Ampliatus and Ulpia Plotina set this up for [her], most devoted, who deserved well.
EDCS-09400307.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Calestrius Ampliatus and Ulpia Plotina for Flavia Philumene, likely their daughter.

EDCS-09400308.text_edition: \n Auggustis II ddominis nnostris Flavio Valerio Severo et Galerio Valerio Maximino Piis Fe[licibus ------\n
EDCS-09400308.translation: To our Lords II, Flavius Valerius Severus and Galerius Valerius Maximius, the Pious, Fortunate [---]
EDCS-09400308.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicated to the emperors Severus and Maximian during their joint reign, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09400309.translation: Here rests [innoxia?], who lived [one year?]; dedicated under the consulship of Domitius Modestus and Flavius Arontius.
EDCS-09400309.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a person and the consuls, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09400310.translation: To Constantius Maximus, defender of peace, preserver of the Roman Empire, our Lord, the victorious and ever-triumphant Augustus, Pious and Fortunate, born for the good of the Republic, Romulus, a most distinguished man and ex-consul, devoted to his divine majesty, [dedicates this].
EDCS-09400310.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Emperor Constantius II, praising his virtues and power, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09400315.translation: To our Lords, Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, the Pious, Fortunate, and ever-triumphant Augusti, born for the good of the Republic.
EDCS-09400315.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, dating to their joint rule in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-09700124.text_edition: \n Marco Gavio Marci filio Sergia Maximo praefecto praetorio conscripti publice\n
EDCS-09700124.translation: To Marcus Gavius Maximus, son of Marcus, of the Sergia tribe, praetorian prefect, enrolled by public decree.
EDCS-09700124.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Gavius Maximus, a high-ranking official and praetorian prefect, likely erected during his lifetime or posthumously by public subscription.

EDCS-09701354.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Silliae Tertiae Sillia Fortunata filia matri pientissimae\n
EDCS-09701354.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Silla Tertia, her daughter Silla Fortunata, to her most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09701354.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a daughter to her devoted mother, Silla Tertia.

EDCS-10800050.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titi Furi Titi fili Velina Vitalis magistri municipi Furia Paezusa filia patri piissimo et Aemilia T coniugi bene merenti\n
EDCS-10800050.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Titus Furius Vitalis, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, magistrate of the municipality, his daughter Furia Paezusa, to her most dutiful father and to Aemilia T[---], his deserving wife.
EDCS-10800050.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a daughter for her father, who was a magistrate, and also for his wife.

EDCS-10800053.text_edition: \n Sexto Calavio Sexti filio Velina Basso Obulciae Luci filiae Quintae Sextus Calanius Sexti filius Velina Maximus filius posuit in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XII\n
EDCS-10800053.translation: Sextus Calavius Basso, son of Sextus, of the Velina tribe, and Quintus, son of Lucius, of the Obulcia tribe. Sextus Calavius Maximus, son of Sextus, of the Velina tribe, set this up. 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the ground.
EDCS-10800053.summary: This is a funerary dedication by sons for their father, Sextus Calavius Basso, also specifying the dimensions of the plot of land.

EDCS-10800054.translation: To Ennius Clemens, to his excellent brother.
EDCS-10800054.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a sibling to their highly regarded brother.

EDCS-10800055.text_edition: \n Flaviae Luci filiae Silvinae Publius Ve<t=I>tius Polytimus uxori \n
EDCS-10800055.translation: To Flavia Silvina, daughter of Lucius. Publius Vettius Polytimus, to his wife.
EDCS-10800055.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, Flavia Silvina.

EDCS-10800058.text_edition: \n Quintus Mulius Chaerea co et tu\n
EDCS-10800058.translation: Quintus Mulius Chaerea to you also...
EDCS-10800058.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or a funerary marker, mentioning Quintus Mulius Chaerea.

EDCS-10800059.text_edition: \n Tiberio Petronio Tiberi filio Velina bino filio hones[tissimo ------\n
EDCS-10800059.translation: To Tiberius Petronius Bino, son of Tiberius, of the Velina tribe, to his most honorable son [---]
EDCS-10800059.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription honoring Tiberius Petronius Bino, described as a most honorable son.

EDCS-10800060.text_edition: \n Publicia Faventina et Festus pater filiae piissimae\n
EDCS-10800060.translation: Publicia Faventina and Festus, her father, to their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-10800060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father and presumably his wife for their very devoted daughter.

EDCS-10800259.translation: To Marcus Titius, son of Lucius, pontiff, patron of the colony, by public decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10800259.summary: This is a public dedication honoring Marcus Titius, a prominent citizen and patron, likely from a colonial town.

EDCS-10800261.translation: Publius Attius, son of Titus, and Publius Attius, son of Publius, serving as aediles, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10800261.summary: This inscription records a building project commissioned by two individuals identified as aediles, likely responsible for public works.

EDCS-10800262.text_edition: \n Quintus Annius |(mulieris) libertus Acastus VIvir Annia |(mulieris) liberta Cha Quintus Annius Quinti libertus? et ephano\n
EDCS-10800262.translation: Quintus Annius Acastus, freedman of Annia, and Annia Cha, freedwoman of Quintus Annius, and Quintus Annius, freedman of Quintus, and Ephano [---].
EDCS-10800262.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that seems to list several individuals, possibly related to a funerary monument or association, with a VIvir mentioned.

EDCS-10800263.translation: Gaius Ruficanius Severus, son of Gaius, and Lucius Vettenus Atticus, freedman of Lucius, made [this] at their own expense.
EDCS-10800263.summary: This inscription records a private dedication or commission funded by two individuals, one of whom is a freedman.

EDCS-10800264.translation: To Balbus, son of Caius, of the Cornelia tribe.
EDCS-10800264.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary or honorific inscription mentioning Balbus, son of Caius.

EDCS-10800266.text_edition: \n Marc-- Cardan Cardana |(mulieris) liberta P merentibus po et posterisque\n
EDCS-10800266.translation: Marc-- Cardan Cardana, freedwoman of P--, for the deserving and their descendants.
EDCS-10800266.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to be for the benefit of deserving individuals and their descendants, possibly related to a funerary or commemorative purpose.

EDCS-10800268.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for a woman named Fulvia Doxa.

EDCS-10800269.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription that lists several names, making its specific purpose unclear without further context.

EDCS-10800270.text_edition: \n Velina NAIRI testamento Marci Vibi Marci filii V\n
EDCS-10800270.translation: Velina Nairi, by the will of Marcus Vibius, son of Marcus V[---].
EDCS-10800270.summary: This inscription records a bequest or dedication made in a will by Marcus Vibius, concerning Velina Nairi.

EDCS-10800272.text_edition: \n Lucius Oplelius |(mulieris) libertus Carito sibi et Opleliae |(mulieris) libertae Attice in fronte pedes XII in agro pedes XX sibi et suis\n
EDCS-10800272.translation: Lucius Oplelius Carito, freedman of [a woman], for himself and Oplelia Attice, freedwoman of [a woman], in front 12 feet and in the field 20 feet, for himself and his family.
EDCS-10800272.summary: This inscription records the purchase or dedication of land with specific dimensions by Lucius Oplelius Carito for himself and his family, including a freedwoman.

EDCS-10800335.translation: Quintus Camidienus Crates, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-10800335.summary: This is a simple funerary or commemorative inscription for Quintus Camidienus Crates, identified as a freedman.

EDCS-10800337.text_edition: \n ia |(mulieris) liberta Menophila Dorcha onius |(mulieris) libertus Clario vivi fecerunt\n
EDCS-10800337.translation: ia, freedwoman of [a woman], Menophila, Dorcha, onius, freedman of [a woman], Clario, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-10800337.summary: This inscription records a work commissioned by several individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, who made it during their lifetimes.

EDCS-10900143.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintiliae Marci libertae Ampelidis Marcus Quintilius Marci filius Pollia Vibianus coniugi bene merenti fecit loco dato ex decreto tribullium sic tribus Polliae\n
EDCS-10900143.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Quintilius Vibianus, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, erected this for his well-deserving wife Quintilia Ampelidis, freedwoman of Marcus. The site was granted by decree of the tribullii, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-10900143.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintilia Ampelidis, erected by her husband Marcus Quintilius Vibianus, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10900145.text_edition: \n Publius Statius Quinti filius Aniensis Optatus scriba aedilium curulium sexsprimus sic\n
EDCS-10900145.translation: Publius Statius Optatus, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe, chief scribe of the curule aediles.
EDCS-10900145.summary: An inscription recording the official position of Publius Statius Optatus as chief scribe of the curule aediles, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-10900611.translation: The stone worker Aur(elius) Androneikos from Nikaia dedicated this memorial to myself and to my wife Aiboutia Fortunata.
EDCS-10900611.summary: A funerary monument erected by Aur(elius) Androneikos, a stone worker from Nikaia, for himself and his wife, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900614.translation: Here rests Innoxia, who lived one year, [some months, and some days]; dedicated under the consulship of Domitius Modestus and Flavius Arintheus.
EDCS-10900614.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Innoxia and the consuls, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-10900615.translation: Secundus rests here. He lived for 50 years. He lived with his wife for 23 years. Interred on the 12th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-10900615.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Secundus, providing his age at death and marital duration, with a specific burial date.

EDCS-10900616.translation: To the blessed spirit of Flavius Lampas, who lived 11 years and 9 months. Interred on the 17th day before the Kalendas of August.
EDCS-10900616.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Lampas, giving his age at death and burial date.

EDCS-10900617.translation: For himself and his own. Fourth day before the Ides of April, the burial of Helvia Tertia, who lived with her husband Licinius Honoratus for 42 years, 3 months, 16 days, and 3 hours. To his most deserving wife. Farewell, faithful ones. Tertia, truly faithful, rests in peace with the holy faithful. Health. Health.
EDCS-10900617.summary: A funerary epitaph detailing the life and death of Helvia Tertia, providing precise measurements of her lifespan and her relationship with her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900620.translation: To the Divine Shades. Eri[talia?] Thima rests here in peace.
EDCS-10900620.summary: This is a funerary inscription invoking the gods of the underworld for Eri[talia?] Thima.

EDCS-10900622.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae Vulcasiae Uraniae coniugi castissimae omnibus notissimae fama conperta ab origine nativitatis \n
EDCS-10900622.translation: To the good memory of Vulcasia Urania, his most chaste wife, known to all, her reputation established from the beginning of her birth.
EDCS-10900622.summary: A funerary dedication to Vulcasia Urania, praising her chastity and reputation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900623.translation: Estefanus, laid to rest in Christ, rests here, on the 19th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-10900623.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating the burial of Estefanus in Christ on a specific date in November.

EDCS-10900624.summary: An incomplete funerary dedication to Domnus, possibly a son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900630.translation: Stefanus, son of Sarma, rests here; he lived for X years, Y months, and three days. His sons SE...
EDCS-10900630.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and lifespan of Stefanus, son of Sarma, mentioning his sons.

EDCS-10900632.translation: If you happen to ask whose bones are in this tomb, it is Stephanus, lying here, who shone from a noble lineage, the son of the Just, grandson of Hadrian.
EDCS-10900632.summary: This funerary epitaph identifies Stephanus as the deceased, highlighting his noble ancestry from Hadrian.

EDCS-11100460.text_edition: \n Caius Decumius Cai filius Cai nepos duovir honoris decurionum municipumque signum Victoriae sacrum et basim de pequnia sic sua faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11100460.translation: Gaius Decumius, son of Gaius, grandson of Gaius, as duovir, by his authority over the town councillors and citizens, arranged for the statue and base of Victory to be made and dedicated, using his own money.
EDCS-11100460.summary: A dedication of a statue and base of Victory by Gaius Decumius, who held the office of duovir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11100465.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Ampudia Politice, freedwoman of Publius. Ampudia Prisca, freedwoman, [erected this] for her patroness, who deserved well.
EDCS-11100465.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ampudia Politice, erected by her freedwoman Ampudia Prisca, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11100466.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying an individual named Gaius Gavius.

EDCS-11100467.translation: To Gaius O[---]naeus, freedman of Gaius, [---]ol[---], designer.
EDCS-11100467.summary: An incomplete inscription identifying a freedman named Gaius O[---]naeus as a designer, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11100468.translation: Sicin(i)a Piste, freedwoman, for herself and for Decimus Junius Histro, freedman, her husband, and for Agne [her] daughter, and for Agne Sicinia.
EDCS-11100468.summary: A funerary dedication for Sicinia Piste, her husband, daughter, and another Agne, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11600058.translation: To Numisia Secunda Sabina. Claudius Liberalis, priestess of the August Empress, mother of the municipium and colony of Interamna Prauttianorum, set up this statue in honor of her generosity, as the first of all Prauttian women, with money collected by the people; for its dedication, she gave 400 sesterces. (This) place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11600058.summary: This is a statue base erected in honor of Numisia Secunda Sabina by Claudius Liberalis, a priestess, for her generosity towards the people of Interamna, with a donation for the dedication ceremony, dated by the mention of decurions.

EDCS-11600060.translation: To Telonia Atlante. For Lucius Telonius Dicaeus, Augustalis VIvir, and Tibertian. For Telonia Sabina, daughter of Lucius Telonius. For Lucius Telonius Meleager, Augustalis VIvir, and Tibertian, brother.
EDCS-11600060.summary: This is a funerary dedication honoring several members of the Telonia family, including a husband and wife, and their brother, all holding civic and religious offices.

EDCS-13302499.text_edition: \n Quinto Papio Quinti filio Ostleno Celeri tribuno plebis patrono coloniae decreto decurionum publice Petronius Titi filius Rufus IIviri faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-13302499.translation: To Quintus Papius Quintus son Ostlenus Celer, tribune of the plebs and patron of the colony. By decree of the decurions, the duovirs Petronius Rufus, son of Titus, and [ --- ] had this made at public expense.
EDCS-13302499.summary: This is a public monument commissioned by duovirs to honor Quintus Papius Quintus son Ostlenus Celer, a tribune of the plebs and patron of the colony, as decreed by the local council.

EDCS-13302500.text_edition: \n Marco Cassio Cornasidio Sabino egregio viro advocato fisci auditori sacri ad SS CC N advocato fisci stationis heredit[atum ------\n
EDCS-13302500.translation: To Marcus Cassius Cornasidius Sabinus, an outstanding man, advocate of the treasury, auditor of sacred matters, advocate of the treasury of the [ --- ] stationed in the department of inheritances.
EDCS-13302500.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Cassius Cornasidius Sabinus, recognizing his distinguished career as an advocate for the imperial treasury and in matters of inheritance.

EDCS-13302501.text_edition: \n Marco Minicio Titi filio quinquennali iterum a populo praefecto equo publico\n
EDCS-13302501.translation: To Marcus Minicius, son of Titus, quinquennial censor for the second time, prefect, holder of the public horse.
EDCS-13302501.summary: This inscription commemorates Marcus Minicius, son of Titus, who held multiple significant civic offices, including censor and prefect, and was recognized with the public horse.

EDCS-14000159.translation: Publius Salvius made this for his father, Publius Salvius, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, from Asia.
EDCS-14000159.summary: This is a dedication made by Publius Salvius for his father, also named Publius Salvius, indicating his tribal affiliation and origin.

EDCS-14000161.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name of an individual, Stenius Rutilius Somius.

EDCS-14805304.translation: To the departed spirits. To Manlia Maxima, daughter of Gaius, wife of Crispinus, most devoted wife. Sextus Alinnius Festus, primipilaris(?), set this up for her as one who deserved well.
EDCS-14805304.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Sextus Alinnius Festus, a former centurion (primipilaris), for his 'most devoted wife,' Manlia Maxima, honoring her memory.

EDCS-15300618.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Titus Rufrenus Serenus, son of Titus, son of Spurius, who was a VIvir, an aedile, and a duovir, curator of the Ennian funds, made this for himself, for Tertulla his mother, and for his descendants.
EDCS-15300618.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Titus Rufrenus Serenus for himself, his mother, and descendants, detailing his various civic and religious offices.

EDCS-15400508.translation: Aufidena Secunda to Gaius Tullius Fronton, son of Gaius, of the Maecian tribe, quaestor.
EDCS-15400508.summary: This is an epitaph recording Aufidena Secunda's dedication to her husband, Gaius Tullius Fronton, who served as a quaestor.

EDCS-15400509.translation: To Gaius Capivius Vitalis, decurion of the colony of Hadria, aedile, prefect of Castrum Novum, duovir, curator of the calendar of Aveia, prefect for the third time, quinquennial official, curator of public works twice, who lived 52 years, 7 months, and 12 days. Iulia Rufina, his wife, Capiva Vitalis and Vitalis Anpliatus Rufinus, his sons, and his heirs set this up for their most devoted father.
EDCS-15400509.summary: This tombstone commemorates Gaius Capivius Vitalis, a prominent local official in Hadria and other locations, who served in various capacities and lived to the age of 52, erected by his family.

EDCS-15400510.translation: To Gaius Mamilicus Anthus, freedman of a woman, Augustalis, by decree of the decurions, without charge. To Mamilia Grata, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-15400510.summary: This is a funerary monument honoring Gaius Mamilicus Anthus, an Augustalis, and Mamilia Grata, both freedpersons, with the inscription granted free of charge by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-15400511.translation: Sextus Publicius, son of Sextus, of the Maecian tribe, scribe. Publicia Callipolis, freedwoman of Sextus.
EDCS-15400511.summary: This is an epitaph for Sextus Publicius, a scribe of the Maecian tribe, and Publicia Callipolis, his freedwoman.

EDCS-15400512.translation: Sangurius, son of Caius, and Lucius Gargonius, son of Lucius, quaestors, took care to have the shrine enclosed by a fence, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-15400512.summary: This inscription records that two quaestors, Sangurius and Lucius Gargonius, oversaw the fencing of a shrine on the Senate's order.

EDCS-15400513.translation: Venerius Felix, freedman of the colony and Augustalis magistrate, made this for himself, his wife Platorina Aprulla, and his family, while alive. Frontage 30 feet, land 85 feet.
EDCS-15400513.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman and magistrate for himself and his family, indicating property dimensions.

EDCS-15400514.translation: ...enus, son of Lucius, and ...olanus, son of Sextus, gave this work to be done.
EDCS-15400514.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the commission of a work by two individuals, identified by their names and patronymics.

EDCS-15400515.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Atavus Syntrophus, his dearest son, who lived for 3 years, 4 months, and 8 days. Lucius Atavus Syntrophus and Pomponia Liberalis made this.
EDCS-15400515.summary: This is a tombstone for a young child, set up by his parents, Lucius Atavus Syntrophus and Pomponia Liberalis.

EDCS-15400516.translation: Lived / Lucrina, freedwoman of Marcus Disellius, son of Aulus, formerly of Lucrina, [and] of Disellius.
EDCS-15400516.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary notice for Lucrina, a freedwoman, mentioning her former owners.

EDCS-15400517.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely a name panel on a tomb, for Quintus Egnatius.

EDCS-15400518.translation: Lucius Flavius Valens of the Maecian tribe erected this for his sister Tertia, daughter of Lucius. Frontage 15 feet, land 15 feet.
EDCS-15400518.summary: This tombstone was erected by a brother for his sister, specifying property dimensions.

EDCS-15400519.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Publius Naevius Primitivus, father, and Publius Naevius Severus, brother. Quintus Cardenus Priscus and Cardena Saturnina [erected this] for deserving parents.
EDCS-15400519.summary: This funerary dedication is made by children for their deserving parents and brother.

EDCS-15400521.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or tombstone, for Marcus Octavius Gallicanus Malchianus.

EDCS-15400522.translation: Marcus Octavius Philemo, freedman of Marcus. Octavia Dio, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-15400522.summary: This inscription records the names of two freedpersons, Marcus Octavius Philemo and Octavia Dio.

EDCS-15400524.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Parthenophaeus and Eunois, parents, made this for their most beloved daughter Parthenope. She lived 6 years, 4 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-15400524.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating a young girl named Parthenope, erected by her parents.

EDCS-15400525.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Petillius Primigenius, while alive, set this up for himself, for his daughter Petillia Sabina, daughter of Publius, and for his deserving wife Calpurnia Coene.
EDCS-15400525.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Publius Petillius Primigenius for himself, his daughter, and his wife.

EDCS-15400526.translation: From the will of Gaius Petronius Antiochus, freedman of Gaius. For Gaius Petronius Quartio and Grata.
EDCS-15400526.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication made from the will of Gaius Petronius Antiochus for Gaius Petronius Quartio and Grata.

EDCS-15400527.translation: Titus Pomponius Rufus of the Maecian tribe, for himself and his family.
EDCS-15400527.summary: This is a funerary or dedication inscription set up by Titus Pomponius Rufus for himself and his family.

EDCS-15400528.translation: For Pomponia Prisca, daughter of Publius(?), and for himself, Sextus Votienus Etnicus.
EDCS-15400528.summary: This inscription is a dedication likely made by Sextus Votienus Etnicus for Pomponia Prisca and himself.

EDCS-15400530.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. He placed this for his most devoted wife, Successiana, who deserved it, with his own money, and also for himself.
EDCS-15400530.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where a husband dedicates a monument to his devoted wife and also provides for himself.

EDCS-15400531.translation: To Terminia Sabina, daughter of Quintus. Brittia Sabina, her mother, set this up. She lived 26 years. The mother did for her daughter what she had wished to do for her own parent, but premature death prevented it. In front 15 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-15400531.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a mother for her deceased daughter, Terminia Sabina, indicating the plot size.

EDCS-15400533.translation: Lucius Tettius Primus and Gelatia Saturnina.
EDCS-15400533.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph naming two individuals, Lucius Tettius Primus and Gelatia Saturnina.

EDCS-15400534.translation: She made this for her own Anterus and for her son Gaius Vicirius Epafroditus and for her grandson Celer, while she was alive. Why should I recall what you have done, too cruel and unjust? Why do you weep and fall without cause? This boy, still with weak strength, as if he were entering his eighth year, the stars consumed him. Oh envious death, you force us to deceive (you). It would have been fairer for you to do this.
EDCS-15400534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph expressing grief over the death of a young boy named Anterus, commissioned by his mother.

EDCS-15400540.translation: Marcus Avidius, son of Publius, and Gaius Flavonius, son of Caius, as magistrates, took care of the construction of the wall and steps.
EDCS-15400540.summary: This is a public works inscription recording the construction of a wall and steps, undertaken by two magistrates.

EDCS-15400542.translation: Caius Norbanus Mena, freedman of Caius, made this for himself and for his wife, Decimia Dorina, freedwoman of Publius, and for his freedwoman Fusca and his freedman Tertius, while alive.
EDCS-15400542.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Caius Norbanus Mena for himself, his wife, and his freedpersons, indicating it was made during his lifetime.

EDCS-15400543.translation: To Caius Pontedius Tiberius, freedman of Caius. To Caius Pontedius Suavius, freedman of Caius. Stacte, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-15400543.summary: This funerary monument records the dedication to two freedmen, Caius Pontedius Tiberius and Caius Pontedius Suavius, and to Stacte, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-15600695.translation: Caius Septimius Lupus, son of Caius, of the Maecia tribe, and Lattiae, daughter of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-15600695.summary: This inscription lists the names and parentage of a man, Caius Septimius Lupus, and his wife, Lattiae, likely for a tomb.

EDCS-15600696.translation: Quintus Ofillius, son of Caius Rufus, Sextus Calidenus, son of Kaeso, grandson of Quintus, and Titus Temonius, freedman of Titus Flaccus, as magistrates, took care of the construction and painting of the temple of Hercules, as decided by the district, and approved it themselves, under consuls Gnaeus Pompeius and Marcus Licinius, for the second time.
EDCS-15600696.summary: This is a public works inscription detailing the construction and decoration of a temple of Hercules by two magistrates during the consulship of Pompeius and Licinius.

EDCS-15600698.translation: Decimus Fundilius, freedman of Numerius, dedicated this gift to Hercules.
EDCS-15600698.summary: This is a votive inscription where Decimus Fundilius dedicates a gift to Hercules.

EDCS-15600699.translation: Lychinis, priestess of Venus, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-15600699.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Lychinis, a priestess of Venus.

EDCS-15600701.translation: To Publius Caudius, son of Publius.
EDCS-15600701.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription, likely honoring Publius Caudius, son of Publius.

EDCS-15600702.translation: Sextus Egnatius, son of Titus, ordered this to be made by his will, under the supervision of Maxuma, daughter of Titus, of the Carsedia tribe.
EDCS-15600702.summary: This inscription indicates that Sextus Egnatius, son of Titus, established by his will that this monument be erected under the supervision of Maxuma.

EDCS-15600705.translation: Titus Attius Atianus, freedman of Titus, priest of the Mother of the Great Goddesses of the Vestini, from Victoria.
EDCS-15600705.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Attius Atianus as a priest of the Mother of the Great Goddesses and a freedman, possibly indicating his origin or a benefactor.

EDCS-15600707.translation: Aulus Numisius Montanus gave this, as he saw it, to Silvanus.
EDCS-15600707.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Aulus Numisius Montanus to Silvanus, possibly a votive offering.

EDCS-15600708.summary: This inscription identifies Polybius as a secretary for Emperor Augustus, suggesting an official capacity in the imperial administration.

EDCS-15600709.translation: [Caius] Caesius, son of [Caius], of the Velina tribe, trumpeter, ordered this to be made by his will under the supervision of Caius Caesius Phil[---], freedman of Caius. Caius [freedman of Caius?] Ho[---].
EDCS-15600709.summary: This funerary inscription, though fragmentary, indicates that Caius Caesius, a trumpeter of the Velina tribe, arranged for its construction by his will, with mentions of other individuals likely involved.

EDCS-15600710.translation: To Titus Statins Praetuttianus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, prefect of the Second Cohort of Breuci, tribune of the Second Cohort of Spaniards, equipped with cavalry, Roman citizens; his brother Gaius Statius Praetuttianus dedicated this place by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-15600710.summary: Funerary monument for a military officer, Titus Statins Praetuttianus, dedicated by his brother.

EDCS-15600711.translation: Lucius Agusius Mussus, son of Gnaeus, grandson of Lucius, and Gaius Arrenus Rufus, son of Titus, twice members of the board of eight, saw to the rebuilding of the baths by order of the senators.
EDCS-15600711.summary: Record of public works, the rebuilding of baths, undertaken by two officials.

EDCS-15600712.translation: To Attia Maxima, daughter of Publius, priestess of the Augustales; Tiberius Claudius Vitalis dedicated this place to his excellent wife by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-15600712.summary: Funerary monument for Attia Maxima, a priestess, dedicated by her husband.

EDCS-15600713.summary: This is an inscription recording the dedication or construction of seating benches and small shrines by Diphilus.

EDCS-15600714.translation: Eleutherus, freedman of Titus, [---]; Pamphilus, freedman of Titus, Ruc[---], duovir; Licinia Eleutheris, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-15600714.summary: Fragmentary inscription possibly recording the names of freedmen and a duovir, with incomplete details.

EDCS-15600716.translation: Titus Licinius Dem(), freedman of Titus, duovir.
EDCS-15600716.summary: Dedication or record of office for Titus Licinius Dem(), a freedman and duovir.

EDCS-15600717.summary: This inscription records the name and title of Manlius Maltinus, a praetor, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-15600718.translation: Quintus Caius Poppaeus, son of Quintus, patron of the municipality and colony, gives a bath in perpetuity at his own expense to the municipal citizens, colonists, residents, guests, and visitors.
EDCS-15600718.summary: Public benefaction in which Quintus Caius Poppaeus provides a public bath for the citizens and residents of the municipality and colony.

EDCS-15600720.translation: Lucius Tettaienus Barcha, son of Lucius, and Lucius Fistanus, son of Lucius, took charge of constructing a road to the field, with the funds of the associates of the field, by decree of the senators, and approved it themselves. Outside the wall, into the land, on precarious tenure.
EDCS-15600720.summary: Record of public works concerning the construction of a road to a field, financed by associates and approved by officials.

EDCS-15600724.translation: To Publius Salvius Secundus, freedman of Publius, Augustalis; Caesia Coene for his deservingness, and for herself and her descendants, 25 feet in frontage and 10 feet in depth.
EDCS-15600724.summary: Funerary monument or plot dedication for Publius Salvius Secundus, an Augustalis, and his family, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-15600727.translation: Lenus, son of Gaius, freedman, quinquennial.
EDCS-15600727.summary: This inscription likely refers to Lenus, a freedman and quinquennial, possibly holding a local office.

EDCS-15600731.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. To Publius Fructosus, born in the province of Africa, colony of Tapsus, who lived 3 years.
EDCS-15600731.summary: Child's tombstone recording his birth province and short lifespan.

EDCS-15600732.translation: Lucius Ampius Severus, son of Lucius, and Lucius Ampius, son of Lucius, his father, and Publicia Paulla, daughter of Sextus, his mother, ordered this to be made in his will, under the supervision of Erotis, his freedman.
EDCS-15600732.summary: Funerary monument commissioned in a will for Lucius Ampius Severus and his parents, supervised by a freedman.

EDCS-15600734.translation: To Publius Arruntius Nymphaeus, son of Publius, for himself, and for his father Publius Arruntius Nymphio, and for his mother Albia Thespias, and for Quintus Fulvius Ascanus, son of Quintus, and for Arruntia Pyrallidis, and for Gaius Attius Sabinus, and for Gaius Pomponius Thespius, and for their descendants and their descendants. In front 18 feet, in the field 18 feet.
EDCS-15600734.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Publius Arruntius Nymphaeus for himself and his family, specifying the dimensions of his plot of land.

EDCS-15600735.summary: This inscription records the name of Quintus Artorius, son of Quintus, likely a personal dedication or tombstone.

EDCS-15600736.translation: Gaius Aufidenus Philarurus, son of Gaius, freedman; Aufidena, freedwoman of the wife of Aufidius, [daughter] of Erotis.
EDCS-15600736.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication for two individuals, Gaius Aufidenus Philarurus and Aufidena, potentially related through freedman/freedwoman status.

EDCS-15600738.translation: To Nic(...) Bassianus, aged 50. Marcus Servilius [dedicated this] to his father, well-deserving.
EDCS-15600738.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Servilius for his father, Nic(...) Bassianus, who lived to be 50 years old.

EDCS-15600740.translation: Aulus Caesellius, son of Numerius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-15600740.summary: This inscription provides the name and tribal affiliation of Aulus Caesellius, likely for an official record or monument.

EDCS-15600742.translation: Gaius Carfinius Capitio, son of Gaius, grandson of Quintus, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-15600742.summary: This is a standard Roman naming formula, likely an epitaph or a dedication, for Gaius Carfinius Capitio.

EDCS-15600743.summary: This is a very brief epitaph simply stating the name of the deceased, Coelia Pyralis.

EDCS-15600744.translation: Sacred to the divine shades. Flavia Priscilla, daughter, to her most dutiful mother, Cornelia Sulpiciana.
EDCS-15600744.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a daughter, Flavia Priscilla, to her devoted mother, Cornelia Sulpiciana.

EDCS-15600745.translation: Lucius Cuspedius, son of Sextus(?), Granea.
EDCS-15600745.summary: This inscription gives the names Lucius Cuspedius and Granea, possibly related individuals or a dedication.

EDCS-15600746.translation: [...] in the field 16 feet. Egnatius Gemellus, son of Lucius, freedman, lives. [---] to Salvia, freedwoman.
EDCS-15600746.summary: This inscription seems to record land dimensions and mentions Egnatius Gemellus, who is alive, and a freedwoman named Salvia, possibly related to his plot.

EDCS-15600747.translation: To Fabia Fortunata Septimina, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-15600747.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fabia Fortunata Septimina, daughter of Aulus.

EDCS-15600748.translation: To Publius Federus for himself and for his patroness Fadia, and for his mother Famae, and for his wife Feronia, and for his freedman Spurius Federote.
EDCS-15600748.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Publius Federus for himself and his family and freedman, indicating a complex set of relationships including a patroness.

EDCS-15600749.translation: To the divine shades. Publius Fadius Gratus, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, from Interamna, for himself and for Vettia Severa, his most dutiful wife, and for their descendants, freedmen and freedwomen who will be of his name. In the field 40 feet, in front 40 feet.
EDCS-15600749.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Publius Fadius Gratus for himself, his wife, and descendants, specifying plot dimensions and including provisions for future freedmen.

EDCS-15600750.translation: To the divine shades. Lucius Gentius Mansuetus lived 18 years, 5 months, 15 days.
EDCS-15600750.summary: This is a funerary dedication recording the age at death of Lucius Gentius Mansuetus, who lived 18 years, 5 months, and 15 days.

EDCS-15600751.translation: Gaius Licinius Mancia, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-15600751.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Licinius Mancia, likely for an official record or monument.

EDCS-15600752.translation: Lucius Lusius Eros, freedman of Lucius, and Victoria Systasium, freedwoman of Publius, and Hilara.
EDCS-15600752.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lusius Eros, Victoria Systasium, and Hilara.

EDCS-15600754.translation: To Marcia, by the arbitration of Ter...
EDCS-15600754.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcia, made by the arbitration of someone named Ter, possibly related to a legal settlement or will.

EDCS-15600755.translation: To Claudio Amelaeuntius, a patron well deserving.
EDCS-15600755.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudio Amelaeuntius, honoring him as a deserving patron.

EDCS-15600756.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apisia Capriola made this for her husband Publius Petisedius Successus, with whom she lived for 35 years and 5 months, a well-deserving man, and for her sons Petisedius Capriolus and Successus.
EDCS-15600756.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Apisia Capriola for her husband Publius Petisedius Successus and their sons, detailing their marriage length.

EDCS-15600757.translation: Prima Petronia, freedwoman of Publius, Petronia Spectata...
EDCS-15600757.summary: This inscription mentions Prima Petronia, a freedwoman of Publius, and Petronia Spectata, likely a family tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-15600758.summary: This inscription names Philotimus, a freedman of Marcus, and refers to pietas, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-15600759.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Philtal.

EDCS-15600760.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pomponia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-15600761.translation: To Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius Pomponius.
EDCS-15600761.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hilara, a freedwoman.

EDCS-15600762.translation: Marcus Publicius Ph[---] and Corru[---]. Philoxenus, freedman, by will, bequeathed [---]
EDCS-15600762.summary: This inscription records a bequest made in a will by Philoxenus, a freedman, to Marcus Publicius and Corru[---].

EDCS-15600763.translation: Gaius Rufrius, son of Titus, from the Claudia tribe. Utiaca, daughter of Publius, his wife.
EDCS-15600763.summary: This is an epitaph identifying Gaius Rufrius and his wife Utiaca.

EDCS-15600764.translation: Lucius Sentius Mico, freedman of Lucius, the father; Lucius Sentius Faustus, freedman of Lucius, the son; Acusia Tyrannis, freedwoman of Titus, the mother; Lucius Acusius Philologus.
EDCS-15600764.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sentius Faustus, son of Lucius Sentius Mico and Acusia Tyrannis, with an additional mention of Lucius Acusius Philologus.

EDCS-15600766.translation: To Torquata, daughter, who lived 1 year, 10 months, 7 days, a well-deserving [person], made by Crescens, father.
EDCS-15600766.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Torquata and was dedicated by her father, Crescens.

EDCS-15600767.translation: Gaius Tullius, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius. Gaius Tullius, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius. Gaius Tullius, son of Gaius, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-15600767.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary marker or record for multiple individuals named Gaius Tullius, all freedmen.

EDCS-15600768.translation: Gnaeus Varenus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe. Rutila Brutsena, wife of Gaius, daughter of Brutus.
EDCS-15600768.summary: This inscription identifies Gnaeus Varenus and his wife Rutila Brutsena.

EDCS-15600769.translation: [---] Secundus, slave of Vergiliae, lived 22 years.
EDCS-15600769.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundus, a slave who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-15600770.translation: Rogata, daughter of Publius, named Procula, took care to have this made for her son Gaius Vettius Laetus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, and for his mother Vitellia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, by will.
EDCS-15600770.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Rogata Procula for her son Gaius Vettius Laetus and his mother Vitellia Tertia, indicating it was specified in a will.

EDCS-15600771.translation: Publius Vibius Philotimus, freedman of Titus. Coxso.
EDCS-15600771.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Vibius Philotimus and Coxso.

EDCS-15600772.translation: Lucius Vifius Ocella, son of Caius.
EDCS-15600772.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Vifius Ocella, identified by his father and tribe.

EDCS-15600773.translation: To Ulpius Septimius Iulius Felicianus, the most innocent boy, who lived 3 years and 5 months.
EDCS-15600773.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Ulpius Septimius Iulius Felicianus, with his age at death partially restored.

EDCS-15600774.translation: Volia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius. (with a correction note for Maxuma).
EDCS-15600774.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Volia Maxuma, identified by her father and tribe.

EDCS-15600781.translation: For Sextus Pompeius Laenas, son of Sextus, of the Sabatina tribe, and for Pompeia Anthusa, freedwoman of Sextus, and for Sextus Pergamos, freedman of Sextus. Vetiedia Donata, freedwoman of Quintus, his concubine, [made this] for herself and her kin. In front 18 feet, in depth 20 feet.
EDCS-15600781.summary: This is a funerary dedication for multiple individuals, including a family and a concubine, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-15600782.translation: Aiedia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, for herself and for her father Lucius Aiedius, son of Marcus, and for Novernia Mater, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-15600782.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a woman named Aiedia Tertia, for herself and her parents.

EDCS-15600783.translation: Sextus Albanius Maximus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-15600783.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Sextus Albanius Maximus.

EDCS-15600784.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Dentria, my mother; for Aulus Livius Decembrius, freedman; for Dentria Nacta, his wife; for Aulus Livius Dentrius Romanus, brother, citizen; for Amanda, freedwoman. [They] lived 20 years. These two, bound by an agreement, having followed the same fate, placed together on the same bed, lie in the same ashes. Aulus Livius Bassus [dedicated this] for the deserving.
EDCS-15600784.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Aulus Livius Bassus to his mother, his freedman, his wife, his brother, and a freedwoman, with poetic lines describing their shared fate.

EDCS-15600785.translation: Lucius Ferontios, freedman of Lucius, Salvios. Quintus Veidios, freedman of Quintus, Philositos.
EDCS-15600785.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Lucius Ferontios and Quintus Veidios, likely freedmen, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-15600788.translation: The public revenue of the Interamnians from the baths.
EDCS-15600788.summary: This inscription records a public tax or revenue related to the baths in Interamna.

EDCS-15600789.translation: Marcus Petulcius, son of Marcus, and Lucius Satrius, son of Lucius, as praetors, took care to have this made by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-15600789.summary: This inscription records that two individuals, Marcus Petulcius and Lucius Satrius, acting as praetors, commissioned this work by senatorial decree.

EDCS-15600790.translation: To Gaius Vettius, prefect of the pagus of the Albenses and Fucentii, who lived 32 years, 5 months, 10 days. Babiena Bardalis made [this] for her incomparable husband.
EDCS-15600790.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Babiena Bardalis to her husband, Gaius Vettius, who was a prefect of a local administrative district.

EDCS-15600792.translation: Arrediana Chrestilla, for reasons of piety, in the same consulship. Pulcher, the best.
EDCS-15600792.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly funerary, by Arrediana Chrestilla, mentioning piety and possibly a magistrate named Pulcher.

EDCS-15600793.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a beloved son.

EDCS-15600794.translation: Lucius(?) Lartius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe.
EDCS-15600794.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lartius Rufus, identified by his father and tribe, with some parts restored.

EDCS-15600795.summary: This is a funerary dedication or identification for Lucius Septimius Praeco.

EDCS-15600797.translation: Lucius Vettius Menophilus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Vettius Crinus, freedman of Lucius. Vettia Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius. Vettia Ge, freedwoman of Lucius. In the field 16 feet, in front 18 feet.
EDCS-15600797.summary: This is a funerary inscription for multiple freedmen and freedwomen of Lucius Vettius, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-15600798.translation: Publius Vibius Donatus, freedman of Publius, alive, made [this] for himself and for Publius Vibius Gemellus, freedman of Publius, and for Gemella, his sister, and for Aninia Protogenia, freedwoman of Caius, and for Herennia Protogenia, twin sister.
EDCS-15600798.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Publius Vibius Donatus for himself and his family, including his freedman, his sister, and another woman and her twin sister.

EDCS-15600800.translation: Quintus Eppius, son of Publius, of the Maecia tribe, sexvir.
EDCS-15600800.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Eppius, a member of the Maecia tribe and a sexvir.

EDCS-15600801.translation: To Mestrius, son of Caius, of the Maecia tribe, VIvir of Hadria, to his father Caius Mestrius, son of Caius, of the Maecia tribe, to his mother Festimia, and to his brother Maximus, to Hilara his freedwoman, to Principes his freedman.
EDCS-15600801.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Mestrius for his father, mother, brother, and freedmen.

EDCS-15600805.translation: Avillia Hilara, freedwoman of Quintus Avillius, and Avillia Appia, freedwoman of Quintus Avillius, to their father. In front, 12 feet of land, 12 feet.
EDCS-15600805.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication for a father, specifying land dimensions for the tomb or plot.

EDCS-15600806.translation: Publius Egnatius, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-15600806.summary: This inscription identifies Publius Egnatius, son of Publius, belonging to the Velina tribe.

EDCS-15600807.summary: This is a funerary dedication or identification for Flavius Atticus.

EDCS-15600808.translation: Lucius Frus made this place for himself, 10 feet in every direction, while alive.
EDCS-15600808.summary: This inscription records Lucius Frus commissioning a tomb or plot for himself during his lifetime, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-15600809.translation: Luccia, mother, made [this] and for Luccia, daughter of Spurius, her daughter.
EDCS-15600809.summary: This funerary inscription records Luccia dedicating a monument to her daughter, Luccia.

EDCS-15600810.translation: Lucius Modiarius, freedman of Lucius; Hera; Nevia, freedwoman of Publius; Crysarium.
EDCS-15600810.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, possibly marking graves or belonging to a funerary context.

EDCS-15600811.translation: To the departed spirits. [The parents, mindful of whose] piety and sweetness, [will remember] Publicus Augustalis, son of [---], as long as they live, until the time of Julius.
EDCS-15600811.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the departed spirit of Publicus Augustalis, praising his virtues and mentioning his parents' enduring memory.

EDCS-15600812.translation: To Gnaeus Septimius Olycon, freedman of Gnaeus. Gnaeus Septimius Agatho, freedman of Gnaeus, made this for his patron and for himself.
EDCS-15600812.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a freedman to his patron and himself, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-15600813.translation: Tertia Turpedia, according to the will of Lucius Betuvius, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, her son.
EDCS-15600813.summary: A funerary dedication made by Tertia Turpedia in accordance with the will of her deceased son, Lucius Betuvius.

EDCS-15600814.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Quintus Umbricius and his father, Quintus.

EDCS-15600821.translation: To Fortuna Redux. Rufus, the paymaster of the city's treasury, adorned with every care, erected this at his own expense. He also, by decree of the council, undertook the completion of the temple from the ground up at his own great expense, at whose dedication he gave 20,000 sesterces to each member of the college. Dedicated on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, when Orfitus and Maximus were consuls. Whoever wishes to set up a shield will pay 2,000 sesterces to the treasury.
EDCS-15600821.summary: A dedication to Fortuna Redux by Rufus, a city official, who paid for the adornment of a temple and funded a distribution of money upon its dedication.

EDCS-15600823.translation: To Isis Victrix and Juno. Valeria Citheris, freedwoman of Marcus, arranged for the circuit to be made, at her own expense, as a result of a vision.
EDCS-15600823.summary: A votive offering to Isis Victrix and Juno, commissioned by Valeria Citheris, a freedwoman, in fulfillment of a vision.

EDCS-15600829.translation: To Allidius, son of Marcus, of the Velina tribe, military tribune. Marcus Allenidius, of the Velina tribe, centurion. From Castro Truentino. His daughter, [name illegible], daughter of Titus, made this for her sons while alive.
EDCS-15600829.summary: A funerary monument set up by a mother for her sons, possibly indicating a military family background.

EDCS-15600831.translation: Titus Didius, [name illegible], Valeria [name illegible], from C...
EDCS-15600831.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely funerary, mentioning Titus Didius and Valeria.

EDCS-15600833.translation: To Quintus Iunius Severianus, son of Quintus, of the Oufentina tribe, a veteran of our Emperor, who received an honorable discharge, quaestor of the public treasury of Asculum, patron of the guilds of fullers and tree-bearers of Tibur. Mansueta, his freedwoman, gave this statue to her excellent patron, on whose dedication she also gave a banquet, distributing 8 denarii to each of the council members and 2000 sesterces to each of the populace. A site was granted by decree of the council members.
EDCS-15600833.summary: This is a funerary inscription and dedication honoring Quintus Iunius Severianus, a veteran and local official, detailing his benefactions to the community of Asculum and Tibur.

EDCS-15600834.translation: Mu[name illegible] Repentina. Quintus Petronius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Cominia tribe, six-time official, clerk, quinquennial magistrate. Caius Tampius, client.
EDCS-15600834.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Quintus Petronius Rufus, who held several civic and religious offices, and mentioning his client Caius Tampius.

EDCS-15600835.translation: Titus Satanus Sabinus, son of Titus, twice chief magistrate, and twice chief magistrate. Caius A() P() P(), prefect of artisans.
EDCS-15600835.summary: A funerary inscription recording the magistracies held by Titus Satanus Sabinus and Caius A() P() P().

EDCS-15600836.translation: Felix, freedman of Publius Tebeianus, freedman of the woman, one of the six priests of Augustus. (In honor of) Num Sal (or Salus?).
EDCS-15600836.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Felix, a freedman and a member of the college of six priests of Augustus.

EDCS-15600837.translation: Lives Caius Tettaeus Antipho, freedman of Caius, a six-time official, for his wife Lusia. Caius Tettaeus Amans, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-15600837.summary: A funerary monument set up by a freedman, Caius Tettaeus Amans, for his wife Lusia and mentioning his own status as a six-time official.

EDCS-15600838.translation: To Titus Vettius Sallen[t]inus, son of Lucius, duovir. [---] Vettius, son of Titus. [---] no. [---] VII. [---] da. [---] ND. [---]
EDCS-15600838.summary: This inscription appears to be a public dedication or a funerary epitaph for Titus Vettius Sallen[t]inus, a duovir, with further names and details heavily reconstructed.

EDCS-15600841.translation: [...] to Vesta, daughter of Caius, Celerina, and from her own property, the temple, portico, and guardhouse.
EDCS-15600841.summary: This inscription appears to record a dedication of a temple, portico, and guardhouse to the goddess Vesta, possibly by Celerina, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-15600845.translation: Aelia Tertulla, daughter of Lucius, for herself and her family. Considia Rufa, daughter of Lucius. For Marcus Valerius Melantho, freedman of Marcus. 15 feet at the front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-15600845.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a land measurement, recording Aelia Tertulla and Considia Rufa dedicating the plot for themselves and their families, including Marcus Valerius Melantho.

EDCS-15700203.translation: Titus Alfius Chresimus, freedman of Titus. Valeria [---] luch[---]
EDCS-15700203.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription likely for Titus Alfius Chresimus, a freedman, with additional incomplete names.

EDCS-15700204.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Alinia Procula, freedwoman of Sextus, to Gaius Nonius Festus, his most beloved and devoted wife.
EDCS-15700204.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Gaius Nonius Festus to his cherished wife, Alinia Procula.
