EDCS-15700206.translation: Aulus Allidius Lucrio, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe. Aulus Allidius Lucrio, freedman of Aulus. Allidia Hilara, freedwoman of Aulus. Aulus Allidius Philotimus, freedman of Aulus. Aulus Allidius Lucrio, freedman of Aulus, while living, for himself and [---]
EDCS-15700206.summary: This funerary inscription records multiple members of the Allidius family, including freedmen, dedicating a burial plot for themselves while alive.

EDCS-15700207.translation: Titus Aufidius Hilarus. Titus Aufidius Dida. Titus Aufidius Pothus. Anteia Samera. Anteia Cilissa. Aufidia Citheris made this. 16 feet in the field.
EDCS-15700207.summary: This funerary inscription records several individuals, likely family members named Aufidius and Anteia, who commissioned the monument and specifies the land size.

EDCS-15700208.translation: Of Marcus Caepio Novellus, son of Titus. [---]
EDCS-15700208.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that likely refers to Marcus Caepio Novellus, son of Titus, possibly in a public or funerary context.

EDCS-15700209.translation: Publius Antiochus, freedman of Publius. Publius, freedman of Publius Apo[---] lived. 10 feet at the front. [---]
EDCS-15700209.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription for Publius Antiochus, a freedman, and another freedman named Publius, specifying the frontage of the plot.

EDCS-15700210.translation: Samus, son of Titus, lived 16 years. This was made in Campania.
EDCS-15700210.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Samus, son of Titus, stating his age at death and place of origin or creation.

EDCS-15700211.translation: Lucius Acutius, freedman of Lucius. Cennia Amonia, freedwoman of a woman. Cennia Horania, freedwoman of Titus. Made for themselves and their families.
EDCS-15700211.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Acutius, Cennia Amonia, and Cennia Horania, all freedpersons, who commissioned a burial plot for themselves and their families.

EDCS-15700212.translation: [---] LV. [---] Mag[---], son of Titus Cluvius. [---]
EDCS-15700212.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription that mentions Cluvius Mag[---], son of Titus, with the beginning of the text being illegible.

EDCS-15700213.translation: To [3]rnelius [3] Primus [3]dia, freedwoman of Quintus, [3]cunda, lived 25 years. In front 20 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-15700213.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedwoman, likely marking a plot of land with specific dimensions for burial.

EDCS-15700214.translation: The bones of Nigra, of the Fabia tribe, daughter of Publius Dianus, son of Publius.
EDCS-15700214.summary: This inscription records the location of the remains of Nigra, identified by her father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-15700215.translation: Urnia, daughter of Titus Didiu, son of Titus.
EDCS-15700215.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Urnia, daughter of Titus Didiu, son of Titus.

EDCS-15700217.translation: Titus Helvius Teucer, freedman of Titus, in front 15 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-15700217.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot or tomb with land dimensions and identifies the owner as Titus Helvius Teucer.

EDCS-15700218.translation: Titus Helvius Teucer, freedman of Titus, in front 15 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-15700218.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot or tomb with land dimensions and identifies the owner as Titus Helvius Teucer, similar to EDCS-15700217.

EDCS-15700219.translation: Live on: Publius Fadius Philomusus, freedman of Publius, and Orcia Niu[...].
EDCS-15700219.summary: This is a funerary inscription that names two individuals, possibly a couple, and indicates they are alive (or remembered as living).

EDCS-15700220.translation: To Lucius Gavius Crescens the younger, for his well-deserving wife Procula, daughter of Caius, and for himself and his descendants. In front 25 feet.
EDCS-15700220.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Gavius Crescens the younger to his wife Procula and for himself and his descendants, specifying front plot dimensions.

EDCS-15700221.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Gaius Iulius Pamphilus, husband, and Gaius Iulius Elpid[...].
EDCS-15700221.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld spirits for Gaius Iulius Pamphilus and another Gaius Iulius, likely family members.

EDCS-15700222.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lusia, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-15700223.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication, possibly for Aulus Marcius Lucrio and Marcia, though it is heavily damaged.

EDCS-15700224.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to definitively identify its purpose but likely records names associated with a monument or burial.

EDCS-15700225.translation: Publius Mun, freedman of Publius Mun, Phil Mun Cre.
EDCS-15700225.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Mun, a freedman, also mentioning Phil Mun Cre.

EDCS-15700226.translation: [restored] Ocbrotsini, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, and to his wife Flacca, daughter of Lucius, of the Calpurnia [tribe].
EDCS-15700226.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring a man (Ocbrotsini) and his wife (Flacca), providing paternal and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-15700227.translation: Titus Titi libertus Surus; Titus Titi libertus Laumedo; Titus Titi libertus Speratus; Titus Titi libertus Princeps; Titi liberta Rufa.
EDCS-15700227.summary: This inscription lists several freedmen and a freedwoman, all associated with a Titus, likely their former master.

EDCS-15700228.translation: Lives Gaius Pedienus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, in the field 20 feet, in front 20 feet. Lives Gaius Pedienus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, in the field 20 feet, in front 20 feet.
EDCS-15700228.summary: This inscription seems to record the dimensions of a property, possibly a tomb, belonging to Gaius Pedienus, and is repeated perhaps for emphasis or due to a textual error.

EDCS-15700229.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Gaius Petronius Etruscus.

EDCS-15700230.translation: Phaedra, mother, lived 10 years, from her own property.
EDCS-15700230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Phaedra, a mother, stating her age at death and that the monument was funded by her own property.

EDCS-15700231.translation: To the gods of the departed. Philosterus and Successa erected this for Crescentia and Primigenius, their mother and grandmother, who deserved well, and for themselves, with the permission of Enia Ephina, a boundary of thirty feet in all directions.
EDCS-15700231.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Philosterus and Successa for their mother and grandmother, establishing a burial plot of a specific size.

EDCS-15700232.translation: Publius Aeritius Philostratus and Tiberius Eleuther, Cleopatra, in front 17 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-15700232.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a burial plot, naming Publius Aeritius Philostratus, Tiberius Eleuther, and Cleopatra as the owners or dedicators.

EDCS-15700233.translation: Lucius Pituanius Epigonus, father, [for] Pituania, daughter of Lucius, [named] Glaphyra.
EDCS-15700233.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Lucius Pituanius Epigonus for his daughter, Pituania Glaphyra.

EDCS-15700234.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Pomponia Euposia.

EDCS-15700235.translation: To Pontia Callista, freedwoman of a woman, concubine. To Titus Avi[---], freedman of Titus, Phal[---], *sexvir* [---].
EDCS-15700235.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pontia Callista and Titus Avi[---], likely a couple, with a mention of a *sexvir* role.

EDCS-15700236.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Pontulenus Rufus, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-15700237.translation: Lucius? Post[---], freedman? of Lucius?, Philo? Prot[---]
EDCS-15700237.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, naming individuals with uncertain relationships and names.

EDCS-15700238.translation: To Spinther, to Atheneis, freedwoman of Sabidius, to Felicula, to Vibius Primigenia. Decimus Sabidius Primigenius dedicated this.
EDCS-15700238.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including Atheneis, freedwoman of Sabidius, and is dedicated by Decimus Sabidius Primigenius.

EDCS-15700239.translation: To Quintus Salius Blesamus, freedman of Quintus Publilius. To Salia Storge, freedwoman of Quintus Publilius.
EDCS-15700239.summary: This inscription is a joint dedication to Quintus Salius Blesamus and Salia Storge, both freedmen of Quintus Publilius.

EDCS-15700240.translation: Titus Satanius Amelintus, freedman of Titus, lived 35 years.
EDCS-15700240.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, paternity, freedman status, and lifespan of Titus Satanius Amelintus.

EDCS-15700241.translation: Lives Gaius Satanus Matogenes, freedman of Gaius, in front 10 feet, in the field 10 feet.
EDCS-15700241.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or tomb dimensions for Gaius Satanus Matogenes, a freedman.

EDCS-15700242.translation: I, Clematis, freedwoman of Titus Satrius. Ratia, freedwoman of Titus Satrius, wife. Titus Satrius, freedman of a woman, Modestus. In front, [X] feet.
EDCS-15700242.summary: This inscription likely marks the boundaries of a property, mentioning Titus Satrius, his freedwoman Clematis, and his wife Ratia.

EDCS-15700243.translation: Lucius Saturius Clemens. To Chiae, freedwoman of Lucius Saturius. Daughter of Staphinus. She lived 26 years.
EDCS-15700243.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Chiae, daughter of Staphinus and freedwoman of Lucius Saturius, who died at age 26.

EDCS-15700244.translation: Lucius Ianuarius, freedman of Lucius Saturus, in front 20 feet.
EDCS-15700244.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a property or tomb belonging to Lucius Ianuarius, a freedman.

EDCS-15700245.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Saturius Sic[---]us, Att[---]us, to Saturnia, [daughter] of Caius Saturius, and to Erhennia. Caius Saturius Picens [dedicated this].
EDCS-15700245.summary: A funerary inscription for multiple individuals, dedicated by Caius Saturius Picens, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700246.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name Lucius Sau--- Rufus, likely a personal dedication or epitaph from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700247.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for Spetinia Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700248.translation: [---]videnus, [---] Statius, freedwoman of [---]ntia, freedwoman of [---]ntia Phil[---], freedwoman of [---]L T[---]tia, [---] Cleopatra, [---]tia, [---] Artia [---].
EDCS-15700248.summary: A heavily damaged inscription listing several names, some of whom are identified as freedwomen, likely a collective funerary monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700249.translation: Stritia Primilla, daughter of Titus, [dedicated this] for Gnaeus Cornelius Iustus, her husband, and for her sons Gnaeus Cornelius Legitimus and Gnaeus Cornelius Iustus, and for their descendants.
EDCS-15700249.summary: A funerary dedication by Stritia Primilla for her husband and two sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700250.translation: [---] Suriscus, freedman of Caius [---], [---]ius, freedman of a woman, [---]ius.
EDCS-15700250.summary: A fragmentary inscription listing at least three individuals, two of whom are identified as freedmen, possibly part of a funerary context from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700251.translation: To Martialis. To Telonia Prima. To Telonia Ampliata. To Lucius Telonius Clemens.
EDCS-15700251.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members or beneficiaries, with the gentile name Telonius.

EDCS-15700253.translation: [---]rius, freedman of Caius, Thales Luper, according to the will, by the judgment of Hilarius, freedman. Martin Longob[---]
EDCS-15700253.summary: This fragmented inscription details the execution of a will, mentioning a freedman named Thales Luper and the executor Hilarius.

EDCS-15700254.translation: To Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius Titus.
EDCS-15700254.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius Titus.

EDCS-15800508.translation: Marcus Valerius Pietas, freedman of Marcus. For himself.
EDCS-15800508.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Marcus Valerius Pietas, freedman of Marcus, for himself.

EDCS-15800510.text_edition: \n Locus Titi Ventedi Cai filii Afri pedes quadrati XX\n
EDCS-15800510.translation: The area belonging to Titus Ventedius, son of Caius, Africanus, twenty square feet.
EDCS-15800510.summary: A property marker recording the size of an area belonging to Titus Ventedius Africanus, son of Caius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15800511.translation: Arescusa, freedwoman of Publius Ventidius, [dedicates this] in front for 20 feet and in the field for [---] feet.
EDCS-15800511.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land dedicated by Ventidia Arescusa, a freedwoman.

EDCS-15800513.translation: They live. For Caius Vibius Balbus, son of Caius Vibius Petronis, for himself and his concubine or wife, and for the freedman Amphionis, freedman of Titus Lorenz, son of Titus, and moreover for one person in front, twenty feet [long].
EDCS-15800513.summary: A funerary or property inscription specifying dimensions and naming individuals, including a freedman and a concubine/wife, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15800514.translation: Died. Vicrena Antigona, freedwoman of Caius, [with space for her] descendants. Twenty feet in front, twenty feet in the ground.
EDCS-15800514.summary: An epitaph for Vicrena Antigona, freedwoman of Caius, specifying plot dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15800517.translation: To the veins [of the body] of a freedwoman, to her sister.
EDCS-15800517.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the veins of a freedwoman, possibly a medical or funerary dedication.

EDCS-15800526.translation: [---] made while living. Laria Egelana, daughter of Titus [---], P(ublius?) daughter.
EDCS-15800526.summary: A fragmented inscription recording a dedication made during the lifetime of the dedicator(s), possibly Laria Egelana and another woman, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15800527.translation: Fabius, son of Quintus, husband of Offa P[---].
EDCS-15800527.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription identifying Fabius, son of Quintus, and his wife Offa.

EDCS-15800532.translation: To Lucius Afranius, son of Aulus, consul, and to the scribes and colonists of the colony of Vallis.
EDCS-15800532.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Afranius, a consul, and the civic body of the colony of Vallis.

EDCS-15800533.translation: Gaius Marcilius Eros, a purple-dyer, one of the six officials of Truentum.
EDCS-15800533.summary: This is an epitaph identifying a purple-dyer and a member of the vigintivirate in Truentum.

EDCS-15800534.translation: Publius Pantilius Auctus, freedman of Publius, a Six-member of the Augustales, for himself and his family.
EDCS-15800534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Pantilius Auctus, a freedman and a member of the collegium of Augustales, dedicating the plot for himself and his family.

EDCS-15800535.translation: Titus Sentius Men(---), scribe, one of the six officials, and Gargonia Alete, his wife, and Titus Sentius Chresimus.
EDCS-15800535.summary: This epitaph records Titus Sentius Men, a scribe and vigintivir, his wife Gargonia Alete, and Titus Sentius Chresimus.

EDCS-15800536.translation: Publius Buxurius, son of Publius, from Truentum, rests here; his name is Tracalo. May you fare well, skilled in the arts of architecture.
EDCS-15800536.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Buxurius (also known as Tracalo), identified as being from Truentum and skilled in architecture.

EDCS-15800537.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Argenus, slave of Perseus of Caius Ancharus, [erected this] for his well-deserving fellow freedwoman, Successa, freedwoman of Caius Ancharus.
EDCS-15800537.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Argenus, a slave, to his fellow freedwoman Successa, for whom he has set up a monument.

EDCS-15800538.translation: Isutia Theumas, daughter of Isutia, erected [this] for her freedwoman mother, Optata.
EDCS-15800538.summary: This funerary inscription records that Isutia Theumas dedicated a monument to her freedwoman mother, Optata.

EDCS-15800539.translation: Publius Statius, son of Se, erected [this] for his mother, Iulia Ampliata.
EDCS-15800539.summary: This funerary inscription records that Publius Statius dedicated a monument to his mother, Iulia Ampliata.

EDCS-15800540.translation: Suetia, daughter of Gaius, wife of Publius Audienus Capitolinus, son of Quintus, of the Fabian tribe. In front 13 feet, on the side 13 feet.
EDCS-15800540.summary: This is a funerary or property boundary inscription for Suetia, dedicating a plot of land measuring 13 by 13 feet to her husband Publius Audienus Capitolinus.

EDCS-15800549.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Traiani Parthici filius divi Nervae nepos Traianus Hadrianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XI consul III munificentia sua templum Deae Cuprae restituit\n
EDCS-15800549.translation: Emperor Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 11th time, consul for the 3rd time, restored the temple of the goddess Cupra through his munificence.
EDCS-15800549.summary: This imperial dedication records Emperor Hadrian restoring the temple of the goddess Cupra, with dates inferable from his tribunician power and consulships.

EDCS-15800550.translation: Veidia Auge, freedwoman of Titus, and Iulia Urbana, freedwoman of Gaius, officials of Venus, have given.
EDCS-15800550.summary: This inscription records two women, Veidia Auge and Iulia Urbana, freedwomen and officials of the cult of Venus, making a dedication.

EDCS-15800555.translation: To Castorius, my dearest husband, who lived 35 years, 8 months, and 15 days, who departed on the third day before the Ides of December and was buried on the Ides of December, during the consulship of our lords Arcadius and Bauto. [Erected by his wife] of Mira's piety, wisdom, and innocence, the vicarius of the whole of Sicily, of Africa, to his most beloved husband.
EDCS-15800555.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Castorius, husband of a vicarius of Sicily and Africa, providing details of his life and death during the consulship of Arcadius and Bauto.

EDCS-15900590.translation: Lucius Caecilius Proculus and Lucius Caecilius Cinnamus, father, with his own money, on account of this, was granted Augustality and the office of vigintivir by decree of the decurions, free of charge, in memory of [[TIGIAE]].
EDCS-15900590.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caecilius Proculus and his father Lucius Caecilius Cinnamus being granted the offices of Augustalis and vigintivir by decree of the decurions at their own expense.

EDCS-15900591.translation: Lucius? Ofa[--] Auct[--] Aug[--] made it (?).
EDCS-15900591.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the maker of an object, possibly dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-15900592.translation: Procilla, mother, [dedicated this] to Lucius Publicius Consultinus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, who held public equestrian rank and was a selected judge of the Decursi, [this was erected] five [years ago?].
EDCS-15900592.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother, Procilla, to her son Lucius Publicius Consultinus, who held equestrian status and served as a judge.

EDCS-15900593.translation: Procilla, mother, [dedicated this] to her daughter Publicia Bassilla, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-15900593.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother, Procilla, to her daughter Publicia Bassilla.

EDCS-15900594.translation: Publius Rupilius, son of Aulus, and Lucius Minicius, son of Lucius, as duovirs, undertook the construction of the field and wall by decree of the decurions and approved it themselves.
EDCS-15900594.summary: This inscription records two duovirs, Publius Rupilius and Lucius Minicius, overseeing and approving the construction of a field and wall by decree of the local council.

EDCS-15900596.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sextilia Adiecta [erected this] to her husband, Publius Sentius Felix, Augustalis of Ravenna, an oil merchant, the best husband.
EDCS-15900596.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sextilia Adiecta for her husband Publius Sentius Felix, an Augustalis and oil merchant from Ravenna.

EDCS-15900599.translation: [---]antius, son of Lucius, [---]t, son of Publius Ulvius, dedicated [it] from his own funds.
EDCS-15900599.summary: This is a dedication of an unknown object or building by a person named Antiantius, son of Lucius, and a certain t, son of Publius Ulvius, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900600.translation: [---] Lucius Ae[---], Gaius Rufren[us ---] for the construction of [---].
EDCS-15900600.summary: This inscription fragment likely records a dedication or commission for a building project, mentioning individuals named Lucius Ae[---] and Gaius Rufrenus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900603.translation: Arsinia Thalassa, freedwoman of Gaius, made this for Titus Baebius Potitus, freedman of a woman, and for herself, while alive.
EDCS-15900603.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Arsinia Thalassa for herself and for Titus Baebius Potitus, indicating it was a private commission made during their lifetimes, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900604.summary: This is a simple inscription marking the burial place of Marcus Caesius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900605.translation: The bones of Titus Calvius [---]lanci CT[---]S TL[---].
EDCS-15900605.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription indicating the burial place of Titus Calvius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900606.translation: [---] Dacun[---]da. Celadus lived 30 years for your ashes.
EDCS-15900606.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Celadus, who lived 30 years and is associated with the ashes of an unknown person, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900607.translation: To the divine shades. Publius Petronius Proculus made this for his well-deserving wife, Cossinia Fortunata.
EDCS-15900607.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Publius Petronius Proculus to his wife, Cossinia Fortunata, likely set up in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900608.translation: Gaius Fufius Lathris, Cassia, freedwoman of Titus [---].
EDCS-15900608.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary epitaph or a dedication naming Gaius Fufius Lathris and Cassia, possibly related to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900609.summary: This is a simple inscription marking the burial place of Herennia Helice, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900610.translation: Laetus, his freedman brother, erected this.
EDCS-15900610.summary: This inscription records that Laetus, a freedman and brother, erected a monument.

EDCS-15900611.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Liccaeus.

EDCS-15900612.translation: To the divine shades. Marcus Livius Gallus, son of Marcus, made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-15900612.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by Marcus Livius Gallus for himself and his family during their lifetime, likely set up in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900613.translation: Marcia, freedwoman of Quintus, made this for herself and her daughter while alive.
EDCS-15900613.summary: A funerary monument erected by Marcia for herself and her daughter.

EDCS-15900614.translation: Of Lucius Nummius Herm(es), freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Obulcius Pyrrus, freedman of Lucius, (and) Numia Acume, by the will of Lucius Obulcius Pyrrus, freedman of Lucius, under the supervision of Numia Acume.
EDCS-15900614.summary: A funerary inscription concerning multiple individuals, likely specifying inheritance or burial rights, possibly dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15900615.translation: Titus Olius, son of Titus, and Titus Olius Ingenuos, freedman of Titus, and Olia Erotis, freedwoman of Titus, and Olia Nice, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-15900615.summary: A list of names, possibly belonging to a family or group, likely related to a funerary monument or property ownership.

EDCS-15900617.translation: Premature death caused [his] father (?) to make [this for him]. Lucius Pituanius Quintilla (his) son (?).
EDCS-15900617.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription indicating a premature death and a parent's or child's erection of the monument.

EDCS-15900618.translation: To Lucius Pomponius Corbulus, son of Gaius, [chief magistrate/duovir]
EDCS-15900618.summary: A dedication to Lucius Pomponius Corbulus, an official who held the office of duovir, likely in the context of a public building or honorific monument.

EDCS-15900619.translation: Sacred to the shades of the underworld. For Primitia, who deserved well, [this was made].
EDCS-15900619.summary: A funerary dedication to a woman named Primitia, indicating she was well-regarded by the dedicator.

EDCS-15900620.translation: Gaius Tarquinius Pollio, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, rests here in a plot 20 feet square.
EDCS-15900620.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial plot dimensions for Gaius Tarquinius Pollio, suggesting ownership of a burial space.

EDCS-15900621.translation: Tulliena Herais lies here. Her pious son placed (this).
EDCS-15900621.summary: A funerary inscription for Tulliena Herais, erected by her devoted son.

EDCS-15900622.translation: The bones of Titus Veidius Optatus, who lived 31 years.
EDCS-15900622.summary: A funerary inscription stating the age at death of Titus Veidius Optatus.

EDCS-15900624.translation: For Vibius, son of Lucius, of the Maecia tribe; Caninia [---] and Aucta, his freedwoman wife, who lived in harmony, Philo nicius and Grata, freedmen, set this up.
EDCS-15900624.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Vibius and his wife, set up by their freedmen, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-15900625.translation: The bones of Aulus Volumnius Platani, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-15900625.summary: A funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Aulus Volumnius Platani, a freedman.

EDCS-15900628.translation: To the departed spirits, Gaius F A Primum for his wife Thicchia Cupra.
EDCS-15900628.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) for Thicchia Cupra, set up by her husband Gaius F A Primum.

EDCS-15900629.translation: Certe Cupra lived years [---]; while remaining here, she dedicated this.
EDCS-15900629.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Certe Cupra and suggests she dedicated something during her life.

EDCS-15900630.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a woman named Mammaea, likely on a tomb or a shrine.

EDCS-15900636.translation: Artas, the heir, made this, the burial of Paulus and Eufimia, betrothed, on Saturday, the 13th day before the Kalends of February, in the consulship of Basilius.
EDCS-15900636.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Paulus and Eufimia, set up by their heir Artas, with a precise date in February during the consulship of Basilius.

EDCS-15900639.translation: Lucius Pescenius, son of Titus, gave this gift to Mercurius, deservedly. Sacred rites to Jupiter Styx.
EDCS-15900639.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the god Mercurius by Lucius Pescenius, son of Titus, and mentions sacred rites to Jupiter Styx, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000364.translation: Lucius Terentius, son of Lucius; Caius Aprufenius, son of Caius; Lucius Turpilius, son of Caius; Marcus Albanius, son of Lucius; Titus Munatius, son of Titus, quaestors, gave this from the toll duties.
EDCS-16000364.summary: This inscription records a dedication by several quaestors for public works, funded by toll revenues, likely during the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16000365.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Conservator for the health of Lucius Hermonius Forensianus, his son. Lucius Hermonius Pierus made this.
EDCS-16000365.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Silvanus Conservator by Lucius Hermonius Pierus for the health of his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000367.translation: To Marcus Aelius Aurelius Caesar, consul for the second time, son of Emperor Antoninus Pius, father of the country, by decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-16000367.summary: This is a public dedication by decree of the town council to Marcus Aelius Aurelius Caesar, consul and son of Antoninus Pius, likely dating to the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16000370.translation: To Titus Appalius Alfinus Secundus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, procurator of the Emperor for the twentieth part of inheritances, procurator of the Alpes Atrectianae, prefect of the transport service, sub-prefect of the Praetorian fleet at Ravenna, prefect of the First Augusta Thracian Ala, tribune of the First Aelia Brittonum Cohort, prefect of the Fourth Gallorum Cohort, patron of the colony, priest of all the deified emperors, twice duumvir for five years, because of his merits, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000370.summary: This extensive funerary or honorific inscription details the distinguished career of Titus Appalius Alfinus Secundus, a Roman official of equestrian rank, and records his recognition by the town council, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16000371.translation: To Marcus Gavius Maximus, son of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe, prefect of the Praetorian Guard, honored with consular ornaments. Tiberius Claudius Firmus, a former centurion, a primus pilus, gave this plot of land by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000371.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a burial plot by Tiberius Claudius Firmus to Marcus Gavius Maximus, a prefect of the Praetorian Guard, by decree of the town council, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000376.translation: To Lucius Volcacius Primus, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, prefect of the First Noricorum Cohort in Pannonia, prefect of the bank of the Danube and of the two civitates of the Boii and Azalii, military tribune of the Fifth Macedonian Legion in Moesia, prefect of the First Pannoniorum Ala in Africa, duumvir for five years, priest of all the deified emperors, patron of the colony. Placed according to his will. To Marcus Accius Seneca and Manlius Planta, duumvirs for five years, the plot was given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000376.summary: This inscription details the military and civic career of Lucius Volcacius Primus and records the posthumous placement of his monument, funded by his will and approved by the town council, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000378.translation: To Lucius Volcacius Primus, son of Quintus, duumvir, duumvir for five years, priest of all the deified emperors, patron of the colony. Placed according to his will. To Quintus Licinius Crispus and Gaius Herennius Maximus, duumvirs.
EDCS-16000378.summary: This inscription records the posthumous placement of a monument to Lucius Volcacius Primus, funded by his will and erected by the local duumvirs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000380.translation: The bones of Titus Accaeus Philadelphus, freedman of Titus, an official of the VIIIviri.
EDCS-16000380.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Titus Accaeus Philadelphus, a freedman who held an official position within the VIIIviri, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000381.translation: To Alliena, daughter of Titus, Berenice. Gaius Vettius Polus to his most chaste wife, and Gaius Vettius Polus to his most dutiful mother, patroness of the guilds of smiths and centonarii. The plot was given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000381.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a burial plot by Gaius Vettius Polus for his wife and mother, who was a patroness of craft guilds, by decree of the town council, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000382.translation: Quintus Attius, son of Caius, and Septimius, son of Caius, aediles, and Caesonius, son of Publius, quaestor, saw to the water supply by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000382.summary: This inscription records the civic officials (aediles and quaestor) responsible for a water supply project funded by a decree of the town council.

EDCS-16000383.translation: For Aurelia Picentina, her mother. Titus Grassius Sabinus, her son, granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000383.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot granted by the town council to Aurelia Picentina, dedicated by her son.

EDCS-16000384.translation: To Gaius Calpurnius Celadus, twice holder of the office of VIIIvir, and to his wife, Accavae Salvillae.
EDCS-16000384.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Calpurnius Celadus, a local magistrate, and his wife.

EDCS-16000385.translation: The bones of Quintus Laetor Lucrio, VIIIvir, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16000385.summary: This inscription indicates the burial of Quintus Laetor Lucrio, a local magistrate, whose burial place was granted by the town council.

EDCS-16000386.translation: Quintilia Procilla, his wife, placed with willing love and devotion the bones of her husband, Publicius Optatus, a deserving VIIIvir.
EDCS-16000386.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication from a wife to her husband, Publicius Optatus, who was a local magistrate.

EDCS-16000387.translation: To Marcus Septimius Anterotus, VIIIvir of Firmius; Septimia Attice, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-16000387.summary: This inscription records the burial of Marcus Septimius Anterotus, a local magistrate, and his freedwoman Septimia Attice.

EDCS-16000390.translation: To the departed spirits. To Philumenus, the actor, and his children.
EDCS-16000390.summary: This is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld for Philumenus, an actor, and his children.

EDCS-16000392.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented dedication or list of names, possibly for a funerary monument.

EDCS-16000393.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Alleius Dexter.

EDCS-16000394.translation: Allia Helpis, freedwoman of Quintus and Marcus.
EDCS-16000394.summary: This inscription identifies Allia Helpis as a freedwoman and likely marks her burial or memorial.

EDCS-16000395.translation: The remains of Cosm(us), freedman of Lucius Anicius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-16000395.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the remains of a freedman, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-16000396.translation: [---] D S D lived 22 years, Q ISI of the convictor.
EDCS-16000396.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the age of an individual and mentioning a 'convictor', possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000397.summary: This is a simple patronymic inscription, likely recording a father-son relationship.

EDCS-16000398.translation: Of Aulus Cassidius, freedman of Aulus Bassus.
EDCS-16000398.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying an individual named Bassus, freedman of Aulus Cassidius, likely funerary, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000399.translation: Marcus Clodius Rufus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, rests here. Publius Clodius, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, made this for his brother.
EDCS-16000399.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Clodius Rufus, with his brother Publius Clodius as the dedicator, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000400.translation: Logas [Clodia?], mother and father for their most sweet son, who lived 5 years, 10 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-16000400.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a young child, Logas, with parents as dedicators, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000401.translation: Marcus Eppius Rufio, freedman of Marcus, and Salvia, freedwoman of his concubine, placed this.
EDCS-16000401.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by a freedman and his concubine's freedwoman, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000402.translation: To Euodia, most sweet daughter, who lived 14 years, 6 months, and 24 days. Zosimus and Laudice, parents, for a deserving daughter.
EDCS-16000402.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Euodia and is dedicated by her parents, Zosimus and Laudice, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000403.translation: Publius Fabius Blandus, Fabia Bassus, freedwoman of Publius, [Anteros, freedman of the woman?], [Pollitta, daughter?], [...]IAS[.
EDCS-16000403.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning several individuals, possibly related to a funerary monument or ownership, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000404.text_edition: \n Fadiae Titi filiae Paullae uxori Titi Saturi Titi filii Celeris matri Quinti Latroni Quinti filii Asclepiad(is) in fronte pedes XV in agro pedes XV\n
EDCS-16000404.translation: To Fadiana Paula, daughter of Titus, wife of Titus Saturius Celer, son of Titus, and mother of Quintus Latro, son of Quintus. 15 feet in front, 15 feet in the ground.
EDCS-16000404.summary: This funerary inscription records the deceased Fadiana Paula and details the dimensions of her burial plot, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000405.translation: Publius Florius Optatus [dedicated this] for himself and Rufria Prima, Utilis(?), a slave, lived 18 years. 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the ground.
EDCS-16000405.summary: This funerary inscription records Publius Florius Optatus dedicating a tomb for himself and his slave Utilis, specifying plot dimensions, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000406.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Gavius, son of Titus.

EDCS-16000407.translation: To the Divine Shades. Antherus for his most excellent wife Helladis, well deserving.
EDCS-16000407.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades by Antherus for his wife Helladis, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16000408.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Herennius Onirus.

EDCS-16000409.translation: Lucius Herennius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Velina tribe, erected this for his freedwoman Corinthis, measuring 14 feet in depth and 12 feet in frontage.
EDCS-16000409.summary: This is a boundary inscription indicating property dimensions, set up by Lucius Herennius Rufus for his freedwoman Corinthis.

EDCS-16000410.translation: Hospes placed this while alive for Homulla.
EDCS-16000410.summary: This is a dedication, possibly funerary, placed by a living person named Hospes for Homulla.

EDCS-16000411.translation: The bones of Ikari, slave of the Tigidii.
EDCS-16000411.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Ikari, a slave belonging to the Tigidii family.

EDCS-16000412.translation: The bones of Faustus, freedwoman of Lucius, [placed here] by her children Lucius, Secunda, and Felix, at their own expense.
EDCS-16000412.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fausta, freedwoman of Lucius, placed by her children.

EDCS-16000413.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Manilius, son of Publius, freedman B[---], [erected this for] Vibia I[---]IAID, his wife.
EDCS-16000413.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Vibia, wife of Publius Manilius.

EDCS-16100750.translation: To Marcius Frugi, to Marcia Cypare, daughter of Lucius. Why do you hurry, traveler, to go? Three days of sorrow will hold you. Do not believe, man, that you belong to future time. Here a few events will indicate to you, with sweet weight, that a mother rejoiced in her enclosed womb to have given birth to a boy ten days before the Kalends. And already the father was asking the gods that he might see the boy's first years, [and later] dedicate the young man to military service. Fortune, while she strives to emulate the great.
EDCS-16100750.summary: This is a funerary epigram, likely for a young man named Marcius Frugi, lamenting his death and reflecting on life, family, and fortune.

EDCS-16100751.translation: The bones of Eronis, of Caius Modus.
EDCS-16100751.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Eronis, associated with Caius Modus.

EDCS-16100752.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Munatius Felix, identified as the recipient's father.

EDCS-16100753.translation: To the departed spirits. [They] placed [this] for Numisia Silvina, a deserving wife, [who deserved well].
EDCS-16100753.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Numisia Silvina, described as a deserving wife, placed by her husband (vicarius).

EDCS-16100754.translation: The bones of Numitoria Murenilla, daughter of Caius, who lived 14 years.
EDCS-16100754.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Numitoria Murenilla, daughter of Caius, who died at the age of 14.

EDCS-16100755.translation: Rufilia, daughter of Rufilius, set this up for Sabina, daughter of Lucius, her Saturnina.
EDCS-16100755.summary: A funerary monument set up by Rufilia for Sabina, likely her daughter or relative.

EDCS-16100756.translation: To the departed spirits. Spurius Saufeius, son of Spurius, lived for 6 years and 1 month and 5 days. Fate, which had been destined for the parent, death's premature arrival made the father perform.
EDCS-16100756.summary: A tombstone for a young boy, Spurius Saufeius, noting his short life and the premature death that compelled his father to erect it.

EDCS-16100758.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcus Siccius Firmanus, who lived 16 years and 10 days. Siccius Dexter (father) and Iunia Apra (mother) and Iunius Dexter and Siccius... [---]
EDCS-16100758.summary: A tombstone for a young man named Marcus Siccius Firmanus, erected by his parents and siblings.

EDCS-16100760.translation: Syrus is buried here for Suedia Doris and for Quintus Suedius Communis, freedman of my freedmen. He lived 18 years.
EDCS-16100760.summary: A funerary inscription for a freedman named Syrus, likely belonging to the household of Suedia Doris and Quintus Suedius Communis.

EDCS-16100761.translation: To the departed spirits. For Terentius Paullinus, a most excellent young man, who lived 35 years, 2 months, and 15 days. Vindia Restuta, his mother, and Atilia Tertia, his wife, deceived by sorrow with her sons, set this up for him, who deserved well.
EDCS-16100761.summary: A tombstone for Terentius Paullinus, erected by his mother and wife with their sons, honoring his virtuous life.

EDCS-16100762.translation: To the divine spirits of Tigidia, daughter of Sextus, called Accepta.
EDCS-16100762.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Tigidia Accepta.

EDCS-16100763.translation: The bones of Tusidia Chloe, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-16100763.summary: A simple funerary marker indicating the resting place of Tusidia Chloe.

EDCS-16100764.translation: Veturia Gratilla and Thais, daughter of Caius, freedwoman of Aquila, patroness.
EDCS-16100764.summary: This funerary inscription records Veturia Gratilla and Thais, freedwoman and patroness.

EDCS-16100765.translation: For Urso. Petronia Ephapronis, freedwoman of Titus Petilius Expectatus, lived for 1 year, 8 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-16100765.summary: A tombstone for Urso, erected by Petronia Ephapronis, a freedwoman.

EDCS-16100769.translation: Maxima, a good, Christian, chaste woman, in peace, who died before the seventh day before the Kalends of June, who lived 15 years with her husband and died at about 30 years of age.
EDCS-16100769.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Maxima, a Christian woman who died around the age of 30 after 15 years of marriage, dated to late May.

EDCS-16100770.translation: Emperor Caesar Domitianus Augustus, son of the deified Vespasian, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the second time, consul for the eighth time, designated consul for the ninth time, father of the fatherland, sends greetings to the IIvirate and decurions of the Falerienses from Picenum. As you have learned what I have decreed concerning the unassigned lands, the case between you and the Firmani having been investigated, I have ordered it to be attached to this letter. On the 19th day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Publius Valerius Patruinus and Lucius Antonius Saturninus. Emperor Caesar Domitianus Augustus, son of the deified Vespasian, having summoned eminent men of both orders, having investigated the case between the Falerienses and the Firmani, I have decreed what is written below. And the long-standing dispute, which is being revived by the Firmani against the Falerienses after so many years, greatly disturbs me, since fewer years may suffice for the security of possessors. And the most diligent and most indulgent deified Augustus, in a letter to his 'quartani' (tenants/landholders?), admonished them to collect and sell all their unassigned lands, and I do not doubt that they obeyed such a salutary admonition. For which reason I confirm the right of the possessors. Farewell. On the 22nd day before the Kalends of August, at Alba, while the care was being managed by Titus Bovius Verus, legate, to Publius Bovius Sabinus, to Publius Petronius Achilles, by decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-16100770.summary: An imperial rescript issued by Emperor Domitian, clarifying land ownership rights between the communities of Falerii and Firmum, confirming the rights of existing possessors based on previous imperial advice.

EDCS-16100771.translation: Picentina, freedwoman of Atellia, Bonae Deae, paid her vow for [our] health.
EDCS-16100771.summary: A votive offering dedicated by a freedwoman to the goddess Bona Dea for the health of her patroness Atellia.

EDCS-16100772.translation: Sacred to Imperial Faith. Gaius Servilius Aper, an *Augustalis* of the *collegium* of eight priests, made this at his own expense for honor, by the indulgence of his patroness Servilia Bassilla and her daughter Clodia Prisca.
EDCS-16100772.summary: A dedication to Fides Augustae (Imperial Faith) made by a local magistrate (Augustalis), funded by himself and also mentioning his patroness and her daughter.

EDCS-16100775.translation: To Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus, designated consul.
EDCS-16100775.summary: An inscription dedicated to Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus and designated consul.

EDCS-16100776.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus; high priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, imperator for the 3rd time, father of the country. Lucius Celer, on behalf of his son and himself, ordered this to be made by his will. Gaius Octavius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, with additional funds, saw to its construction.
EDCS-16100776.summary: A dedication to Emperor Claudius Germanicus, commissioned by Lucius Celer and completed by Gaius Octavius Celer, likely for a public monument.

EDCS-16100777.summary: A fragmented inscription indicating that someone named Nerva made something.

EDCS-16100778.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-16100778.translation: To Emperor Caesar Antoninus Augustus Pius. Antonia Picentina, daughter of Gnaeus, [---] Secundus, praetor, patron of the colony, priestess of the divine Faustina, placed the statues she had promised for the adornment of the theatre to the people of Falerii, and at the dedication gave distributions to the decurions and the urban populace.
EDCS-16100778.summary: A dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius by Antonia Picentina, a priestess and patron of the colony, who also funded statues and distributions to the populace.

EDCS-16100780.text_edition: \n Marco Aurelio Commodo Augusto Antonini Augusti Pii filio principi iuventutis tribunicia potestate II consuli Volsae aedilis IIvir quinquennalis\n
EDCS-16100780.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Commodus Augustus, son of Antoninus Augustus Pius, prince of the youth, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, aedile, duovir for five years.
EDCS-16100780.summary: An inscription honoring Marcus Aurelius Commodus, detailing his titles and magistracies.

EDCS-16100781.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus.

EDCS-16100789.translation: To Titus Cornasidius Sabinus, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, a man of distinguished memory, procurator of Augustus in Dacia Apulensis, procurator of the Cottian Alps and the Pennine Alps with the right of the sword, subprefect of the Praetorian fleet at Ravenna, prefect of the ala veterana Gallorum, tribune of the II Augusta legion, prefect of the I Cohortis Montanorum, patron of the colony, augur of the Laurentes Lavinates, aedile, duovir for five years, quaestor of public funds. In honor of Titus Cornasidius Clementis, son of Vesennius, his son, of the Laurentes Lavinates, possessing public equestrian rank, patron of the populace and the collegia, who transmitted the honor of the statue offered to him by them, in honor and memory of his father.
EDCS-16100789.summary: An extensive cursus honorum and dedication for Titus Cornasidius Sabinus, detailing his many offices and patronage, and a subsequent honor for his son.

EDCS-16100791.translation: To Quintus Allius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, duovir for five years, for the second time, Augustan flamen, military tribune, prefect of the artisans, prefect of a cohort.
EDCS-16100791.summary: An inscription listing the offices held by Quintus Allius Rufus, including duovir, flamen, tribune, and prefect.

EDCS-16100793.translation: To Gaius Annius Tiron, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, aedile, duovir for five years, here after [---] Lucius Octavius and Gaius [---] ius [---].
EDCS-16100793.summary: An inscription mentioning Gaius Annius Tiron, who held the offices of aedile and duovir, with fragmented context about others.

EDCS-16100794.translation: To Lucius Brittius, son of Lucius, aedile, duovir, affairs of state remitted.
EDCS-16100794.summary: An inscription honoring Lucius Brittius for his service as aedile and duovir, indicating a remission of public duties.

EDCS-16100795.translation: To Marcus Fabio Maximo, son of Marcus, of the Velina tribe, upon the remission of his aedileship, as duovir, prefect of the craftsmen, and patron of the colony, for the republic.
EDCS-16100795.summary: This is a dedication honoring Marcus Fabio Maximo for his public service, likely on a public building or monument.

EDCS-16100796.translation: Procula, wife of Gaius Fuficius Genialis, freedman of Gaius, an Augustalis, and of Firmius and Faleriō, daughter of Titus Cardanus, set this up.
EDCS-16100796.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Procula for her husband, Gaius Fuficius Genialis, a freedman and Augustalis.

EDCS-16100797.translation: Gaius Helvius Agens, an unofficial diviner, by decree of the decurions, and his concubine, Orbicia Procula, freedwoman of a woman named Orbicia, lived 30 years.
EDCS-16100797.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Helvius Agens, a diviner, and his concubine Orbicia Procula, noting Agens's status and Procula's age at death.

EDCS-16100798.translation: Julius Eros, Augustalis duovir, made honorary member by decree of the decurions, erected [this].
EDCS-16100798.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Eros, an Augustalis duovir who was granted honorary citizenship.

EDCS-16100799.translation: Marcus Ancharius and Gaius Decimius, son of Gaius Valerius, set this up to be made for Octavia, sister of the deified Augustus.
EDCS-16100799.summary: An inscription indicating that Marcus Ancharius and Gaius Decimius Valerius were responsible for the construction of a monument or tomb for Octavia, sister of Augustus.

EDCS-16100800.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Sillius Priscus, freedman of Titus, master and quaestor of the guild of craftsmen, master and quaestor of the association of fullers, and to his wife, Claudia Procula, freedwoman of Tiberius, mother of the association of fullers. Titus Sillius Karus and Tiberius Claudius Philippus, masters and quaestors of the guild of craftsmen, their sons, [set this up] for their most devoted parents.
EDCS-16100800.summary: A funerary dedication by two sons for their parents, Titus Sillius Priscus and Claudia Procula, who held distinguished positions in guilds of craftsmen and fullers.

EDCS-16100801.translation: To the departed spirits. To Gaius Valerius Onesimus, freedman of Gaius, an Augustalis. Faleriō. Trebia Cervia, to her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-16100801.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Valerius Onesimus, a freedman and Augustalis, erected by his wife Trebia Cervia.

EDCS-16100802.translation: To Lucius Veianius Mamulla, son of Gaius, who received the public horse, prefect of the craftsmen, duovir for the second time, quinquennalis, by decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-16100802.summary: An inscription honoring Lucius Veianius Mamulla, detailing his public career and honors, likely displayed on a public building or monument.

EDCS-16100803.translation: [---]ontius, aedile, remitted by the duovir for the state affairs.
EDCS-16100803.summary: This inscription records a remission of duties or fines related to public office, involving an aedile and a duovir.

EDCS-16100811.summary: A brief funerary epitaph for Sermo, a young slave of Apollonius.

EDCS-16100812.translation: To Quintus Tullienus Marion, the designer. The associates, the designers.
EDCS-16100812.summary: An inscription honoring Quintus Tullienus Marion, a designer, erected by his colleagues.

EDCS-16100813.translation: Phanias, freedman of Quintus Tullienus, physician.
EDCS-16100813.summary: A very brief inscription identifying Phanias as a freedman and physician.

EDCS-16100815.translation: Quintus Annalius Ases, freedman of Quintus, and Annalia Stratonice, freedwoman of Quintus, rest here.
EDCS-16100815.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of two freedpersons, Quintus Annalius Ases and Annalia Stratonice.

EDCS-16100816.translation: To Atalante, by Caius Petronius Crescentis.
EDCS-16100816.summary: This is a dedication to Atalante, likely a freedwoman or family member, by Caius Petronius Crescentis.

EDCS-16100817.translation: To the divine spirits of Caius Atalius Lucilianus, son of Caius.
EDCS-16100817.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Atalius Lucilianus.

EDCS-16100818.translation: Lucius Attius Philo and Lucius Attius Thallus.
EDCS-16100818.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple naming of two individuals, Lucius Attius Philo and Lucius Attius Thallus, likely related.

EDCS-16100819.translation: To the departed spirits, for the sweetest infant Basilides, who lived 7 years, 2 months, and 8 days. Hilarianus, father, and Basilia, mother, for their most unhappy but deserving child.
EDCS-16100819.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Basilides, set up by his grieving parents, Hilarianus and Basilia.

EDCS-16100820.translation: To Boviae Faustae, by Bovi[us] Flaccus.
EDCS-16100820.summary: This is a dedication to Boviae Faustae, likely a relative, by Bovi(us) Flaccus.

EDCS-16100821.translation: To the departed spirits. Of Quintus Caecilius Eroticus, who lived 42 years [and 3 days]. Caecilius Chrestus, for an incomparable freedman, and Caecilia Romana, with whom he lived 25 years and 7 months without complaint. Here, seven months after the death of his daughter, he died.
EDCS-16100821.summary: This funerary inscription honors Caecilius Chrestus, a freedman, and his wife Caecilia Romana, and also mentions their deceased daughter.

EDCS-16100822.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Erotice, who lived 11 years and 30 days. Caecilius Eroticus and Romana, parents.
EDCS-16100822.summary: This funerary epitaph is for Caecilia Erotice, who died at a young age, and was set up by her parents, Caecilius Eroticus and Romana.

EDCS-16100823.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tiberius Claudius Philippus. Terentia, freedwoman of a woman, for herself and her husband.
EDCS-16100823.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Philippus, with Terentia, a freedwoman, dedicating it for herself and her husband.

EDCS-16100825.translation: Fannia, daughter of Aulus, wife of Lucius Vetilius Praetutianus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-16100825.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription identifying Fannia and her husband, Lucius Vetilius Praetutianus.

EDCS-16100826.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to record the grief of parents and a sister named Felicitas.

EDCS-16100827.translation: For six months Vlius Sta and Festa to the most dutiful.
EDCS-16100827.summary: This inscription likely refers to a funerary dedication for Vlius Sta and Festa, possibly for a period of six months.

EDCS-16100828.translation: To Petronia Florida, dearest and most beloved friend, well-deserving.
EDCS-16100828.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia Florida, dedicated by a friend.

EDCS-16100829.translation: To Fuficia Tyche, most loving and incomparable wife. Marcus Paccius Athenodorus, with whom she lived for 26 years, chaste, pious, and holy, died at the age of 13.
EDCS-16100829.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fuficia Tyche, wife of Marcus Paccius Athenodorus, and provides her age at death.

EDCS-16100830.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, with an unknown dedicant and recipient.

EDCS-16100831.translation: Publius Gavius Camars, son of Publius, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-16100831.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Gavius Camars.

EDCS-16100832.translation: To the Divine Shades. Italicus, our most beloved freedman, lived 3 years, 5 months. Urbanus, a servant of Caesar, and Claudia Pelagia made this.
EDCS-16100832.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the freedman Italicus by his owners, Urbanus and Claudia Pelagia.

EDCS-16100834.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Quintus Marcius Victor, who lived.
EDCS-16100834.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Quintus Marcius Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100835.translation: To Gaius Marius Sedatus. Optatus, a tenant farmer, from his own funds.
EDCS-16100835.summary: This is a dedication by Optatus, a tenant farmer, to Gaius Marius Sedatus.

EDCS-16100836.translation: To Quintus Obilenus Celer, son of Quintus.
EDCS-16100836.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Obilenus Celer, son of Quintus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100837.translation: From Lucius Obilius Plator. Auge Obilia.
EDCS-16100837.summary: This inscription appears to record a dedication or a funerary dedication from Lucius Obilius Plator to Auge Obilia.

EDCS-16100838.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Oppia, wife of Publius. [Elected as] curule aedile three times, Publius Stla MAR nus.
EDCS-16100838.summary: This funerary inscription honors Oppia and mentions Publius, who held the curule aedileship three times, suggesting a high-ranking individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100839.translation: To Caius Popillius Philero, freedman of Caius, twelve square feet for himself and his family.
EDCS-16100839.summary: This inscription records the purchase or allocation of burial space measuring twelve square feet for Caius Popillius Philero and his kin, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100840.translation: Lucius Postimius Tintyrita, freedman of Lucius, for himself and his freedwoman Urbana.
EDCS-16100840.summary: This funerary inscription indicates the purchase or allocation of burial space by Lucius Postimius Tintyrita for himself and his freedwoman Urbana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100841.translation: Titus Postumius Florus, freedman of a woman, for himself and for his dear wife Plotia Blaste, nothing...
EDCS-16100841.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Postumius Florus and his wife Plotia Blaste, with an incomplete final phrase.

EDCS-16100842.translation: To the Divine Shades. Rufilla, his fellow slave and concubine.
EDCS-16100842.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Rufilla, described as a fellow slave and concubine.

EDCS-16100843.translation: To Salvia Philematio, freedwoman of Lucius, mother. To Salvia Chrestina, freedwoman of Lucius, sister. Lucius Salvius Philemo, freedman of Lucius, at his own expense.
EDCS-16100843.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Lucius Salvius Philemo for his mother Salvia Philematio and his sister Salvia Chrestina, both freedwomen of Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100844.translation: To Seiana Philumina, freedwoman of Titus, according to the will.
EDCS-16100844.summary: This inscription records a bequest to Seiana Philumina, freedwoman of Titus, as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-16100845.translation: Sicinia Calliopa, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-16100845.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Sicinia Calliopa as a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100846.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Sillia Tertia. Sillia Fortunata, daughter, to her most devoted mother.
EDCS-16100846.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Sillia Fortunata to her mother, Sillia Tertia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100849.translation: Vitellus lived 17 years. Praesentia Accepta, mother, made this.
EDCS-16100849.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Vitellus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-16100850.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Ussius Icesius, an unparalleled man. Ussia E[3]tho to her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-16100850.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Lucius Ussius Icesius by his wife, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16100851.translation: Ussia Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and for Lucius Apidius Acutus, freedman of Lucius, from her own money.
EDCS-16100851.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a freedwoman for herself and another freedman, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16200600.translation: Gaudentia rests here. She lived for 85 years, was married for 30 years, and a widow for 37 years. She was interred on the third day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-16200600.summary: This funerary epitaph provides biographical details for Gaudentia, including her lifespan, marital status, and date of burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200601.translation: Buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of August. Masinia [3]ntia lived 3 years... with her husband... 17 years, 6 months, 11 days.
EDCS-16200601.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial date and lifespan of Masinia [3]ntia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200602.translation: Gaius Sillius Princeps, son of Gaius, freedman, rests here. Nobilis, a freedman, set this up at his own expense.
EDCS-16200602.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Sillius Princeps, with the monument erected by Nobilis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200603.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Decimius Fortunatus. Calvia Arethusa to her well-deserving husband and to herself.
EDCS-16200603.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Lucius Decimius Fortunatus by his wife, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16200604.translation: Gaius Petillenus Rufus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe. Publius Gavius Phileros, from money bequeathed.
EDCS-16200604.summary: An inscription recording a bequest from Publius Gavius Phileros, possibly for a public work or monument, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200605.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Decimia Propasidis. Gnaeus Sentius Ampliator to his most beloved wife.
EDCS-16200605.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Decimia Propasidis by her husband, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16200606.translation: Lucius Papirius, son of Gaius, of the Lemonia tribe. Son of Adoptatus.
EDCS-16200606.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the parentage of Lucius Papirius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200607.translation: Sertoria Myrine, freedwoman of Sertorius. Here rests Athenor, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-16200607.summary: A funerary epitaph mentioning two individuals, Sertoria Myrine and Marcus Athenor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200608.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Orbia Aphrodisia, most dutiful daughter. Lucius Orbius Verinus, the father.
EDCS-16200608.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a father to his virtuous daughter, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-16200609.translation: To Gaius Vettius, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, Tusk, standard-bearer of the Fourth Macedonian Legion.
EDCS-16200609.summary: This inscription honors a standard-bearer of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, identified as Gaius Vettius Tusk, likely a funerary or dedication text from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200610.translation: Gaius Lusius Auctus [---], Gaius Lusius Clienus [---], from their own money.
EDCS-16200610.summary: This is a record of a construction project paid for by private individuals, possibly Gaius Lusius Auctus and Gaius Lusius Clienus, indicating a private benefaction to the community.

EDCS-16200611.translation: To the gods and goddesses of Urbsalvia, Titus Flavius Maximus, procurator of the Emperor from the East, sent this offering.
EDCS-16200611.summary: This inscription records an offering by Titus Flavius Maximus, the Emperor's procurator from the East, to the gods and goddesses of Urbsalvia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200612.text_edition: \n Salutis Augustae Salviensium Marci Atti Fabati\n
EDCS-16200612.translation: To the August Health of the people of Salvia, by Marcus Attius Fabatus.
EDCS-16200612.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the August Health of Salvia, made by Marcus Attius Fabatus, likely a public or private dedication from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200615.translation: [To Gaius Salv]ius Liberalis, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, Nonius Bassus, consul, proconsul of the province of Macedonia, legate of the Emperors, legal officer of Britain, legate of the Fifth Macedonian Legion, brother of the Arvales, advanced by the deified Vespasian and the deified Titus from the ranks of the tribunes, promoted by them to the praetorian rank, holding the office of quinquennial for the fourth time, patron of the colony, was appointed proconsul of the province of Asia by lot, but excused himself.
EDCS-16200615.summary: This is a detailed cursus honorum for Gaius Salvius Liberalis, a prominent Roman official who served in various high-ranking military and administrative positions, including proconsul of Asia, dating to the Flavian or Antonine period.

EDCS-16200616.translation: To Vitellia Rufilla, daughter of Gaius, wife of Gaius Salvius Liberalis, consul, and priestess of the August Health. To his most excellent mother, Gaius Salvius Vitellianus, while living.
EDCS-16200616.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Salvius Vitellianus to his mother, Vitellia Rufilla, who was the wife of a consul and a priestess, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200617.translation: To Liberalis, from Maced, [serving as] praetor, quaestor, from Africa. Nonius.
EDCS-16200617.summary: This inscription honors Liberalis, who held the offices of praetor and quaestor, and was from Africa, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200620.translation: To Lucius Annius Capriolus, freedman of Lucius, a IIvir, Annia Antiochis, freedwoman of a woman, for her fellow freedman, with her daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-16200620.summary: This funerary inscription honors Lucius Annius Capriolus, a freedman and a IIvir, by Annia Antiochis, his fellow freedwoman and her daughter, indicating a relationship within freedman circles.

EDCS-16200621.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. To Atalia Sabina, daughter of Gaius. Marcus Molletius Valens, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, aedile, to his most pious wife. And Gaius Publicius Florus and Terentia Moderata, to their most pious daughter. She lived 24 years, 5 months, 19 days.
EDCS-16200621.summary: This is a joint funerary inscription for Atalia Sabina, her husband Marcus Molletius Valens, and their daughter, erected by her parents, providing genealogical information and dates of life.

EDCS-16200622.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Marcus Calvius Clemens, IIvir of Urbsalvia. Marcus Calvius Sabinus, to his deserving patron, and to Calvia Iucundissima, his dearest wife, his wife.
EDCS-16200622.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Calvius Clemens, a IIvir of Urbsalvia, and his wife Calvia Iucundissima, erected by Marcus Calvius Sabinus, likely a patron-client relationship.

EDCS-16200623.text_edition: \n ] Herennius Cai filius Aufidius Luci filius IIIIviri viam ad campum lapide sternendam curaverunt de poblico longam pedes DLXX \n
EDCS-16200623.translation: Herennius, son of Gaius, son of Lucius, and Aufidius, son of Lucius, the IIviri, saw to the paving of the road to the field with stones, publicly, 570 feet long.
EDCS-16200623.summary: This inscription records the completion of a public works project, the paving of a road, by two IIviri officials of Urbsalvia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200625.translation: Lucius Satu, one of the four men.
EDCS-16200625.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Satu as holding the office of a 'quattuorvir' (one of four men, likely a local magistrate).

EDCS-16200628.translation: Clemens rests here after 71 years; his wife is dead.
EDCS-16200628.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Clemens at the age of 71 and notes that his wife is also deceased.

EDCS-16200629.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Flavius Epicteus set this up for his well-deserving wife, Flavia Hygeia.
EDCS-16200629.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Hygeia, set up by her husband, Publius Flavius Epicteus, who set this up for his well-deserving wife.

EDCS-16200630.translation: To the departed spirits. For Geminia Severa, his most beloved daughter, who lived 5 years, 8 months. Geminius Primitivus and Severa (set this up) for her as one deserving of remembrance.
EDCS-16200630.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminia Severa, who died at a young age, set up by her parents, Geminius Primitivus and Severa.

EDCS-16200631.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tiberius Julius Telesphorus, who lived 10 years, 2 months, 11 days. His most sorrowful mother, Iulia, set this up.
EDCS-16200631.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Julius Telesphorus, who died as a child, set up by his mother, Iulia.

EDCS-16200632.translation: To the departed spirits. For his most beloved wife, Iulia Fortunata, with whom he lived for 50 years. Manlius Ikarus (set this up) for her as one deserving.
EDCS-16200632.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Fortunata, wife of Manlius Ikarus, set up by her husband.

EDCS-16201187.text_edition: \n Marcus Allius Alli Atti procuratoris Augusti libertus Agenor VIIIvir Augustalis ponderarium cum ponderibus et mensuris pecunia sua loco suo fecit et statuis omnium deorum et dearum exornavit et dedicatione eius sportulas et ludos quos nemo antea eiusdem ordinis hominum dederat dedit\n
EDCS-16201187.translation: Agenor, freedman of Marcus Allius, freedman of the emperor, an Augustalis of the eight, made this weighing station with weights and measures at his own expense, in his own place, and adorned it with statues of all the gods and goddesses, and at its dedication he provided distributions and games, which no one of the same rank of men had previously given.
EDCS-16201187.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public weighing station with amenities, funded and dedicated by Agenor, a freedman and local official, who also provided distributions and games.

EDCS-16400105.text_edition: \n Marco Septimio Marci filioli |(centurioni) legionum X fretensis II primae Minerviae II II primae Parthicae III Gallicae XXII Primigeniae primo pilo praeposito Umbriae Piceni et Apuliae coloniae Anconitanorum et C complurium civitatum heredes patrono\n
EDCS-16400105.translation: To Marcus Septimius, son of Marcus, centurion of Legions X Fretensis, II Primigenia, II II Parthica, III Gallica, XXII Primigenia, first-rank centurion, commander of Umbria and Picenum and Apulia, of the colony of Ancona, and of many cities, his heirs to their patron.
EDCS-16400105.summary: This is a dedication by the heirs of various cities to their patron, Marcus Septimius, a highly decorated centurion and provincial administrator.

EDCS-16700153.text_edition: \n Invicto Propitio Salvius Novanio Lucianus donum posuit\n
EDCS-16700153.translation: Salvius Novanio Lucianus dedicated this offering to the unconquered and propitious god.
EDCS-16700153.summary: This is a dedication of an offering to an unconquered and propitious deity by Salvius Novanio Lucianus.

EDCS-16800244.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucio Septimio Marcelliano <e=F>(gregiae) memoriae viro ex corniculario praeffectorum et duobus fratribus German Lucio Septimio Domitiano <e=F>(gregiae) memoriae viro ex primi pilo \n
EDCS-16800244.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Lucius Septimius Marcellianus, a man of outstanding memory, from the cornucularii of the prefects, and to his two brothers, Germanus and Lucius Septimius Domitianus, a man of outstanding memory, from the primipilaris.
EDCS-16800244.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Lucius Septimius Marcellianus and his two brothers, who held distinguished military and administrative positions.

EDCS-16900007.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Antistio Severo militi cohortis VIIII praetoriae speculatori militans nnos X decessit Faleris cuius cineres Antistius Coraesus rettulit pater\n
EDCS-16900007.translation: To the departed spirits. To Gaius Antistius Severus, soldier of the 9th praetorian cohort, a scout, who served for 10 years and died at Falerii. His father, Antistius Coraesus, brought back his ashes.
EDCS-16900007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Antistius Severus, a praetorian soldier and scout, who died in service, with his ashes returned by his father.

EDCS-16900039.text_edition: \n Divo Severo patri Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Severi Antonini Augusti Pii Felicis Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britannici maximi pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate XV imperatoris II consulis III designati IIII proconsulis decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-16900039.translation: To the deified Severus, father of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 15th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 3rd time, designated Consul for the 4th time, Proconsul, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16900039.summary: This is a posthumous dedication to Emperor Severus, father of Caracalla, honoring his titles and imperial dignities by decree of the local council.

EDCS-17300119.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker for Caius Titus Hermerotis.

EDCS-17300122.summary: This inscription likely refers to Valeria Magna and possibly her slave or freedwoman, Epibana.

EDCS-17300123.summary: This inscription likely refers to Valeria Magna and the beginning of a name, possibly a slave or freedwoman.

EDCS-17300127.translation: Of Tiberius Domitianus, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-17300127.summary: This inscription identifies Tiberius Domitianus, the son of Tiberius.

EDCS-17300129.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus Clodius Ambrosius.

EDCS-17300131.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Epidius Theodorus.

EDCS-17300132.translation: Diogenes, son of Euhemer, son of Maps.
EDCS-17300132.summary: This inscription records the genealogy of Diogenes, tracing his lineage back through his father Euhemer and grandfather Maps.

EDCS-17300133.translation: Of Aulus Faesonius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-17300133.summary: This inscription identifies Aulus Faesonius, the son of Aulus.

EDCS-17300138.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary personal name, likely a dedication or a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-17300150.translation: To Manlia Clodia Subulcinilla, daughter of Gnaeus.
EDCS-17300150.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Manlia Clodia Subulcinilla, daughter of Gnaeus.

EDCS-17300151.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Multasia, dearest daughter, who lived 15 years, 2 months, and 26 days. Publius Multasius Felix and her nurse Multasia Felicitas, to one who deserved well.
EDCS-17300151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Multasia, who died at the age of 15, dedicated by her father and nurse.

EDCS-17300152.translation: To the departed spirits. Philetes lived 14 years, 6 months. Ampliata, his mother.
EDCS-17300152.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Philetes, recording his age and dedicated by his mother Ampliata.

EDCS-17300153.translation: Of Aulus Pompaeius Salvius, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-17300153.summary: This inscription records the name of Aulus Pompaeius Salvius, a freedman, likely on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-17300154.translation: Gaius Sal, son of Gaius Sal, Gaius S.
EDCS-17300154.summary: This inscription seems to be a very abbreviated personal name or a very damaged text, possibly a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-17300155.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Terentia Severa, daughter of Marcus. Quintus Fuionius Firmus, overseer...
EDCS-17300155.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for Terentia Severa, dedicated by Quintus Fuionius Firmus, who was an overseer.

EDCS-17300157.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Veneria, dearest daughter of Martialis and Cupida.
EDCS-17300157.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Veneria, daughter of Martialis and Cupida.

EDCS-17300161.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Marcus Sicinius Olympianus, son of Marcus, of the Velina tribe, who lived 17 years, 8 months, and 4 days. Numisia Tertullina to her most dutiful son.
EDCS-17300161.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Sicinius Olympianus, who died at age 17, dedicated by his mother Numisia Tertullina.

EDCS-17300164.translation: Lucius Veratius Felissimus, patron, sacrificed victims and dedicated a bronze token to the pagani of the Tolentines district of the pagus, according to his vow, on the 6th of May, may it be fortunate.
EDCS-17300164.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a bronze token and the sacrifice of victims by Lucius Veratius Felissimus, patron, to the pagani of the Tolentines district.

EDCS-17300165.translation: Flavius Julius Catervius, a most distinguished man, former prefect of the praetorium, who lived with Septimia Severina, a most distinguished lady, his sweetest wife, for 16 years less 13 days. He rested in peace, aged 56 years and 18 days. He was buried on the 4th day before the Kalends of December.
