Septimia Severina, a most distinguished lady, for her sweetest husband and for herself, arranged and completed this sarcophagus and pantheon with a triclinium. Whom the omnipotent Lord joined in marriage with equal merits, Catervus, Severina rejoices, joined to you. The tomb guards you forever. May you rise together, blessed by Christ's grace, whom the priest of God, Probianus, washed and anointed. You lie weeping in Basso, having died again, Catervus, your lineage died. You are snatched away, Ocyus, which pleases God. Octavus Decimus, pious, had not yet received you, when the year arrived.
EDCS-17300165.summary: This elaborate funerary inscription records the life and death of Flavius Julius Catervius, his wife Septimia Severina, their family, and the tomb they commissioned, with Christian references, dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-17300166.translation: Lucius Quinctius Babilianus, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, who was twice prefect of the fabrica and a judge of the first decuria, and his wife Iconium, freedwoman of Lucius, to him. The monument was made and approved by the arbitration of his son, of the Quirina tribe, Torquatus.
EDCS-17300166.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Quinctius Babilianus and his wife Iconium, detailing his prestigious career.

EDCS-17300167.translation: By decree of the Senate, the August college of carpenters, from their own funds, constructed the building from its start on land given by Titus Furius Primigenius, who also gave 10,000 sesterces at its dedication; from the income of this sum, they will feast every year on the 11th of the Kalends of August, his birthday.
EDCS-17300167.summary: This inscription records the construction of a building for the college of carpenters, funded by its members and supplemented by a donation from Titus Furius Primigenius, who also endowed an annual feast on his birthday.

EDCS-17300168.translation: To Lucius Metilius Fructus, freedman of Lucius, a VIvir of Tolentinus, for Allidia Aria, his deserving wife.
EDCS-17300168.summary: This is a dedication on a tombstone from Tolentinus for a deceased VIvir and his wife, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-17300169.translation: Caius Veienus Trophimus, freedman of a woman, donated his own burial plots, 200 feet in front and 284 feet in depth, between the river bank and the stream, whatever falls within this area, from his own lands, to the municipium of the Tolentinates.
EDCS-17300169.summary: This inscription records the donation of burial land by Caius Veienus Trophimus, freedman, to the municipality of Tolentinates.

EDCS-17300172.translation: To the genius of the century. Vegetius Ingenuus placed (this) for deserving ones.
EDCS-17300172.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a centuria by Vegetius Ingenuus.

EDCS-17300173.translation: To Jupiter of Youth. Annnius Camurenus, [curule aedile], [son of] Genus.
EDCS-17300173.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter of Youth by Annnius Camurenus, who held the curule aedileship, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-17300174.translation: Antestia Sabina and Vibia Politice, and Clymena, Cambosa, the pious, dedicated by Felicissima Oppia Silvana.
EDCS-17300174.summary: This inscription records the dedication of individuals, possibly to a deity or as part of a funerary context, by Felicissima Oppia Silvana.

EDCS-17300176.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, Pius, Felix, Augustus, Unconquered, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, prince of youth. By decree of the decurions, publicly, from the people of Septempeda.
EDCS-17300176.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Septempeda to Emperor Aurelian, honoring his titles and authority, likely from his reign (270-275 AD).

EDCS-17300177.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pius, Felix, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, consul for the 2nd time. From the people of Septempeda.
EDCS-17300177.summary: This is a dedication by the people of Septempeda to Emperor Diocletian, acknowledging his titles and consulships, likely from around 285-295 AD.

EDCS-17300178.translation: To Magnus Princeps, Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar. The council of Septempeda, devoted to his divine majesty. Publicly.
EDCS-17300178.summary: This is a public dedication by the council of Septempeda to Caesar Constantius, recognizing his status and divine favor, likely from the period of his rule as Caesar (305-306 AD).

EDCS-17300179.translation: To Petillius Rufus, military tribune, prefect, duovir. By the townspeople and inhabitants.
EDCS-17300179.summary: This records the dedication to Petillius Rufus, who held several magistracies, by the local citizens, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-17300180.translation: To Quintus Catinus Curvus, son of Gaius, duovir.
EDCS-17300180.summary: This is an inscription honoring Quintus Catinus Curvus, son of Gaius, who held the office of duovir, likely on a public building or monument.

EDCS-17300181.translation: Curvia Nice [dedicates this] to Publius Licinius Philero, one of the six leading citizens.
EDCS-17300181.summary: This is a dedication by Curvia Nice to Publius Licinius Philero, a member of the sexvirate, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17300183.translation: Gaius Petillius Rufus, son of Marcus, and Titus Flavius, son of Salvius, censors, saw to its construction.
EDCS-17300183.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Petillius Rufus and Titus Flavius had a public work constructed during their term as censors.

EDCS-17300186.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Acilius Candidus, son of Gaius, and for Alfia Secunda, parents.
EDCS-17300186.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the parents, Gaius Acilius Candidus and Alfia Secunda, under the invocation of the Manes.

EDCS-17300188.translation: Ullius Ulvius Aterianus Dosius to his mother by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17300188.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a son to his mother, likely commemorating a public honor bestowed upon her.

EDCS-17300189.translation: On the front, 12 feet. Paterianus, freedman, alive. Philem[---]. Aprodisia, freedwoman of Gaius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-17300189.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or a tomb, mentioning Paterianus and Aprodisia, with dimensions indicated, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17300190.translation: Publius Babrenus, freedman of Publius, for himself and his patron and his family. On the front, 12 feet.
EDCS-17300190.summary: This is a funerary or property inscription by Publius Babrenus for himself and his household, indicating a frontage of 12 feet, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17300191.translation: Lucius Bruttius Philoxenus, freedman of a woman, [dedicates this] in the field, 18 feet, on the front, 16 feet.
EDCS-17300191.summary: This inscription seems to mark a property or burial plot, indicating dimensions of 18 feet in depth and 16 feet in frontage, belonging to Lucius Bruttius Philoxenus.

EDCS-17300193.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caesia Prisca, freedwoman of her Caia, [left this monument].
EDCS-17300193.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a freedwoman for herself and her patroness.

EDCS-17300194.summary: This is a simple dedication or identification of Gaius Calpenus, son of Pyiades, possibly from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-17300195.translation: Publius Calpurnius Macedo, freedman of Publius, and Bineta Maximu[---]ria and In[---] Tu[---]s, the guest, eagerly awaits [his] miserable [home].
EDCS-17300195.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Calpurnius Macedo and others, possibly recording their desire for a home or burial place.

EDCS-17300196.translation: Caius Clepius Sodalis, freedman of Caius, a tomb 14 feet in front, for himself and his wife.
EDCS-17300196.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the dimensions of a burial plot for Caius Clepius Sodalis and his wife.

EDCS-17300197.translation: Caius Clepius Sodalis, freedman of Caius, 23 feet in the field, a tomb for himself and his wife.
EDCS-17300197.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the dimensions of a burial plot in a field for Caius Clepius Sodalis and his wife.

EDCS-17300198.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Cominius.
EDCS-17300198.summary: A simple funerary dedication to Caius Cominius.

EDCS-17300199.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Didius Eudemus, freedman of Lucius, set this up for himself in his lifetime.
EDCS-17300199.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Didius Eudemus for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-17300200.translation: Caius Flavius, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300200.summary: This is a funerary or milestone inscription identifying Caius Flavius, son of Lucius, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-17300201.translation: Gaius Flavius Faustus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-17300201.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Gaius Flavius Faustus.

EDCS-17300202.translation: Servius Fulvius Suavis, freedman of Servius, for himself and Baebia Chrestini, freedwoman of Lucius, 18 feet in the field.
EDCS-17300202.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the size of a plot (18 feet) in a field, allocated for Servius Fulvius Suavis and Baebia Chrestini.

EDCS-17300203.translation: Publius Gavillius Dio, freedman of Publius, is buried here, and Gavillia Eucumene, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-17300203.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Publius Gavillius Dio and Gavillia Eucumene are buried here.

EDCS-17300204.translation: is buried here, Gavillia Eucumene, while alive, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-17300204.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Gavillia Eucumene, while alive, had this burial place reserved.

EDCS-17300205.translation: The place of Caius Herenius Montanus, son of Caius.
EDCS-17300205.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Caius Herenius Montanus.

EDCS-17300206.translation: To Lucius Herennius Phileros, freedman of Lucius, by testament.
EDCS-17300206.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Herennius Phileros, established according to his will.

EDCS-17300207.translation: Guest, servant of Matrinus, a good man, lived 24 years.
EDCS-17300207.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave named Guest, who served Matrinus and lived for 24 years.

EDCS-17300208.translation: To Lucumo, freedman, for his freedmen in front, and for his freedwomen in the land, 14 feet.
EDCS-17300208.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary boundary marker or record of land allocation for freedmen and freedwomen, with dimensions specified for front and field measurements.

EDCS-17300209.translation: To Mahena, daughter of Titus, 23 feet in the land.
EDCS-17300209.summary: This inscription records a land measurement of 23 feet associated with Mahena, daughter of Titus, likely a property boundary or allocation.

EDCS-17300210.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Blannnia Ursilla to her well-deserving husband, Lucius Metilius Euthicus.
EDCS-17300210.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Blannnia Ursilla to her deserving husband, Lucius Metilius Euthicus.

EDCS-17300211.translation: Alive. Caius Musenus Aesopus, freedman of a woman, for himself and his relatives and parents, 14 feet in front, 20 in the land.
EDCS-17300211.summary: This epitaph records that Caius Musenus Aesopus, a freedman, erected it for himself and his family, specifying front and land measurements.

EDCS-17300212.translation: Octavia Rufa, freedwoman of a woman, [dedicates this] 12 feet in front and 18 feet in the field.
EDCS-17300212.summary: This inscription details the dimensions of a plot of land dedicated by Octavia Rufa, a freedwoman.

EDCS-17300213.translation: To Quintus Petillius Attalus, freedman of Quintus, by his heirs of their own free will.
EDCS-17300213.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Petillius Attalus, a freedman, and states it was erected by his heirs willingly.

EDCS-17300214.translation: To Quintus Precius Proculus, son of Quintus. Quintus Precius, his father...
EDCS-17300214.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a father to his deceased son, Quintus Precius Proculus.

EDCS-17300215.translation: [?], daughter of Spurius Quarta, 12 feet in front.
EDCS-17300215.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary, indicating 12 feet in front for an individual identified as Quarta.

EDCS-17300216.translation: To Quintia Seve[---], dearest son, well-deserving.
EDCS-17300216.summary: This fragmented inscription is a funerary dedication to a son, described as dearest and well-deserving.

EDCS-17300217.translation: Caius Satellius Myrtilus, freedman of Caius, and Naevia Salvia, freedwoman of a woman, while alive.
EDCS-17300217.summary: This inscription records Caius Satellius Myrtilus and Naevia Salvia, both freedpersons, dedicating it for themselves while alive.

EDCS-17300218.translation: Of Marcus Servilius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-17300218.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Marcus Servilius.

EDCS-17300219.translation: Taflenia Parasita, freedwoman of Lucius, 12 feet in front, 20 in the land.
EDCS-17300219.summary: This inscription seems to mark a land boundary or property allocation for Taflenia Parasita, specifying front and field dimensions.

EDCS-17300220.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Tinnania Quartia, freedwoman of Caius, Quintus Octavius Crescens and Liberalis, [for their] wife/companion.
EDCS-17300220.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Quintus Octavius Crescens and Liberalis to their wife/companion, Tinnania Quartia.

EDCS-17300221.translation: To Lucius Titius Attalus, freedman of Lucius, and to Lucius Titius Antigonus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-17300221.summary: This is a funerary dedication to two freedmen, Lucius Titius Attalus and Lucius Titius Antigonus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300222.translation: Titia Neice, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and for Marcus Aufidius Lucrion, son of Marcus.
EDCS-17300222.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titia Neice, freedwoman of Lucius, for herself and for Marcus Aufidius Lucrion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300223.translation: For Tita Salvia, freedwoman of Lucius, and her freedman Titius Primus, for himself and his family. In front 12 feet, in the field 16 feet.
EDCS-17300223.summary: This is a funerary dedication and plot inscription for Tita Salvia and her freedman Titius Primus, indicating dimensions for a burial plot, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300224.translation: Quintus Veltius Rufillus, son of Quintus, and Veltia Rufilla, daughter of Quintus. Veltia Nice and Veltia Rufilla, daughters of Quintus, had this made for their brother and mother.
EDCS-17300224.summary: This is a funerary dedication by two sisters, Veltia Nice and Veltia Rufilla, for their deceased brother and mother, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300225.translation: Quintus Vibius Maximus, son of Quintus, made this.
EDCS-17300225.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Vibius Maximus for himself, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300226.translation: Alive. Quintus Vibius Rufus, son of Spurius.
EDCS-17300226.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Vibius Rufus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300227.translation: Place. Of Vibius Rufus. In front 20 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-17300227.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to Vibius Rufus, specifying dimensions, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300243.translation: To Manius Vibius Balbinus, son of Manius, of the Velina tribe, military tribune, prefect of the engineers, prefect of the cavalry, quaestor, plebeian aedile, prefect of the treasury, legate of the deified Augustus and of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, proconsul of the province of Narbonensis.
EDCS-17300243.summary: This is a career summary inscription for Manius Vibius Balbinus, detailing his military and political offices under Augustus and Tiberius, likely from the early 1st century CE.

EDCS-17300244.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Ambivius Lupercus and Numitoria Cypare, parents. Lucius Ambivius Traiensis, most dutiful son, dedicated this.
EDCS-17300244.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Ambivius Traiensis to his parents, Lucius Ambivius Lupercus and Numitoria Cypare, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300246.translation: To the departed spirits. To Titus Laticius Zenon, scribe and veteran. He served 20 years, lived 50 years. Claudia Appis made this for a well-deserving recipient.
EDCS-17300246.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Claudia Appis for Titus Laticius Zenon, a scribe and veteran, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300247.translation: To Pontia Euplia, my most beloved wife, a woman of the highest standing, Valerius Sabinianus, a man of the highest rank, retired from the emperor's retinue, erected this memorial from the foundations in recognition of her merit.
EDCS-17300247.summary: A funerary memorial erected by Valerius Sabinianus for his wife, Pontia Euplia.

EDCS-17300249.summary: This fragment of an inscription mentions an individual who held the position of prefect.

EDCS-17300250.translation: Lucretia Sabina, daughter of Marcus, made the pipes for bringing water to her mistress, at her own expense.
EDCS-17300250.summary: A dedication by Lucretia Sabina for the construction of water pipes, funded by herself, for her mistress.

EDCS-17300251.translation: To Lucius Naevius Fronton, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, patron of the municipality and of the guilds: the guild of fabric workers and the guild of weavers.
EDCS-17300251.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Naevius Fronton, a patron, by the guilds of fabric workers and weavers.

EDCS-17300253.translation: Manius Vibius, one of the four Augustales, Emperor.
EDCS-17300253.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Manius Vibius, identified as one of the four Augustales, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-17300257.translation: Quintus Sertorius Antiochus, freedman of Quintus, was a poor farmer but accepted his impending death with a calm spirit; Balbus, freedman of Antiochus, Sertoria Europa, freedwoman of Quintus, and Helena, freedwoman of Lucius Asprenas, sister of Balbus, [left this] 16 feet in the field in front and 14 feet in width.
EDCS-17300257.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial plot size and bequeathing a space for Balbus, Sertoria Europa, and Helena by Quintus Sertorius Antiochus, who faced death with equanimity.

EDCS-17300258.translation: The bones of Musa, freedwoman of Quintus Aconius, son of Titus, are placed here.
EDCS-17300258.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Musa, a freedwoman, indicating the placement of her remains.

EDCS-17300259.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Aufidia Callichore, freedwoman of Gaius. Gaius Aufidius Festus, freedman of Gaius, [erected this] for his most devoted mother, well-deserving.
EDCS-17300259.summary: A tombstone set up by Gaius Aufidius Festus for his mother, Aufidia Callichore.

EDCS-17300260.translation: To Marcus, son of Marcus, grandson of Titus, Augus[...]
EDCS-17300260.summary: This inscription fragment appears to be a dedication or funerary text, mentioning a Marcus and his lineage.

EDCS-17300261.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Copona Ianuaria, for her incomparable husband Baebius Proculus, who deserved well. [She] placed [this].
EDCS-17300261.summary: A tombstone dedicated by Copona Ianuaria to her husband, Baebius Proculus.

EDCS-17300262.translation: Quintus Fabius Abinnaeus, Quintus Fabius, freedman of Marius, Atellia Prisca, daughter of Lucius, her freedwoman Fabia Felicula.
EDCS-17300262.summary: A list of names, possibly family members or fellow freedmen, associated with Quintus Fabius Abinnaeus.

EDCS-17300263.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Faustina, slave of Quintus Rammius Martialis. Felix made [this] in her own name and that of her brother Priscianus. For her most devoted mother. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17300263.summary: A tombstone erected by Felix for her mother Faustina and her brother Priscianus.

EDCS-17300264.summary: An inscription identifying Hiberus as a freedman of the emperor.

EDCS-17300265.translation: To the dearest Horatia Laeta, who deserved well.
EDCS-17300265.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Horatia Laeta for her merits.

EDCS-17300266.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph for Pomponia.

EDCS-17300267.translation: Agathemeris, fellow freedwoman, made this for herself and for her freedman Protas, son of Marcus, of Titus's line.
EDCS-17300267.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Agathemeris for herself and her freedman Protas.

EDCS-17300268.translation: Lucius Pupius, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300268.summary: This inscription likely records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Pupius, possibly for a legal or civic purpose.

EDCS-17300269.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Sabina, described as a deserving mother.

EDCS-17300270.translation: Lucius Statius Priscus, freedman of Lucius, [erected this] at his own expense for his mother Statia Clara and his brother Gaius Gavius Priscus.
EDCS-17300270.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Statius Priscus for his mother and brother.

EDCS-17300271.translation: To Gaius Tuccius Salvius, freedman of Gaius; to Tuccia Chrysaris, freedwoman of Gaius; to Gaius Tuccius Adrastus, freedman of Gaius; to Gaius Tuccius Lucrio, freedman of Gaius; Gaius Tuccius Helius, freedman of a woman; Gaius Tuccius Cnismus, freedman.
EDCS-17300271.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring multiple freedmen of the Tuccius family.

EDCS-17300274.translation: Son of Marcus Test[...]; and Hi[...]
EDCS-17300274.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning a son of Marcus and the beginning of another name.

EDCS-17300277.summary: This inscription mentions two individuals, Terebius and Vibolenus, identified as Magisterei, likely holding a priestly or official role.

EDCS-17300278.translation: Lucius Volusius Saturninus, son of Quintus, had it made by order of the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine [Augustus], pontifex maximus, father of the country, in his twentieth year of tribunician power.
EDCS-17300278.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument, ordered by Emperor Augustus and overseen by Lucius Volusius Saturninus, during Augustus's twentieth year of tribunician power.

EDCS-17300280.translation: To the deified Valerianus Caesar, by public decree of the decurions of Cingulum.
EDCS-17300280.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to the deified Emperor Valerianus Caesar by the town council of Cingulum.

EDCS-17300281.translation: To Publius Licinius Cornelius Saloninus, most noble Caesar, by public decree of the decurions of Cingulum.
EDCS-17300281.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Caesar Publius Licinius Cornelius Saloninus by the town council of Cingulum.

EDCS-17300282.translation: The council of Cingulanum decreed that this should be erected for Flavius Fortunius, most devoted man, worthy patron of the palace, on account of his distinguished merits, on the sixth day before the Ides of October, when Mamertinus and Nevitta were consuls.
EDCS-17300282.summary: This is a public decree from the town council of Cingulanum, honoring Flavius Fortunius for his merits and service, dated to 362 CE.

EDCS-17300283.translation: Atriena Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for Gnaeus Ampudius Auctus Dyrrachinus, a duovir of the Cingulani.
EDCS-17300283.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Atriena Secunda for Gnaeus Ampudius Auctus Dyrrachinus, a local magistrate.

EDCS-17300284.translation: Phiale, freedwoman, made this from her own funds for Marcus Cernitius Pollio, son of Marcus, of the Velina tribe, twice duovir and Augustalis, and for his concubine Cernitia Nimphini, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-17300284.summary: This funerary inscription, funded by a freedwoman, honors her partner, Marcus Cernitius Pollio, a local magistrate, and his concubine.

EDCS-17300285.translation: Publius Septimius [...], son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, a sexvir, for himself and for his descendants.
EDCS-17300285.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Septimius, a sexvir, for himself and his family.

EDCS-17300287.translation: Atriena Callista, freedwoman of Gaius, for herself and for Marcus Pacuvius...
EDCS-17300287.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Atriena Callista for herself and Marcus Pacuvius, likely a relative or partner.

EDCS-17300288.translation: He erected this for his son Cingulanus, for Euander and his wife, and for his son.
EDCS-17300288.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the erection of a monument for several family members, including Cingulanus, Euander, and others.

EDCS-17300289.translation: Clodius Trophimus for his most holy wife Clodia Vitalis and for himself.
EDCS-17300289.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Clodius Trophimus for his wife and himself.

EDCS-17300290.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Freia Paulina, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-17300290.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Freia Paulina.

EDCS-17300291.translation: To Gaius Romatius Manius, son of Spurius, patron.
EDCS-17300291.summary: This is a dedication to a patron named Gaius Romatius Manius, son of Spurius.

EDCS-17300292.translation: For Sabina Thalea, freedwoman of Quintus. Quintus Sabinus Corinthus.
EDCS-17300292.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Sabina Thalea, set up by Quintus Sabinus Corinthus.

EDCS-17300293.translation: A plot of land, in front 11 feet, belonging to Tullius Eutactus and Ampudia Bassa.
EDCS-17300293.summary: This inscription records the dimensions and ownership of a plot of land.

EDCS-17300294.summary: This inscription begins with the name Publius Vibius, but the text is incomplete.

EDCS-17300297.translation: Vibius Avilios, son of Vibius; Vibius Alfienos, son of Poblius, from the village of Veheia.
EDCS-17300297.summary: This inscription records the names and filiation of Vibius Avilios and Vibius Alfienos, who are associated with the village of Veheia.

EDCS-17300298.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 12th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country. The alimentary children of Cuprenses Montani.
EDCS-17300298.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from the alimentary children of Cuprenses Montani, dating to his 12th tribunician power and 2nd acclamation as imperator.

EDCS-17300301.summary: This inscription is a dedication or reference to Emperor Gaius Caesar Augustus.

EDCS-17300302.translation: [...] in judging lawsuits, with a broad-bordered toga [...]. Lucius Vo[...]
EDCS-17300302.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to relate to legal proceedings and a magistracy, possibly mentioning Lucius Vo[...] and the use of the laticlavus.

EDCS-17300304.translation: [...] Augustus, twice holder of the Augustan priesthood(?), lived(?). To [...], mother. [...]rius, freedman helper of the scribe. [...]
EDCS-17300304.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription potentially for a mother, mentioning a freedman helper of a scribe and a possible Augustalis priesthood.

EDCS-17300305.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For [...]ario Saturnino, aedile of the Cuprenses, Rasinia Sucundina [to her father(?)]
EDCS-17300305.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Saturninus, an aedile of Cupra, set up by Rasinia Sucundina.

EDCS-17300309.summary: This is a fragmented inscription recording merit, possibly a dedication or honor for Decimus C[...].

EDCS-17300312.translation: Lucius Plotius Crusta, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300312.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Plotius Crusta.

EDCS-17300328.translation: Sacred to the college of gods; Lucius Tusidius Num willingly gave this gift.
EDCS-17300328.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the college of gods by Lucius Tusidius Num.

EDCS-17300329.translation: To Hercules Compotus; Lucius Masuvius Bassus gave a gift.
EDCS-17300329.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Hercules Compotus by Lucius Masuvius Bassus.

EDCS-17300330.translation: Marcus Fadius Tuliu, freedman of Marcus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for AC.
EDCS-17300330.summary: This inscription records Marcus Fadius Tuliu, a freedman, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-17300332.translation: Dionysius, freedman of Lucius Crasicinus, a woman.
EDCS-17300332.summary: This inscription identifies Dionysius as the freedman of a woman named Lucius Crasicinus.

EDCS-17300333.translation: Quintus Feronius Clemens, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe, Corn[...
EDCS-17300333.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Quintus Feronius Clemens, son of Quintus.

EDCS-17300335.translation: Innocentius, who lived 13 years and 10 months, was buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of September, in the 3rd indiction.
EDCS-17300335.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Innocentius, recording his lifespan and date of burial, likely from the late Roman Empire due to the indiction system.

EDCS-17300339.translation: Lucius Tettius Alypus gives a gift to Jupiter.
EDCS-17300339.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Lucius Tettius Alypus to Jupiter.

EDCS-17300340.translation: Sacred to the divine spirit of Mercury. Publius Licinius Saturninus made this at his own expense.
EDCS-17300340.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury made by Publius Licinius Saturninus at his own expense.

EDCS-17300342.text_edition: \n Nymphis Geminis sacrum Caius Fufius Gemini libertus Politicus idem aquam perduxit\n
EDCS-17300342.translation: Sacred to the Gemini Nymphs. Gaius Fufius Politus, freedman of Gemini, brought the water.
EDCS-17300342.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Gemini Nymphs and states that Gaius Fufius Politus brought water.

EDCS-17300344.text_edition: \n Divos sic Traianus Augustus concessa Tuscili Nominati hereditate rei publicae Ricinensium balneum et platias sic reparari mandavit\n
EDCS-17300344.translation: The deified Trajan Augustus, by the granted inheritance of Tuscilius Nominatus, ordered the bathhouse and porticoes of the community of Ricinium to be repaired in this way.
EDCS-17300344.summary: An imperial order, likely from the reign of Trajan (98-117 CE), regarding the repair of public buildings in Ricinium, funded by a private inheritance.

EDCS-17300346.translation: To Lucius Cirpinius, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, first centurion, second time, prefect of the 22nd legion, second time as duovir, for the fifth year. From the townspeople.
EDCS-17300346.summary: A dedication by the local community to Lucius Cirpinius, a high-ranking military officer and local magistrate, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300347.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Dasiae Verae Marcus Demetrius Epictetus miles classis praetoriae Ravennatis coniugi \n
EDCS-17300347.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Demetrius Epictetus, a soldier of the praetorian fleet at Ravenna, for his wife Dasia Vera.
EDCS-17300347.summary: A tombstone inscription for Dasia Vera, set up by her husband Marcus Demetrius Epictetus, a soldier in the Roman navy, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300348.translation: Caius Aelanius Atam, freedman of Caius, from the colony of Ricinium, according to the will and by the arbitration of Octavia, a freedwoman, Acma.
EDCS-17300348.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a legal disposition or property transfer related to Caius Aelanius Atam and Octavia, associated with the colony of Ricinium.

EDCS-17300349.translation: Publius Cincius, son of Publius, [ Freed ]man, Sextumvir [ ] from the will of Ap...
EDCS-17300349.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording the dedication of a monument or public office by Publius Cincius, as stipulated in a will, possibly from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-17300350.translation: Quintus Lucilius Charinus, a sagarius (maker of sacks) from Milan, one of the six priests of Milan, for himself and for Quintus Sulpicius Celadus, his friend. In front 12 feet, in the field 14 feet.
EDCS-17300350.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Lucilius Charinus and his friend Quintus Sulpicius Celadus, specifying the dimensions of the plot, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300351.translation: To Lucius Naevius Theomede, freedman of Lucius, a sexvir; to Naevia Flora, freedwoman of Lucius, his concubine; to Lucius Naevius Anterotus, freedman, a sexvir; to Maetennia Chrestine, freedwoman of Lucius (a woman), wife of Anteros, freedman.
EDCS-17300351.summary: A funerary inscription for several freedmen and freedwomen, including a couple and their family members, who held the office of sexvir, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300352.translation: Titus Publilius Longus (father) and Annia Publilia (mother) had this made for their dearest son, Gaius Publilius Longus, master of the guild of craftsmen.
EDCS-17300352.summary: A tombstone erected by parents for their deceased son, who held a position of leadership in the local craftsmen's guild, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300353.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the base of a statue or monument, identifying the Helvia Ricina colony and possibly naming a person named Pertinax.

EDCS-17300357.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ephyris [erected this for] her parents, Gaius Annius Zopyrus, freedman of Gaius, and Annia Felice, freedwoman of Gaius, and for Gaius Annius Saturninus, her patron.
EDCS-17300357.summary: A funerary inscription honoring parents and a patron, set up by a woman named Ephyris, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300358.translation: To the departed spirits, Asclepiades, beloved...
EDCS-17300358.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment dedicated to Asclepiades, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300359.translation: To Aurelia Marinnana, who lived 52 years, 3 months, and 21 days, his dearest wife. Aurelius Posforus [her husband] and Valeria Mart[i]... [to] his mother... D...
EDCS-17300359.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription for Aurelia Marinnana, providing her age at death and mentioning her husband and mother, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300360.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Tusidius Cyrus made this monument for his worthy wife Cassia Orestina, chaste, for her merits, for her simple and grateful heart.
EDCS-17300360.summary: A tombstone erected by Tusidius Cyrus for his wife Cassia Orestina, praising her virtues, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300361.translation: Cincius, son of Publius, according to the will of Titus Vib...
EDCS-17300361.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription concerning a bequest or inheritance, initiated by Cincius according to the will of Titus Vibius.

EDCS-17300362.translation: Publius Trebius, son of Gracchus, from the Claudian tribe, purchased by his own money. Salvius and Hilarius erected this monument.
EDCS-17300362.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Salvius and Hilarius for Publius Trebius.

EDCS-17300363.translation: To Tiberius Clodius, freedman of Pupa, Ballaeus.
EDCS-17300363.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Tiberius Clodius, freedman of Pupa, named Ballaeus.

EDCS-17300364.translation: To the well-deserving freedman Clodianus, and Primitius, freedman of Augustus, [---]adio, Magnilla [---]ia, his wife, made this.
EDCS-17300364.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman named Clodianus and Primitius, erected by their wife Magnilla.

EDCS-17300365.translation: To our most sweet son Lucius Decimius, who lived 11 years, 2 months, and 22 days; from Decimia Theodorete his mother and Decimius Facilis his grandfather.
EDCS-17300365.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Decimius, erected by his mother and grandfather, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-17300366.translation: To the parent of Epicarinus, son of Pennia, and her daughters.
EDCS-17300366.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring the parent of Epicarinus and his daughters, likely a mother.

EDCS-17300367.translation: To the departed spirits, to Fortunatus, my well-deserving husband, Flavia Secunda.
EDCS-17300367.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, dedicated by his wife Flavia Secunda.

EDCS-17300369.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Geneia Successa, dearest daughter, who lived 11 years and 30 days. This unfortunate father erected this for his dutiful daughter, who deserved it, and a mother, who joined in similar tears, to adorn the tomb. Death prematurely caused the father to do what the daughter should have done for her father, who deserved well.
EDCS-17300369.summary: This is a tombstone erected by a father and mother for their beloved daughter, Geneia Successa, who died at a young age.

EDCS-17300370.translation: To Lusi(s)tratus, dearest daughter. Titus Simnius Felix and Tusidia Gemella, deserving well.
EDCS-17300370.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lusi(s)tratus, daughter of Titus Simnius Felix and Tusidia Gemella.

EDCS-17300371.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Verginius to his dearest Magia Vitalis.
EDCS-17300371.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Verginius for his wife, Magia Vitalis.

EDCS-17300372.translation: [To] Publius No[---], Nonia [---]. To Gaius Baebius [---]. Marcus Mura[---]. Marcus Mura[---].
EDCS-17300372.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording names and possibly relationships or dedications.

EDCS-17300373.translation: Marcus Numicius, son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300373.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Marcus Numicius by his name, filiation, and tribe.

EDCS-17300374.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Octavia Primitiva, who lived 22 years, 11 months, and 27 days. Aeneas to his deserving wife.
EDCS-17300374.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia Primitiva, erected by her husband Aeneas.

EDCS-17300375.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Petrusidius Secundus to his wife Sapsa Mirtale, with whom he lived for 21 years, and to his deserving father, Quinto Petrusidio Ianuario.
EDCS-17300375.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Petrusidius Secundus to his wife Sapsa Mirtale and his father Quinto Petrusidio Ianuario.

EDCS-17300376.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publicius Sabinus erected this for his deserving wife, Petrusidia Cervilla.
EDCS-17300376.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Publicius Sabinus for his wife, Petrusidia Cervilla.

EDCS-17300377.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus Quintilius Primitivus to his most beloved son, Sextus Quintilius Praxiteles.
EDCS-17300377.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Sextus Quintilius Primitivus for his son, Sextus Quintilius Praxiteles.

EDCS-17300378.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Marcus Tedius Sabinus. Decimia Sabina to her unbearable husband, with whom she lived 30 years, deserving well.
EDCS-17300378.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Decimia Sabina to her husband Marcus Tedius Sabinus, with whom she lived for 30 years.

EDCS-17300379.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Lucius Tusidius Campester.

EDCS-17300380.translation: Lucius Tusidius Faventinus and Vettia Rufina to their most beloved son, Tusidius Iucundus, well-deserving.
EDCS-17300380.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Lucius Tusidius Faventinus and Vettia Rufina for their son, Tusidius Iucundus.

EDCS-17300381.translation: [To the Spirits of the Departed.] To Vettius Ianuarius. Vettius Ianuarius and Veiena Tyche to their most dutiful son.
EDCS-17300381.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Vettius Ianuarius and Veiena Tyche for their son, Vettius Ianuarius.

EDCS-17300382.translation: Petrus Vettienus, son of Publius, from the Velina tribe, to Celerius.
EDCS-17300382.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Petrus Vettienus, son of Publius, from the Velina tribe, to Celerius.

EDCS-17300392.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Antonia Terpsicore and Carinus, most miserable parents, to their most dutiful son, Marcus Antonius Earinos, son of Marcus, and to his spirit.
EDCS-17300392.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from parents Antonia Terpsicore and Carinus for their son, Marcus Antonius Earinos.

EDCS-17300393.translation: To Quintus Attius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe. Quintus [---]. Publius Attius [---] according to the testament.
EDCS-17300393.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quintus Attius Rufus, likely a funerary monument, with a partial record of the dedicator and the terms of the will.

EDCS-17300394.translation: To the memory of Caius Fadenus Secundinus, who lived 36 years. Fadenus Epictetus made this for his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-17300394.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fadenus Secundinus, erected by his brother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300395.translation: To the Divine Shades. Flavia Proba. Parents and her husband [dedicated this].
EDCS-17300395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Proba, dedicated by her parents and husband, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300396.translation: To Helvia Nymphe, freedwoman of Caius. She lived 22 years. Her father, Quintus Helvius Suavis.
EDCS-17300396.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Quintus Helvius Suavis for his freedwoman, Helvia Nymphe.

EDCS-17300397.translation: Titus Pontilius [---], of the Velina tribe, Venal[---] [
EDCS-17300397.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or epitaph for Titus Pontilius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300398.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vettius Modestus and Memmia Rhodine to their dearest son, Publi Vettius Modestus, who lived 11 years, 10 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-17300398.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from Vettius Modestus and Memmia Rhodine for their son, Publi Vettius Modestus.

EDCS-17300399.translation: To Volcacia Potestas, freedwoman of Marcus. Marcus Volcacius Primio and Marcus Volcacius Donatus, freedmen, and Volcacia Nymphe, freedwoman, and the heir(s) dedicated this.
EDCS-17300399.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by freedmen and heirs to Volcacia Potestas, a freedwoman, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300401.translation: Maxima, daughter of Nasia and Cnaeus, dedicates this to Apollo.
EDCS-17300401.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Maxima to the god Apollo.

EDCS-17300402.text_edition: \n RIOR vici Cluentensis vetustate dilapsum us Rufinus et Iustus inpendio sua recuraverunt\n
EDCS-17300402.translation: Rufinus and Justus repaired the Rior of the Cluentian district, which had fallen into ruin from age, at their own expense.
EDCS-17300402.summary: This inscription records the repair of a public structure, the Rior of the Cluentian district, by Rufinus and Justus, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300403.translation: To Publius, son of Publius. Laecania Martina [dedicated this].
EDCS-17300403.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication to Publius, son of Publius, possibly by Laecania Martina, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300404.translation: Gaius Sentidius Saturninus placed this here for me; my death grieved him.
EDCS-17300404.summary: This epitaph records a person named Gaius Sentidius Saturninus who erected a monument for himself because his own death caused sorrow.

EDCS-17300406.translation: Gaius Lucilius Vindex, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, a soldier of the VI Praetorian cohort, lived 30 years and served 12 years, first as a principalis and beneficiarius of a tribune, then as an optio in a centuria. He ordered this to be made by his will, for the sake of honor and duty, and [dedicated] 2,000 sesterces for his father Gaius Lucilius Secundus, and mother Lore[---], and [---] his grandmother, as a prelegacy.
EDCS-17300406.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a will, setting aside funds for relatives, for Gaius Lucilius Vindex, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300407.translation: To the Divine Shades and to the memory of [---] Quietus, son of [---], of the Velina tribe. His father Quietus, of the Velina tribe, and mother made [this] for their dearest son. The site was granted by decree of the decurions of Potentia.
EDCS-17300407.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a son, dedicated by his parents, with the land granted by local authorities, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300409.translation: Marcus Juventius Paulinus made this for his kinsman Gaius Julius Candidus and for his wife Viria Marcella, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-17300409.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Marcus Juventius Paulinus for his relatives Gaius Julius Candidus and Viria Marcella.

EDCS-17300410.translation: Vettiena Cervia made this monument for her son Titus Annio Expectato, most dutiful, aged 16 years, 6 months, and 7 days, which was not permitted by fate. Whoever commits an offense against this plot of land and its shrine, may he suffer such days as I did on the third day before the Nones of June. Malice is absent.
EDCS-17300410.summary: This is a funerary inscription and a curse against those who would disturb the grave, for Vettiena Cervia's son Titus Annio Expectato, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17300412.text_edition: \n Caius Fufius Geminus VIIvir epulonum quaestor Tiberi Caesaris Augusti tribunus plebis designatus patronus coloniae\n
EDCS-17300412.translation: Gaius Fufius Geminus, member of the board of priests for banquets, quaestor to Tiberius Caesar Augustus, tribune of the plebs-elect, patron of the colony.
EDCS-17300412.summary: This inscription lists the career of Gaius Fufius Geminus, a Roman official, likely for a public monument.

EDCS-17300414.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld: Primigenius for his comrade Moschidus and Gaius Cusinius Cyphaerus for his well-deserving [relative/friend].
EDCS-17300414.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes, likely from a tomb, honoring Moschidus and Gaius Cusinius Cyphaerus.

EDCS-17300415.summary: This fragment of an inscription honors a patron named Stephanion.

EDCS-17300416.translation: Hail, Athamania Aristhomace, freedwoman of Quintus Veturtius, son of Titus.
EDCS-17300416.summary: This is a greeting inscribed for Athamania Aristhomace, a freedwoman of Quintus Veturtius.

EDCS-17300417.translation: For his son Publius, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300417.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication or epitaph for a man named Publius, son of [---], from the Velina tribe.

EDCS-17300420.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius and Hygieia. Gaius Oppius Leonas, freedman of Gaius, a vigintivir and Augustalis, honored in the Claudia tribe among the seniors and juniors, clients and new arrivals, has given this gift to his most respected fellow citizens, on the occasion of whose dedication he gave 3 denarii to each decurion and 2 denarii to the Augustales, and a dinner to the colonists. The place was granted by decree of the decurions. Dedicated on the Ides of January, when Plautius Quintillus and Stator Priscus were consuls.
EDCS-17300420.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Oppius Leonas to Aesculapius and Hygieia, including a substantial distribution of money and a dinner to local officials and colonists.

EDCS-17300421.translation: To Jupiter, the Sun, Serapis. To Zeus, Helios, Serapis. Gaius Oppius Irenion willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17300421.summary: This bilingual inscription records a votive offering by Gaius Oppius Irenion to a syncretic triad of deities.

EDCS-17300423.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 17th time, consul for the 3rd time, son of the divine Antoninus Pius, grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva. By the people of Auxima.
EDCS-17300423.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely on a monument, establishing his imperial titulature and referencing the dedicator as the people of Auxima.

EDCS-17300424.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, son of the divine Antoninus Pius, grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva. By the people of Auxima.
EDCS-17300424.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely on a monument, establishing his imperial titulature and referencing the dedicator as the people of Auxima.

EDCS-17300425.translation: To Lucius Aurelius Marcianus, freedman of the emperor, an official in charge of receipts. By the people of Auxima, by decree of the decurions. Marcus, freedman of the emperor, procurator, father, remitted the expense upon accepting the honor. On the occasion of whose dedication he distributed 3 denarii to the decurions and 2 denarii to the colonists.
EDCS-17300425.summary: This inscription records a public honor granted by the people of Auxima to Lucius Aurelius Marcianus, an imperial freedman, including a financial distribution upon dedication.

EDCS-17300427.translation: To Gaius Julius Oppius Clemens, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, decemvir for judging lawsuits, military tribune with broad stripe in the IV Flavia Felix legion, quaestor of the province of Baetica, candidate for tribune of the plebs of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus, candidate for praetor of the same emperor, patron of the colony. By the colonists.
EDCS-17300427.summary: This is a dedication by the colonists of a town to their patron, Gaius Julius Oppius Clemens, listing his significant public and military career.

EDCS-17300428.translation: To Marcus Oppius Capito, son of Quintus, grandson of Titus, great-grandson of Titus, of the Velina tribe, Milasius, Aninius Severus, who held the public horse, was a selected judge from five decades, prefect of the armorers, quinquennial priest twice, quaestor four times, patron of the colony and patron of the colony of Aesis and of the municipality of Numanatium, also quinquennial. By the colonists, on account of his merits. In honor of whose dedication he gave a dinner to the colonists. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17300428.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Oppius Capito, a prominent local figure and patron, detailing his offices and specifying a dinner for colonists upon dedication.

EDCS-17300429.translation: To Marcus Oppius Capito, son of Quintus, grandson of Titus, great-grandson of Titus, of the Velina tribe, Aninius Severus, who held the public horse, was a selected judge from five decades, tribune of the VIII Augusta legion, prefect of the armorers, patron of the colony of Auxima and the colony of Aesis and the municipality of Numanatium. By the council and the people of Trebula, patron of the municipality, curator appointed by the Emperor Antoninus Augustus. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17300429.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Oppius Capito as patron of multiple communities, listing his civic and military roles and noting his appointment as curator by Emperor Antoninus Augustus.

EDCS-17300430.translation: To Gaius Oppius Sabinus Iulius Nepos, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, to Manius Vibius Sollemnis Severus, consul, admitted by the most sacred Emperor Hadrian Augustus among the tribunes, peregrine praetor, candidate of Augustus, legate of the province of Baetica, curator of the roads Clodia, Annia, Cassia, Cimina, of the three Trajan roads, and Amerina, legate of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, legate of the emperor with proconsular power in the province of Lusitania, proconsul of the province of Baetica, patron of the colony. By Leonas, freedman, who was admitted as patron. And on the dedication of the statue, he gave a dinner to the colonists.
EDCS-17300430.summary: This long inscription details the extensive senatorial career of Manius Vibius Sollemnis Severus, who served in various high administrative and military posts, and was honored as patron of the colony by his freedman Leonas.

EDCS-17300431.translation: To Gaius Plautius Rufus, son of Gaius, propraetorian legate, for defending the province of Sicily.
EDCS-17300431.summary: A dedication to Gaius Plautius Rufus, a propraetorian legate, for his defense of the province of Sicily.

EDCS-17300432.translation: To Quintus Plotus Maximus of the Collina tribe, son of Trebellius Pelidianus, Roman knight, tribune of the II Traiana Fortis legion, tribune of the XXXII cohort of volunteers, tribune of the VI Victrix legion, procurator of Augustus, acting deputy of the 20% inheritance tax, prefect of the imperial transport service, quinquennial patron and priest of the city; from the guild of metalworkers of Auximum, for his exceptional love among their fellow citizens.
EDCS-17300432.summary: A dedication by the guild of metalworkers of Auximum to Quintus Plotus Maximus, honoring his love for his fellow citizens and listing his extensive military and administrative career, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300433.translation: To Quintus Plotus Maximus of the Collina tribe, son of Trebellius Pelidianus, Roman knight, tribune of the II Traiana Fortis legion, tribune of the XXXII cohort of volunteers, tribune of the VI Victrix legion, procurator of Augustus, acting deputy of the 20% inheritance tax, prefect of the imperial transport service, quinquennial patron and priest of the city; from the guild of carpet-makers of Auximum, for his exceptional love among their fellow citizens.
EDCS-17300433.summary: A dedication by the guild of carpet-makers of Auximum to Quintus Plotus Maximus, honoring his love for his fellow citizens and detailing his extensive military and administrative career, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300434.translation: To Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, son of Gnaeus, commander, consul for the third time, as patron, publicly.
EDCS-17300434.summary: This is a public dedication to Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, honoring his consulships and his role as patron.

EDCS-17300436.translation: Dedicated on the sixth day before the Kalends of July, during the consulship of Lucius Aelius Caesar (II) and Publius Coelius Balbinus. To Gaius Oppius Bassus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, patron of the colony, praetor, centurion of the IIII Flavia Felix legion, evocatus of Augustus in the office of the forum, deputy of the praetorian prefect, signifer, optio, tessararius of the II Praetorian cohort, soldier in the XIIII and XIII urban cohorts; from the guild of carpet-makers of Auximum, patron, for his merits.
EDCS-17300436.summary: A dedication by the guild of carpet-makers of Auximum to Gaius Oppius Bassus, honoring his military and civic merits, with the date placed in the consulship of Aelius Caesar and Coelius Balbinus, likely early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300437.translation: To Gaius Oppius Bassus, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, former first spear (primus pilus), patron of the colony, praetor with judicial authority in Auximum, centurion of the IIII Flavia Felix legion and the II Traiana Fortis legion, evocatus of Augustus in the office of the forum, deputy of the praetorian prefects, soldier in the II Praetorian cohort and the XIII and XIIII urban cohorts, who served in all offices under his caligae. From the centurions of the II Traiana Fortis legion, to their best and most worthy comrade, who on the occasion of its dedication gave a dinner to the colonists.
EDCS-17300437.summary: A dedication by the centurions of the II Traiana Fortis legion to Gaius Oppius Bassus, honoring his distinguished military career and generosity, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300438.translation: To Lucius Praesentius Paetus, son of Lucius, of the Lemonia tribe, also called Lattius Severus, prefect of the I cohort of Africans (citizens of Rome, equestrian), select judge from five centuries, praetor of Auximum, patron of the colony, aedile, and twice duovir of Ancona; by Vibia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, priestess of the Augustae, for her husband, who deserved well of her in all examples and who, at the dedication of the statue, gave a dinner to the colonists and a feast to the people.
EDCS-17300438.summary: A dedication by Vibia Marcella to her husband Lucius Praesentius Paetus, honoring his public service in Auximum and Ancona and his generosity, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300439.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Publicius Apronianus, former first spear (primus pilus), patron of the municipality of Ricinium, [aedile]; Lucius Publicius Florianus, tribune of the VIIII cohort.
EDCS-17300439.summary: A tombstone inscription for Lucius Publicius Apronianus and Lucius Publicius Florianus, noting their military and civic roles, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300440.translation: To Titus Salenus Sedatus, son of Titus, of the Velina tribe, a veteran of the Augusti who received an honorable discharge from the XIIII urban cohort, quinquennial praetor, quaestor of the public treasury of Auximum, patron of the guild of carpet-makers of Mansueta, his freedwoman, to their best patron, who on the occasion of its dedication gave 8 sesterces to each decurion and 4 sesterces to each colonist.
EDCS-17300440.summary: A dedication by the freedwoman Mansueta to her patron Titus Salenus Sedatus, a veteran and civic official of Auximum, honoring his generosity to the decurions and colonists, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300441.translation: Numerius Turcius Rufus, son of Gaius, of the Sergia tribe, a praetorian; his wife Cocceia Italia, freedwoman of Marcus; by Gaius Turcius Rufus, son of Numerius, of the Sergia tribe, in accordance with the will of Numerius Turcius, son of Gaius, of the Sergia tribe, under the supervision of his wife Cocceia Italia.
EDCS-17300441.summary: A funerary inscription establishing the burial arrangements for Numerius Turcius Rufus and his wife Cocceia Italia, based on the will of Numerius Turcius, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300442.translation: [...]ius, tribune of soldiers, twice prefect of the guild, praetor for public affairs, left 50,000 sesterces and the estate of Hermedianum, [and two estates] Herenniana, from the income of which each year a victim should be provided and sacrificed to the Augustan Fides.
EDCS-17300442.summary: A testamentary inscription detailing a bequest of funds and property to provide for an annual sacrifice to Fides Augusta, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17300443.translation: Gaius Baianius Auctus, son of Gaius, freedman; Saufeia Eucumene, freedwoman of a woman; Gaius Baianius Faustus, son of Gaius, freedman.
EDCS-17300443.summary: This epitaph lists three individuals, likely freedmen and their patron, with no further context about their lives or deaths, probably dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300444.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Numerius Fresidius Successus lived 14 years, by decree of the guild of artisans. His father Numerius Fresidius Florentinus and mother Fresidia Successa.
EDCS-17300444.summary: This is a tombstone for a young boy named Numerius Fresidius Successus, who died at age 14, set up by his parents and mentioning his membership in the guild of artisans, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300446.translation: To Gaius Oppius Pallantius, son of Gaius, of the Velina tribe, former praetor and quaestor of Auximum; the same was quaestor of the grain supply. Oppia Prisca, his mother, to her dearest son. The burial place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17300446.summary: This funerary monument honors Gaius Oppius Pallantius, a former praetor and quaestor, with his mother dedicating the burial place granted by a decree of the local council, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300447.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Lucius Praesentius Florus, freedman of Lucius, a six-man official and Augustalis. Lucius Praesentius Aprio, freedman of Lucius, to his deserving friend.
EDCS-17300447.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to Lucius Praesentius Florus by his friend Lucius Praesentius Aprio, a fellow freedman and member of the VIvirate and Augustales, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300448.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Titus Tamudius Eglectus, freedman of Titus, a colonist of Auximum. He lived 7 years and 30 days. Eglectus, his father, to his most devoted son.
EDCS-17300448.summary: This epitaph records the death of Titus Tamudius Eglectus, son of Eglectus, a colonist of Auximum, who died at the age of 7, with his father dedicating the monument, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300449.translation: Gaius Titus Tamudii Gemellus and Albanus [dedicated] the water at their own expense.
EDCS-17300449.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a water supply at private expense by Gaius Titus Tamudii Gemellus and Albanus, likely related to civic works, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300450.translation: To Marcus Titius, son of Lucius, of the Collina tribe, pontifex, patron of the colony, by decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-17300450.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Titius, a pontifex and patron of the colony, recognizing a public dedication by the town council, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300455.translation: To Lucius Ferioni Rufus(?), son of Lucius, of the Velina tribe, scribe. Lucius Ferioni Amphio, father, and Ammea Iocunda, mother.
EDCS-17300455.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated to Lucius Ferioni Rufus(?), a scribe, by his parents Lucius Ferioni Amphio and Ammea Iocunda, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300456.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Octavia Prisca, who lived 28 years, 5 months, and 23 days. Restutus, administrator of the grain supply, to his deserving wife.
EDCS-17300456.summary: This tombstone honors Octavia Prisca, who died at age 28, erected by her husband Restutus, an administrator of the grain supply, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300457.translation: I, Aureliana, lie here. I lived 28 years, 2 months, and 27 days. Born in the sacred city, I traveled through Italy and the provinces, and paid my debt in Nicomedia, and was brought here. My most beloved husband Euaristo, freedman of the emperor, that you travelers may know by reading of my piety and chastity with which I lived with him, that I deserved this in this sarcophagus. When my most beloved husband Euaristo shall have been lost, it shall be permitted to no one either to open or to transfer [this sarcophagus] or to do anything else from the marbles of the monument. Whoever shall do otherwise shall pay 10,000 denarii to the treasury of the public fund and 5,000 denarii to the public fund of Ricinenses.
EDCS-17300457.summary: This elaborate sarcophagus inscription by Aureliana details her life, travels, and her wishes for her burial and that of her husband Euaristo, setting penalties for violation, and indicating a date likely in the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-17300458.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Julia Sabina, freedwoman of Quintus, a doctor. Quintus Julius Atimetus to his deserving wife.
EDCS-17300458.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Julius Atimetus to his wife, Julia Sabina, who was a doctor.

EDCS-17300459.translation: Gaius Plotus Alexander, freedman of Gaius, a timber worker and craftsman.
EDCS-17300459.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Gaius Plotus Alexander as a timber worker and craftsman.

EDCS-17300460.translation: Amerimnus, slave of Abnatiaes Cypare, lived 7 years.
EDCS-17300460.summary: This epitaph records the short life of Amerimnus, a slave of Abnatiaes Cypare, who died at the age of seven.

EDCS-17300461.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld: For his well-deserving wife Appuleia Vitalina, Gaius Oppius Clemens, her husband.
EDCS-17300461.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Gaius Oppius Clemens to his wife Appuleia Vitalina.

EDCS-17300462.translation: To Lucius Aurelius, son of Marcus, of the [---] tribe.
EDCS-17300462.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a funerary dedication, for Lucius Aurelius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-17300465.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Detellius Trophimus, also called Fortunatus, made this monument for his wife Trebellia, and for himself, his freedmen and freedwomen, and their descendants, provided that no one from the family leaves it, nor shall an heir succeed to it other than those inscribed on this title.
EDCS-17300465.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Detellius Trophimus to his wife, with provisions regarding inheritance.

EDCS-17300467.translation: To the departed spirits. For Expectatus, a husband well-deserving, from Amanda, his devoted partner.
EDCS-17300467.summary: A funerary dedication to Expectatus by his devoted partner Amanda.

EDCS-17300468.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Numerius Fresidius, son of Thy melicus, most beloved, who lived 32 years, 10 months, and 20 days. Caecilia Felicitas to her most devoted son, the well-deserving.
EDCS-17300468.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caecilia Felicitas for her son, Numerius Fresidius, providing his age at death.

EDCS-17300469.translation: To the departed spirits. For Herennius Primianus, who lived 3 years, 9 months, and 27 days, from his most devoted parents, Tusidius Primus and Ciprinia Calliste.
EDCS-17300469.summary: A funerary epitaph for Herennius Primianus, detailing his short life and dedication by his parents.

EDCS-17300470.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Quintus Laetorius Proculus. Laetoria Procula to her most dutiful brother.
EDCS-17300470.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Laetoria Procula to her brother, Quintus Laetorius Proculus.

EDCS-17300471.translation: To the departed spirits. For Caius Larsi Maritimus, who lived 37 years, 10 months, and 28 days, from his mother, Cominia Luci f. Severa, to her most devoted son, well-deserving.
EDCS-17300471.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Larsi Maritimus, detailing his age and dedication by his mother.

EDCS-17300472.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Marius Primigenius rests here; he lived 28 years. From Titus Tenius Martialis and Maria Prisca, to the most worthy.
EDCS-17300472.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Marius Primigenius, stating his age and dedication by Titus Tenius Martialis and Maria Prisca.

EDCS-17300473.translation: Caius Oppius Sabinus [---]. Gaius Julius Clemens [---] lived [---] years.
EDCS-17300473.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for Gaius Oppius Sabinus and Gaius Julius Clemens, with incomplete age information.

EDCS-17300474.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Oppia Vera, daughter of Gaius. Claudius Severus to his most holy, chaste, and incomparable wife, with whom he lived 17 years, 7 months, and 26 days. She herself lived 32 years, 2 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-17300474.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Claudius Severus for his wife, Oppia Vera, detailing their married life and her age at death.

EDCS-17300475.translation: To LI, dearest son. Caius Petronius, son of Caius, and to his most rare and dearest wife, with whom he lived without offense or reproach.
EDCS-17300475.summary: A dedication by Caius Petronius to his son LI and his wife, praising their relationship.

EDCS-17300476.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Praesentius Pollux, son of Lucius. Lucius Praesentius Victor to his most devoted son, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-17300476.summary: This is a funerary epitaph by Lucius Praesentius Victor for his son, Lucius Praesentius Pollux, stating his age at death.

EDCS-17300477.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Praesentia Nereis. Lucius Praesentius Blastus to his well-deserving freedwoman and wife.
EDCS-17300477.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Praesentius Blastus to Praesentia Nereis, identified as both his freedwoman and wife.

EDCS-17300478.translation: To Caius Sacellius, son of Quintus, of the Velina tribe.
EDCS-17300478.summary: A dedication to Caius Sacellius, son of Quintus, likely indicating his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-17300479.translation: From... and Servatus to their most devoted mother.
EDCS-17300479.summary: A dedication from two individuals, possibly siblings, to their devoted mother.

EDCS-17300480.translation: To the departed spirits. For Statia Cincinnata, from Petroni Nico.
EDCS-17300480.summary: A funerary dedication to Statia Cincinnata by Petroni Nico.

EDCS-17300481.translation: Tullia Polla, daughter of Titus, ordered this to be made by her will for Veturia, daughter of Marcus, her mother.
EDCS-17300481.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Tullia Polla through her will for her mother Veturia.

EDCS-17300482.translation: To Latia Crescentina, for her well-deserving comrade.
EDCS-17300482.summary: This is a funerary dedication on a monument, likely a tomb, for a well-deserving comrade named Latia Crescentina.

EDCS-17300486.translation: [---] to the most noble Caesar Numerianus, devotedly by the public [---].
EDCS-17300486.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely dedicating something to the Caesar Numerianus, possibly by a public body.

EDCS-17300488.translation: Titus Flavius Optatus, for his own health and that of his family and colleagues, set up this votive offering to the August Nymphs.
EDCS-17300488.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Flavius Optatus dedicated to the Nymphs for the health of himself, his family, and colleagues.

EDCS-17300489.translation: Sacred to Vertumnus Augustus. Karus, the steward, paid his vow.
EDCS-17300489.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Vertumnus Augustus by Karus, likely a steward, who paid his vow.

EDCS-17300490.translation: Alexander, servant of Quintus Julius Melior, from his own property.
EDCS-17300490.summary: This inscription records a contribution made by Alexander, a servant of Quintus Julius Melior, for a monument or project, funded from his own resources.

EDCS-17300491.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-17300491.text_edition: \n Plotinae Augustae coniugi Augusti Imperatori Caesari divi Nervae filio Nervae Traiano optimo Augusto Germanico Dacico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XVIIII imperatori IX consuli VI patri patriae providentissimo principi senatus populusque Romanus quod accessum Italiae hoc etiam addito ex pecunia sua portu tutiorem navigantibus reddiderit Divae Marcianae Augustae sorori Augusti\n
EDCS-17300491.translation: To Plotina Augusta, wife of the Emperor, son of the divine Nerva, Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Optimus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 19th time, imperator for the 9th time, consul for the 6th time, father of his country, most provident prince, the Senate and the Roman People, because by adding this port, made safer for sailors, from his own funds, to the port of Italy, they have given it. To the divine Marciana Augusta, sister of the Emperor.
EDCS-17300491.summary: This is a dedication by the Senate and Roman People to Emperor Trajan, honoring his wife Plotina and sister Marciana for improving the port of Italy.

EDCS-17300494.translation: Flavius Gorgonius, a most distinguished man, formerly Count of Private Donations and Praetorian Prefect, ordered this to be made for himself.
EDCS-17300494.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument commissioned by Flavius Gorgonius, who held significant imperial administrative posts, indicating his high status.

EDCS-17300495.translation: To Petronia Sabina, daughter of Lucius Petronius Sabinus, twice first-rank centurion, procurator of the Augusti, of the department of inheritances and also of the province Narbonensis, patron of the colony. The decurions.
EDCS-17300495.summary: This is a dedication by the decurions of a colony to Petronia Sabina, daughter of a high-ranking military official and provincial procurator.

EDCS-17300497.translation: I, Flavius Evintius, veteran, well-deserving, made this tomb on my property where I may rest; if anyone violently wishes to be [here] and attempts [this] against the laws, let him forfeit one pound of gold to the treasury. By law, depart.
EDCS-17300497.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Evintius, a veteran, who established his own tomb with a strict legal warning against disturbance, including a penalty payable to the treasury.

EDCS-17300499.translation: To Gnaeus Marcius Macro, son of Sextus, of the voting tribe Quirina. Aulus Fabius Fortuitus, son of Aulus, his client.
EDCS-17300499.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, establishing a relationship of patronage between Aulus Fabius Fortuitus and Gnaeus Marcius Macro.

EDCS-17300500.translation: To Rubria, freedwoman of Titus, wife of Statia and Titus Rubrius, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Lemonia. To Varicus, patron, quaestor. To Gaius Fulvius, son of Caius, of the voting tribe Lemonia. To her husband. By the will, by the arbitration of Lucius Setrius Philodoxus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-17300500.summary: This complex funerary inscription lists multiple individuals, including a freedwoman, her husbands, a patron, and an arbiter, indicating familial and legal relationships.

EDCS-17300502.translation: While alive, they set this up for themselves for Titus Asinius Severus, the unguentarius, and for his wife Vecilia Leva.
EDCS-17300502.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a couple, Titus Asinius Severus and Vecilia Leva, who set up their own tomb while alive.

EDCS-17300503.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Beryllus Secunda and all the officials, honorably made this for Tiberius Claudius Celer, conjuror from the line of Claudius Saturninus, the departed, to a deserving person.
EDCS-17300503.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Tiberius Claudius Celer, a conjuror, by Beryllus Secunda and other officials.

EDCS-17300504.translation: Father [---]us Pudens and mother Aurelia Africana set this up for a deserving person.
EDCS-17300504.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents, [---]us Pudens and Aurelia Africana, for their deceased child.

EDCS-17300505.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aurelius Pardus, with his daughter Aurelia Secunda, arranged for this monument to be set up for his most rare wife, Aurelia Fortunata, well-deserving.
EDCS-17300505.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified dead (Dis Manibus) for Aurelia Fortunata, erected by her husband Aurelius Pardus and daughter Aurelia Secunda.

EDCS-17300506.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Benignus, who lived 1 year and 2 months, for his well-deserving son.
EDCS-17300506.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified dead (Dis Manibus) for a child named Benignus, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-17300507.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Caecilia Anconitana, his most obedient and incomparable wife, who lived 47 years and was in marriage for 30 years and 3 months. Publius Annius Severus, husband, and Annia Severa, daughter, placed this for their most dutiful mother, well-deserving of them.
EDCS-17300507.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified dead (Dis Manibus) for Caecilia Anconitana, erected by her husband and daughter, detailing her lifespan and duration of marriage.

EDCS-17300508.translation: To Caesias, daughter of Publius, Honorata.
EDCS-17300508.summary: This is a simple dedication, likely funerary, to Caesias Honorata, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-17300509.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Caius Calusius Victor, his sister Calusia Ursa and Voconius Venustus [erected this] for one who deserved well.
EDCS-17300509.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Calusius Victor, set up by his sister and another individual.

EDCS-17300510.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Calusia Ianuaria, Lucius Voconius Venustus and his sister Calusia Ursa [erected this] for one who deserved well, for one who deserved well, for one who deserved well.
EDCS-17300510.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication for Calusia Ianuaria, made by Lucius Voconius Venustus and his sister Calusia Ursa.

EDCS-17300511.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Calusia Veneria, Baebius Fileros made [this].
EDCS-17300511.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Calusia Veneria, made by Baebius Fileros.

EDCS-17300512.translation: To the good memory of Camuria Exuperia, who lived 72 years, 2 months, 10 days. Camu-
EDCS-17300512.summary: This inscription commemorates Camuria Exuperia, providing her name and age at death, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-17300513.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Clodius Donatus, Metilia Attica [erected this] for her grandfather, who deserved well.
EDCS-17300513.summary: This funerary dedication is for Clodius Donatus, set up by his granddaughter Metilia Attica.

EDCS-17300514.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Clodia Munatia, who lived 49 years and 1 day.
EDCS-17300514.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Clodia Munatia, who lived 49 years and 1 day.

EDCS-17300515.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Faustilla, who lived 27 years and 14 days, her mother Rhodine [erected this] for her most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-17300515.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Faustilla, who died at age 27, and was set up by her mother Rhodine.

EDCS-17300516.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Flavia Castricia, sweet daughter, a virgin, who lived 16 years, 5 months, and 8 days. Flaviaus Castricianus, her father, set this up. Placed on the 10th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-17300516.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Flaviaus Castricianus for his daughter Flavia Castricia, a virgin, who died at age 16.

EDCS-17300517.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Marcus Gratius Coronarius, who perished at sea by the violence of a storm, Scaefia Calliope [erected this] for her most excellent husband and for Scaefia Tertulla, her sweetest daughter, who lived 1 year and 13 days, for those who deserved well.
