EDCS-17300517.summary: This funerary monument honors Marcus Gratius Coronarius, lost at sea, and his infant daughter Scaefia Tertulla, with dedications from his wife Scaefia Calliope.

EDCS-17300518.translation: For Gaius Heiulius Alexander, freedman of Gaius, by testament and at the arbitration of Gaius Heiulius Metrodo[rus], freedman of Gaius, and Gaius Heiulius Capito, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-17300518.summary: This funerary inscription records the arrangements for the burial of Gaius Heiulius Alexander, a freedman, made through a will and arbitration.

EDCS-17300519.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Labienus Renatus, Labiena Procula [erected this] for him, her mother, for one who deserved well.
EDCS-17300519.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Labienus Renatus, made by his mother Labiena Procula.

EDCS-17300520.summary: This inscription indicates the burial of the remains of Latina Lycnidis.

EDCS-17300521.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Licustena Veneria, his most chaste wife, who lived with me for 16 years, 7 months, and 22 days. Lucius Gavius Anconitanus.
EDCS-17300521.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Gavius Anconitanus for his wife Licustena Veneria, recording their shared life of 16 years.

EDCS-17300522.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Marcia Euhemeriana, daughter of Marcus, of the Marcia family, our lady, and Proxima. Marcus Marcius, son of Marcus, her father, and Flavia Euhemerina, daughter of Quintus, her mother, deceived and bereaved by the loss of their growing flower, have built this tomb.
EDCS-17300522.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcia Euhemeriana, set up by her parents, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300523.translation: To Metrodo, his well-deserving wife. Ofellius made this.
EDCS-17300523.summary: A funerary epitaph for Metrodo, set up by her husband Ofellius, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-17300524.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Ramia Callytiche, [erected this] for her most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-17300524.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication for Ramia Callytiche, set up by her daughter.

EDCS-17300525.translation: Eight months and fifteen days. Scaepeia Calliope [erected this for her] well-deserving mother.
EDCS-17300525.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a mother, Scaepeia Calliope, dedicated by her daughter.

EDCS-17300526.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Scefeia Restuta. Scefeia Calliope, her sister, [erected this] for [her] well-deserving sister.
EDCS-17300526.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by a sister, Scefeia Calliope, to her deceased sister, Scefeia Restuta.

EDCS-17300527.translation: To the Divine Shades, sacred. For Servilia Felicissima, [his] most chaste wife.
EDCS-17300527.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Servilia Felicissima, the "most chaste wife" of an unnamed husband.

EDCS-17300528.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Sextus Truttedius Sabinus, son of Sextus Truttedius Pollia, a most sweet infant. Sextus Truttedius Clemens, his father, [erected this].
EDCS-17300528.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of an infant, Sextus Truttedius Sabinus, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-17300529.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucius Valerius Saturninus, son of Lucius, and Chreste, freedwoman of Freia, daughter of Lucius. Lucius Freius Saturninus erected [this] for his most dutiful parents, who deserved well.
EDCS-17300529.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Lucius Freius Saturninus for his parents, Lucius Valerius Saturninus and Chreste.

EDCS-17300533.translation: Imperator Titus Caesar Vespasianus Augustus, son of the deified Vespasian, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 9th time, imperator for the 15th time, consul for the 8th time, father of the country, censor. Year 142.
EDCS-17300533.summary: An inscription recording the titles and regnal years of Emperor Titus, likely from 80/81 CE.

EDCS-17300537.translation: To the Liberator of the Roman World, the restorer of liberty and the republic, the preserver of soldiers and provincials, our lord Magnentius, the Invincible Prince, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus. Flavius... [partially illegible]
EDCS-17300537.summary: A dedication to Emperor Magnentius, praising him as a restorer and preserver, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-17300538.translation: To our lords Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Maximianus, the Invincible and Most Clement Augusti, and to our lords Flavius Valerius Severus and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most noble and most blessed Caesars. To the preserver of peace and preserver of the Roman Empire, our lord Constantius Maximus, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus.
EDCS-17300538.summary: A dedication to Emperors Constantius II and his co-emperors, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-17400002.translation: Caius Turpidius Severus, son of Caius, son of Publius, of the Horatia tribe, lived 16 years. His father and mother's comfort, a joy to his friends, the promise of a boy, his virtue, died undeservedly. The people bore his bitter fate unworthily and followed his funeral with great weeping.
EDCS-17400002.summary: An epitaph for Caius Turpidius Severus, who died at 16, lamenting his unfulfilled potential, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-17500003.translation: Of Aulus Faesonius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-17500003.summary: This inscription likely refers to the ownership or ancestry of Aulus Faesonius, son of Aulus.

EDCS-17500012.summary: This inscription likely refers to the ownership or ancestry of Marcus Annius Modestus.

EDCS-17500016.summary: This inscription likely refers to the ownership or ancestry of Titus Silius Petrus Vari.

EDCS-17500019.translation: Caius Lucentius, may you live in Christ.
EDCS-17500019.summary: This is a Christian inscription wishing Caius Lucentius a blessed afterlife in Christ.

EDCS-17500043.summary: This inscription likely refers to the ownership or ancestry of Hortesia Alcis.

EDCS-17500051.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Appius Paullinus, likely a high-ranking individual.

EDCS-17500305.summary: This inscription names Sextus Avellius Felix, possibly as the subject of a dedication or a tomb inscription.

EDCS-17500310.summary: This inscription names Mesenus Menupilus, possibly as the subject of a dedication or a tomb inscription.

EDCS-17500350.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Albius Secundus, likely a benefactor or local dignitary.

EDCS-17500351.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Manlius Cominius Cypriacus, who was likely a prominent figure in the community.

EDCS-17500352.summary: This inscription refers to the Epidii family, sons of Marcus, likely for a property boundary or familial dedication.

EDCS-17500372.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly an ownership mark or a dedication by Caius Iulius Castinus, date uncertain.

EDCS-17500379.translation: Of the Lucii, sons of Rufus
EDCS-17500379.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a tomb inscription.

EDCS-17500380.translation: Of Quintus Verus, son of Arte
EDCS-17500380.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a tomb inscription.

EDCS-17500381.translation: The pottery works of Gnaeus Domitius Asiaticus, from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, daughter of Publius
